## File: dev/active/independent-project-setup.md
````markdown
  1: # Independent Project Setup Guide
  2: 
  3: > **Purpose**: Configure User Secrets to run Explore.API and Explore.Blazor independently without Aspire orchestration.
  4: >
  5: > **Date**: January 2026
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## Executive Summary
 10: 
 11: This guide decouples local development from Aspire + Infisical orchestration by using .NET User Secrets for local configuration. After setup, you can:
 12: 
 13: - Run `Explore.API` standalone with `dotnet run`
 14: - Run `Explore.Blazor` standalone with `dotnet run`
 15: - Generate API clients without starting the full Aspire stack
 16: - Keep Infisical for orchestration (AppHost) and production deployments only
 17: 
 18: ---
 19: 
 20: ## Architecture Change
 21: 
 22: ```
 23: BEFORE (Tightly Coupled):
 24: +----------------------------------------------------------+
 25: |                    Aspire AppHost                         |
 26: |  +----------+   +----------+   +----------------------+   |
 27: |  | Infisical|--->|  Secrets |--->| API / Blazor / etc |   |
 28: |  +----------+   +----------+   +----------------------+   |
 29: +----------------------------------------------------------+
 30:      Must run AppHost to run ANY service
 31: 
 32: AFTER (Decoupled):
 33: +----------------------------------------------------------+
 34: | Local Development (User Secrets)                          |
 35: |  +----------+        +----------+                         |
 36: |  |   API    |<------>|PostgreSQL|  (direct connection)    |
 37: |  +----------+        +----------+                         |
 38: |  +----------+        +----------+                         |
 39: |  |  Blazor  |<------>|   API    |  (direct connection)    |
 40: |  +----------+        +----------+                         |
 41: +----------------------------------------------------------+
 42:      Each service runs independently
 43: 
 44: +----------------------------------------------------------+
 45: | Integration / Production (Keep Infisical)                 |
 46: |  +----------+   +----------+   +----------------------+   |
 47: |  | Infisical|--->| AppHost  |--->| Full Stack Testing |   |
 48: |  +----------+   +----------+   +----------------------+   |
 49: +----------------------------------------------------------+
 50: ```
 51: 
 52: ---
 53: 
 54: ## Prerequisites
 55: 
 56: 1. **PostgreSQL Database** running locally or accessible remotely
 57: 2. **Keycloak Instance** (use existing `keycloak.openislamu.org` for dev)
 58: 3. **.NET 10 SDK** installed
 59: 4. **Existing Infisical secrets** (to copy values from)
 60: 
 61: ---
 62: 
 63: ## Step 1: Get Current Secret Values from Infisical
 64: 
 65: Before setting up User Secrets, retrieve current values from Infisical. You can either:
 66: 
 67: **Option A: From Infisical Web UI**
 68: 1. Go to `https://infisical.openislamu.org`
 69: 2. Navigate to your project -> `dev` environment
 70: 3. Copy values from paths: `/keycloak`, `/api`, `/blazor`, `/postgresql`
 71: 
 72: **Option B: From Infisical CLI**
 73: ```powershell
 74: # Install Infisical CLI if not installed
 75: # https://infisical.com/docs/cli/overview
 76: 
 77: # Login
 78: infisical login
 79: 
 80: # Export all secrets (replace with your project ID)
 81: infisical export --projectId=YOUR_PROJECT_ID --env=dev --format=dotenv > secrets.env
 82: 
 83: # View specific paths
 84: infisical secrets --projectId=YOUR_PROJECT_ID --env=dev --path=/postgresql
 85: infisical secrets --projectId=YOUR_PROJECT_ID --env=dev --path=/keycloak
 86: infisical secrets --projectId=YOUR_PROJECT_ID --env=dev --path=/api
 87: infisical secrets --projectId=YOUR_PROJECT_ID --env=dev --path=/blazor
 88: ```
 89: 
 90: ---
 91: 
 92: ## Step 2: Configure Explore.API User Secrets
 93: 
 94: ### Initialize User Secrets (if not already)
 95: 
 96: ```powershell
 97: cd Explore.API
 98: dotnet user-secrets init  # Skip if already initialized (UserSecretsId exists in .csproj)
 99: ```
100: 
101: ### Set Required Secrets
102: 
103: ```powershell
104: cd Explore.API
105: 
106: # ============================================
107: # DATABASE (REQUIRED)
108: # ============================================
109: # Replace with your actual PostgreSQL connection string
110: dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection" "Server=localhost;Port=5432;Database=explore_dev;User Id=postgres;Password=YOUR_PASSWORD;Include Error Detail=true"
111: 
112: # ============================================
113: # KEYCLOAK AUTHENTICATION (REQUIRED)
114: # ============================================
115: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:Realm" "islamu-dev"
116: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:Authority" "https://keycloak.openislamu.org/realms/islamu-dev"
117: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:MetadataAddress" "https://keycloak.openislamu.org/realms/islamu-dev/.well-known/openid-configuration"
118: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AuthorizationUrl" "https://keycloak.openislamu.org/realms/islamu-dev/protocol/openid-connect/auth"
119: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:RequireHttpsMetadata" "true"
120: 
121: # ============================================
122: # S3 OBJECT STORAGE (OPTIONAL - for file uploads)
123: # ============================================
124: # Skip these if you don't need file upload functionality during development
125: dotnet user-secrets set "S3Settings:Region" "YOUR_REGION"
126: dotnet user-secrets set "S3Settings:BucketName" "YOUR_BUCKET_NAME"
127: dotnet user-secrets set "S3Settings:AccessKeyId" "YOUR_ACCESS_KEY"
128: dotnet user-secrets set "S3Settings:SecretAccessKey" "YOUR_SECRET_KEY"
129: dotnet user-secrets set "S3Settings:Endpoint" "YOUR_S3_ENDPOINT"
130: dotnet user-secrets set "S3Settings:PublicEndpoint" "YOUR_S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT"
131: 
132: # ============================================
133: # EMAIL (OPTIONAL - for email notifications)
134: # ============================================
135: # Skip if not testing email functionality
136: dotnet user-secrets set "EmailSettings:ApiKey" "YOUR_EMAIL_API_KEY"
137: dotnet user-secrets set "EmailSettings:FromAddress" "contact@openislamu.org"
138: dotnet user-secrets set "EmailSettings:FromName" "Explore Dev"
139: 
140: # ============================================
141: # DEPLOYMENT MODE (OPTIONAL)
142: # ============================================
143: # Default is MultiTenant - set to SingleTenant for simpler local dev
144: dotnet user-secrets set "Deployment:Mode" "SingleTenant"
145: dotnet user-secrets set "Deployment:DefaultTenantId" "018e4e5c-7f00-7000-8000-000000000001"
146: ```
147: 
148: ### Verify Secrets Were Set
149: 
150: ```powershell
151: cd Explore.API
152: dotnet user-secrets list
153: ```
154: 
155: Expected output:
156: ```
157: ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection = Server=localhost;Port=5432;...
158: Keycloak:Authority = https://keycloak.openislamu.org/realms/islamu-dev
159: Keycloak:AuthorizationUrl = https://keycloak.openislamu.org/realms/islamu-dev/protocol/openid-connect/auth
160: Keycloak:MetadataAddress = https://keycloak.openislamu.org/realms/islamu-dev/.well-known/openid-configuration
161: Keycloak:Realm = islamu-dev
162: Keycloak:RequireHttpsMetadata = true
163: ...
164: ```
165: 
166: ---
167: 
168: ## Step 3: Configure Explore.Blazor User Secrets
169: 
170: ### Initialize User Secrets (if not already)
171: 
172: ```powershell
173: cd Explore.Blazor
174: dotnet user-secrets init  # Skip if already initialized
175: ```
176: 
177: ### Set Required Secrets
178: 
179: ```powershell
180: cd Explore.Blazor
181: 
182: # ============================================
183: # KEYCLOAK AUTHENTICATION (REQUIRED)
184: # ============================================
185: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:Authority" "https://keycloak.openislamu.org/realms/islamu-dev"
186: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:ClientId" "explore-blazor-server"
187: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:ClientSecret" "YOUR_BLAZOR_CLIENT_SECRET"
188: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:RequireHttpsMetadata" "true"
189: 
190: # ============================================
191: # API BASE URL (REQUIRED)
192: # ============================================
193: # Points to locally running API
194: dotnet user-secrets set "ExploreApi:BaseUrl" "https://localhost:7039/"
195: 
196: # ============================================
197: # MULTI-TENANCY (OPTIONAL)
198: # ============================================
199: dotnet user-secrets set "Explore:MultiTenancy:DefaultTenantId" "018e4e5c-7f00-7000-8000-000000000001"
200: ```
201: 
202: ### Verify Secrets Were Set
203: 
204: ```powershell
205: cd Explore.Blazor
206: dotnet user-secrets list
207: ```
208: 
209: ---
210: 
211: ## Step 4: Configure Event.MigrationService User Secrets (Optional)
212: 
213: Only needed if you want to run migrations independently.
214: 
215: ```powershell
216: cd Event.MigrationService
217: 
218: # DATABASE (REQUIRED)
219: dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:EventMigrationService" "Server=localhost;Port=5432;Database=explore_dev;User Id=postgres;Password=YOUR_PASSWORD;Include Error Detail=true"
220: ```
221: 
222: ---
223: 
224: ## Step 5: Test Independent Execution
225: 
226: ### Run API Independently
227: 
228: ```powershell
229: cd Explore.API
230: dotnet run
231: ```
232: 
233: Expected output:
234: ```
235: info: Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime[14]
236:       Now listening on: https://localhost:7039
237: info: Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime[14]
238:       Now listening on: http://localhost:5035
239: info: Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime[0]
240:       Application started. Press Ctrl+C to shut down.
241: ```
242: 
243: **Verify API is working:**
244: ```powershell
245: # Health check
246: curl https://localhost:7039/health
247: 
248: # Swagger UI
249: # Open browser: https://localhost:7039/scalar/v1
250: ```
251: 
252: ### Run Blazor Independently
253: 
254: ```powershell
255: # First, ensure API is running (in another terminal)
256: cd Explore.API
257: dotnet run
258: 
259: # Then run Blazor
260: cd Explore.Blazor
261: dotnet run
262: ```
263: 
264: Expected output:
265: ```
266: info: Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime[14]
267:       Now listening on: https://localhost:7177
268: info: Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime[14]
269:       Now listening on: http://localhost:5144
270: ```
271: 
272: **Verify Blazor is working:**
273: ```powershell
274: # Open browser: https://localhost:7177
275: ```
276: 
277: ---
278: 
279: ## Step 6: Create API Client Generation Script
280: 
281: Create a PowerShell script to regenerate the API client without Aspire:
282: 
283: ### Create Script File
284: 
285: ```powershell
286: # Create scripts directory if it doesn't exist
287: New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path scripts
288: ```
289: 
290: Create `scripts/update-api-client.ps1`:
291: 
292: ```powershell
293: #!/usr/bin/env pwsh
294: <#
295: .SYNOPSIS
296:     Regenerates the Blazor API client from the running API's OpenAPI schema.
297:     
298: .DESCRIPTION
299:     This script:
300:     1. Starts Explore.API temporarily
301:     2. Waits for it to be healthy
302:     3. Downloads the OpenAPI schema (swagger.json)
303:     4. Regenerates the API client using NSwag
304:     5. Stops the API
305:     
306: .EXAMPLE
307:     ./scripts/update-api-client.ps1
308: #>
309: 
310: $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
311: 
312: # Configuration
313: $ApiProjectPath = "Explore.API"
314: $ApiUrl = "https://localhost:7039"
315: $SwaggerUrl = "$ApiUrl/swagger/v1/swagger.json"
316: $OutputSwaggerPath = "Explore.API/swagger.json"
317: $ClientOutputPath = "Explore.Blazor.Client/Clients/EventApiClient.g.cs"
318: $MaxWaitSeconds = 60
319: $PollIntervalSeconds = 2
320: 
321: Write-Host "========================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
322: Write-Host "  API Client Generation Script" -ForegroundColor Cyan
323: Write-Host "========================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
324: Write-Host ""
325: 
326: # Check if API is already running
327: Write-Host "[1/6] Checking if API is already running..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
328: $apiAlreadyRunning = $false
329: try {
330:     $response = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "$ApiUrl/health" -TimeoutSec 5 -SkipCertificateCheck -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
331:     if ($response.StatusCode -eq 200) {
332:         $apiAlreadyRunning = $true
333:         Write-Host "  API is already running" -ForegroundColor Green
334:     }
335: } catch {
336:     Write-Host "  -> API is not running, will start it" -ForegroundColor Gray
337: }
338: 
339: $apiProcess = $null
340: 
341: if (-not $apiAlreadyRunning) {
342:     # Start the API
343:     Write-Host "[2/6] Starting Explore.API..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
344:     Push-Location $ApiProjectPath
345:     try {
346:         $apiProcess = Start-Process -FilePath "dotnet" -ArgumentList "run", "--no-build" -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden
347:         Write-Host "  API process started (PID: $($apiProcess.Id))" -ForegroundColor Green
348:     } finally {
349:         Pop-Location
350:     }
351: 
352:     # Wait for API to be healthy
353:     Write-Host "[3/6] Waiting for API to be healthy..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
354:     $elapsed = 0
355:     $healthy = $false
356:     
357:     while ($elapsed -lt $MaxWaitSeconds) {
358:         try {
359:             $response = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "$ApiUrl/health" -TimeoutSec 5 -SkipCertificateCheck -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
360:             if ($response.StatusCode -eq 200) {
361:                 $healthy = $true
362:                 break
363:             }
364:         } catch {
365:             # Ignore errors, keep polling
366:         }
367:         
368:         Start-Sleep -Seconds $PollIntervalSeconds
369:         $elapsed += $PollIntervalSeconds
370:         Write-Host "  -> Waiting... ($elapsed/$MaxWaitSeconds seconds)" -ForegroundColor Gray
371:     }
372: 
373:     if (-not $healthy) {
374:         Write-Host "  API failed to become healthy within $MaxWaitSeconds seconds" -ForegroundColor Red
375:         if ($apiProcess -and -not $apiProcess.HasExited) {
376:             Stop-Process -Id $apiProcess.Id -Force
377:         }
378:         exit 1
379:     }
380:     
381:     Write-Host "  API is healthy" -ForegroundColor Green
382: } else {
383:     Write-Host "[2/6] Skipping API start (already running)" -ForegroundColor Gray
384:     Write-Host "[3/6] Skipping health check (already running)" -ForegroundColor Gray
385: }
386: 
387: # Download swagger.json
388: Write-Host "[4/6] Downloading OpenAPI schema..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
389: try {
390:     Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $SwaggerUrl -OutFile $OutputSwaggerPath -SkipCertificateCheck
391:     Write-Host "  Downloaded to $OutputSwaggerPath" -ForegroundColor Green
392: } catch {
393:     Write-Host "  Failed to download swagger.json: $_" -ForegroundColor Red
394:     if ($apiProcess -and -not $apiProcess.HasExited) {
395:         Stop-Process -Id $apiProcess.Id -Force
396:     }
397:     exit 1
398: }
399: 
400: # Generate API client
401: Write-Host "[5/6] Generating API client..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
402: 
403: # Check if NSwag is available
404: $nswagPath = Get-Command "nswag" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
405: if (-not $nswagPath) {
406:     Write-Host "  -> NSwag CLI not found, attempting to use dotnet tool..." -ForegroundColor Gray
407:     
408:     # Try dotnet tool
409:     $result = dotnet tool list -g | Select-String "nswag"
410:     if (-not $result) {
411:         Write-Host "  -> Installing NSwag as global tool..." -ForegroundColor Gray
412:         dotnet tool install -g NSwag.ConsoleCore
413:     }
414:     
415:     $nswagCommand = "nswag"
416: } else {
417:     $nswagCommand = $nswagPath.Source
418: }
419: 
420: # Check for nswag.json configuration
421: if (Test-Path "nswag.json") {
422:     Write-Host "  -> Using nswag.json configuration" -ForegroundColor Gray
423:     & $nswagCommand run nswag.json
424: } else {
425:     Write-Host "  -> Generating with inline parameters" -ForegroundColor Gray
426:     & $nswagCommand openapi2csclient `
427:         /input:$OutputSwaggerPath `
428:         /output:$ClientOutputPath `
429:         /namespace:Explore.Blazor.Client.Clients `
430:         /className:EventApiClient `
431:         /generateClientInterfaces:true `
432:         /generateExceptionClasses:true `
433:         /exceptionClass:ApiException `
434:         /useBaseUrl:false `
435:         /injectHttpClient:true
436: }
437: 
438: if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
439:     Write-Host "  Client generated at $ClientOutputPath" -ForegroundColor Green
440: } else {
441:     Write-Host "  Client generation failed" -ForegroundColor Red
442: }
443: 
444: # Stop the API (only if we started it)
445: Write-Host "[6/6] Cleaning up..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
446: if ($apiProcess -and -not $apiProcess.HasExited) {
447:     Stop-Process -Id $apiProcess.Id -Force
448:     Write-Host "  API process stopped" -ForegroundColor Green
449: } else {
450:     Write-Host "  -> API was already running, leaving it running" -ForegroundColor Gray
451: }
452: 
453: Write-Host ""
454: Write-Host "========================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
455: Write-Host "  Done! API client has been regenerated" -ForegroundColor Cyan
456: Write-Host "========================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
457: Write-Host ""
458: Write-Host "Next steps:" -ForegroundColor White
459: Write-Host "  1. Check for compile errors in Explore.Blazor.Client" -ForegroundColor Gray
460: Write-Host "  2. Update Blazor components to match new API contract" -ForegroundColor Gray
461: Write-Host "  3. Run full integration test with Aspire when ready" -ForegroundColor Gray
462: ```
463: 
464: ### Make Script Executable
465: 
466: ```powershell
467: # On Windows, PowerShell scripts are executable by default
468: # On Linux/Mac with PowerShell Core:
469: chmod +x scripts/update-api-client.ps1
470: ```
471: 
472: ---
473: 
474: ## Step 7: New Development Workflow
475: 
476: ### Scenario: Making Breaking API Changes
477: 
478: 1. **Make API changes** in `Explore.API`
479:    - Modify controllers, DTOs, etc.
480: 
481: 2. **Build API to ensure it compiles**
482:    ```powershell
483:    cd Explore.API
484:    dotnet build
485:    ```
486: 
487: 3. **Run the client generation script**
488:    ```powershell
489:    ./scripts/update-api-client.ps1
490:    ```
491: 
492: 4. **Fix compile errors** in `Explore.Blazor.Client`
493:    - IDE shows immediate feedback
494:    - Update components to match new API contract
495: 
496: 5. **Test individually**
497:    ```powershell
498:    # Terminal 1: Run API
499:    cd Explore.API && dotnet run
500:    
501:    # Terminal 2: Run Blazor
502:    cd Explore.Blazor && dotnet run
503:    ```
504: 
505: 6. **Integration test** (when ready)
506:    ```powershell
507:    # Run full stack with Aspire
508:    cd Explore.AppHost && dotnet run
509:    ```
510: 
511: ---
512: 
513: ## Troubleshooting
514: 
515: ### "Connection string not found"
516: 
517: ```
518: System.InvalidOperationException: 'ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection' is null
519: ```
520: 
521: **Fix:** Ensure you set the connection string in user-secrets:
522: ```powershell
523: cd Explore.API
524: dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection" "YOUR_CONNECTION_STRING"
525: ```
526: 
527: ### "Keycloak authentication failed"
528: 
529: ```
530: System.Exception: Unable to retrieve document from: https://keycloak.../well-known/openid-configuration
531: ```
532: 
533: **Fix:** 
534: 1. Verify Keycloak is accessible: `curl https://keycloak.openislamu.org/realms/islamu-dev/.well-known/openid-configuration`
535: 2. Check your secrets are correctly set:
536:    ```powershell
537:    cd Explore.API
538:    dotnet user-secrets list | Select-String "Keycloak"
539:    ```
540: 
541: ### "Certificate error" when running locally
542: 
543: ```
544: The SSL connection could not be established
545: ```
546: 
547: **Fix:** Trust the development certificate:
548: ```powershell
549: dotnet dev-certs https --trust
550: ```
551: 
552: ### "Port already in use"
553: 
554: ```
555: System.IO.IOException: Failed to bind to address https://127.0.0.1:7039
556: ```
557: 
558: **Fix:** Kill existing process or use different port:
559: ```powershell
560: # Find process using port
561: netstat -ano | findstr :7039
562: 
563: # Kill it
564: taskkill /PID <PID> /F
565: 
566: # Or change port in launchSettings.json
567: ```
568: 
569: ### "User secrets not being read"
570: 
571: **Fix:** Ensure you're running in Development environment:
572: ```powershell
573: $env:ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT = "Development"
574: dotnet run
575: ```
576: 
577: ---
578: 
579: ## Secret Locations Reference
580: 
581: User secrets are stored at:
582: - **Windows:** `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\UserSecrets\<UserSecretsId>\secrets.json`
583: - **Linux/Mac:** `~/.microsoft/usersecrets/<UserSecretsId>/secrets.json`
584: 
585: | Project | UserSecretsId |
586: |---------|---------------|
587: | Explore.API | `e88f0772-e883-4ace-8ffe-13303d1355eb` |
588: | Explore.Blazor | `5e896b2d-4efd-42cc-8b6f-f6cc3c5e4c7a` |
589: | Event.MigrationService | `dotnet-Event.MigrationService-3ef3345d-919b-42f0-8c02-2e81a55d3240` |
590: | Explore.AppHost | `cf2496b7-15ad-4167-8905-1b67f7d20442` |
591: 
592: ---
593: 
594: ## Summary: What Changed
595: 
596: | Component | Before | After |
597: |-----------|--------|-------|
598: | **Explore.API** | Requires AppHost + Infisical | Runs standalone with User Secrets |
599: | **Explore.Blazor** | Requires AppHost + Infisical | Runs standalone with User Secrets |
600: | **AppHost** | Required for any development | Only needed for integration testing |
601: | **Infisical** | Required for local dev | Only for AppHost/Docker/Production |
602: | **Client Generation** | Manual, painful process | Automated script |
603: 
604: ---
605: 
606: ## Quick Reference Commands
607: 
608: ```powershell
609: # Run API independently
610: cd Explore.API && dotnet run
611: 
612: # Run Blazor independently (API must be running)
613: cd Explore.Blazor && dotnet run
614: 
615: # Regenerate API client
616: ./scripts/update-api-client.ps1
617: 
618: # List all secrets for a project
619: cd Explore.API && dotnet user-secrets list
620: 
621: # Clear all secrets for a project
622: cd Explore.API && dotnet user-secrets clear
623: 
624: # Run with Aspire (full integration)
625: cd Explore.AppHost && dotnet run
626: ```
627: 
628: ---
629: 
630: **Remember:** User Secrets are for local development only. Production and staging environments should continue using Infisical through AppHost or Docker.
````

## File: dev/active/infisical-report.md
````markdown
 1: # Infisical Optionality Plan (Docker Compose + Image Deployments)
 2: 
 3: ## Executive Summary
 4: You want two deployment modes that share the same images and configuration model:
 5: 1) Docker Compose for self-hosters (no Infisical required, but optional).
 6: 2) Image-only deployments for your hosted instance or advanced users (Infisical required or optional).
 7: 
 8: The key is to make Infisical an **optional configuration provider** that can be enabled by env vars at runtime without changing code paths for non-Infisical deployments.
 9: 
10: ## Current Constraints (from codebase)
11: - API and Blazor use configuration extension classes to map external env vars into .NET config.
12: - Docker Compose relies on direct environment variables.
13: - EntryPoint scripts use Infisical CLI for injected secrets in non-compose deployments.
14: 
15: ## Goals
16: - Keep Docker Compose usable without Infisical.
17: - Allow Infisical as an opt-in feature for Compose users.
18: - Allow image-only deployments to pull secrets from Infisical, but still work with direct env vars.
19: - Preserve security best practices (least privilege, scoped secrets).
20: 
21: ## Recommended Design (No Code Change Yet)
22: 
23: ### 1) Infisical as an optional “overlay”
24: Behavior priority for both API and Blazor:
25: 1. Environment variables (explicit overrides)
26: 2. Infisical CLI injected values (if enabled)
27: 3. Appsettings defaults (fallback)
28: 
29: This keeps Docker Compose working without Infisical, while allowing an Infisical overlay.
30: 
31: ### 2) Runtime toggle via env vars
32: Standardize a minimal set of env flags:
33: - `INFISICAL_ENABLED=true|false`
34: - `INFISICAL_HOST` (for self-hosted Infisical)
35: - `INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID`
36: - `INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID`
37: - `INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET`
38: - `INFISICAL_ENV=dev|staging|prod`
39: 
40: If `INFISICAL_ENABLED=false` or unset, entrypoint should skip Infisical entirely.
41: 
42: ### 3) Docker Compose Profiles
43: Expose two profiles:
44: - `default` (no Infisical, direct env vars)
45: - `infisical` (adds Infisical sidecar or enables Infisical in entrypoint)
46: 
47: This lets users opt-in without editing the file.
48: 
49: ### 4) S3 + Keycloak split for internal vs public
50: Continue separating internal vs public endpoints:
51: - Internal endpoints for service-to-service
52: - Public endpoints for browser-facing redirects and presigned URLs
53: 
54: This supports both local HTTP and VPS HTTPS.
55: 
56: ## Suggested Compose UX (No Code Change Yet)
57: 
58: ### Local (no Infisical)
59: Set direct env vars in compose and use default profile.
60: 
61: ### Local + Infisical (optional)
62: Add `--profile infisical` and provide Infisical env vars.
63: EntryPoints use those to inject secrets at startup.
64: 
65: ### VPS / Hosted Instance
66: Deploy each service separately; enable Infisical via env vars.
67: Use reverse proxy for public URLs; internal URLs stay on private network.
68: 
69: ## Security Notes
70: - Infisical improves governance by centralizing secrets, not by itself “more secure.”
71: - It becomes more secure **when access is scoped** (per service or per environment).
72: - For teams: Infisical reduces secret sprawl in CI/CD and Docker Compose files.
73: 
74: ## Recommendation Summary
75: - Offer Infisical as **optional** everywhere.
76: - Keep env var overrides as the highest priority.
77: - Add a compose profile to toggle Infisical cleanly.
78: - Document separate internal/public endpoint variables for Keycloak and S3.
79: 
80: ## Next Steps (If You Want Implementation)
81: 1) Add `INFISICAL_ENABLED` logic to entrypoint scripts.
82: 2) Provide a Compose profile that injects Infisical envs.
83: 3) Update docs for three deployment paths: local compose, compose+infisical, image-only.
84: 4) Add examples for Keycloak/S3 internal vs public endpoint variables.
````

 1: Role

 3: 
 4:   Objective
 5:   Re-architect observability for my .NET solution using the PLG stack
 6:   (Prometheus, Loki, Grafana) with Serilog + OpenTelemetry, supporting
 7:   dual-mode deployment:
 8:   - Local Dev: .NET Aspire AppHost orchestrates containers
 9:   - Production: fully decoupled Docker containers (no AppHost, no Compose)
10: 
11:   Context (Source Files)
12:   Pay special attention to:
13:   - Explore.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs (current OTel setup)
14:   - Explore.ServiceDefaults/Explore.ServiceDefaults.csproj (current
15:   packages)
16:   - Explore.API and Explore.Blazor startup code (logging/hosting patterns)
17:   - Explore.AppHost (if present) for dev orchestration patterns
18: 
19:   Non‑Negotiable Requirements
20:   1) Logging (Serilog + OTel + Loki)
21:   - Use Serilog for structured JSON logging with enrichers.
22:   - Do NOT use Serilog.Sinks.Loki.

26:   2) Metrics (Prometheus)

## File: dev/active/README.md
````markdown
  1: # Dev Docs Pattern
  2: 
  3: A methodology for maintaining project context across Claude Code sessions and context resets.
  4: 
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: ## The Problem
  8: 
  9: **Context resets lose everything:**
 10: - Implementation decisions
 11: - Key files and their purposes
 12: - Task progress
 13: - Technical constraints
 14: - Why certain approaches were chosen
 15: 
 16: **After a reset, Claude has to rediscover everything.**
 17: 
 18: ---
 19: 
 20: ## The Solution: Persistent Dev Docs
 21: 
 22: A three-file structure that captures everything needed to resume work:
 23: 
 24: ```
 25: dev/active/[task-name]/
 26: ├── [task-name]-plan.md      # Strategic plan
 27: ├── [task-name]-context.md   # Key decisions & files
 28: └── [task-name]-tasks.md     # Checklist format
 29: ```
 30: 
 31: **These files survive context resets** - Claude reads them to get back up to speed instantly.
 32: 
 33: ---
 34: 
 35: ## Three-File Structure
 36: 
 37: ### 1. [task-name]-plan.md
 38: 
 39: **Purpose:** Strategic plan for the implementation
 40: 
 41: **Contains:**
 42: - Executive summary
 43: - Current state analysis
 44: - Proposed future state
 45: - Implementation phases
 46: - Detailed tasks with acceptance criteria
 47: - Risk assessment
 48: - Success metrics
 49: - Timeline estimates
 50: 
 51: **When to create:** At the start of a complex task
 52: 
 53: **When to update:** When scope changes or new phases discovered
 54: 
 55: **Example:**
 56: ```markdown
 57: # Feature Name - Implementation Plan
 58: 
 59: ## Executive Summary
 60: What we're building and why
 61: 
 62: ## Current State
 63: Where we are now
 64: 
 65: ## Implementation Phases
 66: 
 67: ### Phase 1: Infrastructure (2 hours)
 68: - Task 1.1: Set up database schema
 69:   - Acceptance: Schema compiles, relationships correct
 70: - Task 1.2: Create service structure
 71:   - Acceptance: All directories created
 72: 
 73: ### Phase 2: Core Functionality (3 hours)
 74: ...
 75: ```
 76: 
 77: ---
 78: 
 79: ### 2. [task-name]-context.md
 80: 
 81: **Purpose:** Key information for resuming work
 82: 
 83: **Contains:**
 84: - SESSION PROGRESS section (updated frequently!)
 85: - What's completed vs in-progress
 86: - Key files and their purposes
 87: - Important decisions made
 88: - Technical constraints discovered
 89: - Links to related files
 90: - Quick resume instructions
 91: 
 92: **When to create:** Start of task
 93: 
 94: **When to update:** **FREQUENTLY** - after major decisions, completions, or discoveries
 95: 
 96: **Example:**
 97: ```markdown
 98: # Feature Name - Context
 99: 
100: ## SESSION PROGRESS (2025-10-29)
101: 
102: ### ✅ COMPLETED
103: - Refactoring StatusType related classes (renamed StatusType to ApprovalStatus in all api layers of clean architecture)
104: 
105: ### 🟡 IN PROGRESS
106: - Creating example
107: - File: example/example.cs
108: 
109: ### ⚠️ BLOCKERS
110: - Need to decide on example
111: 
112: ## Key Files
113: 
114: **example/Controllers/ExampleController.cs**
115: - Extends example
116: - Handles HTTP requests for posts
117: - Delegates to example
118: 
119: **example/Controllers/Example2Controller.cs** (IN PROGRESS)
120: - Business logic for post operations
121: - Next: Add caching
122: 
123: ## Quick Resume
124: To continue:
125: 1. Read this file
126: 2. Continue implementing example
127: 3. See tasks file for remaining work
128: ```
129: 
130: **CRITICAL:** Update the SESSION PROGRESS section every time significant work is done!
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### 3. [task-name]-tasks.md
135: 
136: **Purpose:** Checklist for tracking progress
137: 
138: **Contains:**
139: - Phases broken down by logical sections
140: - Tasks in checkbox format
141: - Status indicators (✅/🟡/⏳)
142: - Acceptance criteria
143: - Quick resume section
144: 
145: **When to create:** Start of task
146: 
147: **When to update:** After completing each task or discovering new tasks
148: 
149: **Example:**
150: ```markdown
151: # Feature Name - Task Checklist
152: 
153: ## Phase 1: Setup ✅ COMPLETE
154: - [x] Create example
155: - [x] Set up controllers
156: - [x] Configure example
157: 
158: ## Phase 2: Implementation 🟡 IN PROGRESS
159: - [x] Create ExampleController
160: - [ ] Create Example2Controller (IN PROGRESS)
161: - [ ] Create ExampleRepository
162: - [ ] Add validation
163: 
164: ## Phase 3: Testing ⏳ NOT STARTED
165: - [ ] Unit tests for service
166: - [ ] Integration tests
167: - [ ] Manual API testing
168: ```
169: 
170: ---
171: 
172: ## When to Use Dev Docs
173: 
174: **Use for:**
175: - ✅ Complex multi-day tasks
176: - ✅ Features with many moving parts
177: - ✅ Tasks likely to span multiple sessions
178: - ✅ Work that needs careful planning
179: - ✅ Refactoring large systems
180: 
181: **Skip for:**
182: - ❌ Simple bug fixes
183: - ❌ Single-file changes
184: - ❌ Quick updates
185: - ❌ Trivial modifications
186: 
187: **Rule of thumb:** If it takes more than 2 hours or spans multiple sessions, use dev docs.
188: 
189: ---
190: 
191: ## Workflow with Dev Docs
192: 
193: ### Starting a New Task
194: 
195: 1. **Use /dev-docs slash command:**
196:    ```
197:    /dev-docs refactor authentication system
198:    ```
199: 
200: 2. **Claude creates the three files:**
201:    - Analyzes requirements
202:    - Examines codebase
203:    - Creates comprehensive plan
204:    - Generates context and tasks files
205: 
206: 3. **Review and adjust:**
207:    - Check if plan makes sense
208:    - Add any missing considerations
209:    - Adjust timeline estimates
210: 
211: ### During Implementation
212: 
213: 1. **Refer to plan** for overall strategy
214: 2. **Update context.md** frequently:
215:    - Mark completed work
216:    - Note decisions made
217:    - Add blockers
218: 3. **Check off tasks** in tasks.md as you complete them
219: 
220: ### After Context Reset
221: 
222: 1. **Claude reads all three files**
223: 2. **Understands complete state** in seconds
224: 3. **Resumes exactly where you left off**
225: 
226: No need to explain what you were doing - it's all documented!
227: 
228: ---
229: 
230: ## Integration with Slash Commands
231: 
232: ### /dev-docs
233: **Creates:** New dev docs for a task
234: 
235: **Usage:**
236: ```
237: /dev-docs implement real-time notifications
238: ```
239: 
240: **Generates:**
241: - `dev/active/implement-real-time-notifications/`
242:   - implement-real-time-notifications-plan.md
243:   - implement-real-time-notifications-context.md
244:   - implement-real-time-notifications-tasks.md
245: 
246: ### /dev-docs-update
247: **Updates:** Existing dev docs before context reset
248: 
249: **Usage:**
250: ```
251: /dev-docs-update
252: ```
253: 
254: **Updates:**
255: - Marks completed tasks
256: - Adds new tasks discovered
257: - Updates context with session progress
258: - Captures current state
259: 
260: **Use when:** Approaching context limits or ending session
261: 
262: ---
263: 
264: ## File Organization
265: 
266: ```
267: dev/
268: ├── README.md              # This file
269: ├── active/                # Current work
270: │   ├── task-1/
271: │   │   ├── task-1-plan.md
272: │   │   ├── task-1-context.md
273: │   │   └── task-1-tasks.md
274: │   └── task-2/
275: │       └── ...
276: └── archive/               # Completed work (optional)
277:     └── old-task/
278:         └── ...
279: ```
280: 
281: **active/**: Work in progress
282: **archive/**: Completed tasks (for reference)
283: 
284: ---
285: 
286: ## Example: Real Usage
287: 
288: See **dev/active/public-infrastructure-repo/** in this repository for a real example:
289: - **plan.md** - 700+ line strategic plan for creating this showcase
290: - **context.md** - Tracks what's completed, decisions made, what's next
291: - **tasks.md** - Checklist of all phases and tasks
292: 
293: This is the actual dev docs used to build this showcase!
294: 
295: ---
296: 
297: ## Best Practices
298: 
299: ### Update Context Frequently
300: 
301: **Bad:** Update only at end of session
302: **Good:** Update after each major milestone
303: 
304: **SESSION PROGRESS section should always reflect reality:**
305: ```markdown
306: ## SESSION PROGRESS (YYYY-MM-DD)
307: 
308: ### ✅ COMPLETED (list everything done)
309: ### 🟡 IN PROGRESS (what you're working on RIGHT NOW)
310: ### ⚠️ BLOCKERS (what's preventing progress)
311: ```
312: 
313: ### Make Tasks Actionable
314: 
315: **Bad:** "Fix the authentication"
316: **Good:** "Implement JWT token validation in AuthMiddleware.ts (Acceptance: Tokens validated, errors to Sentry)"
317: 
318: **Include:**
319: - Specific file names
320: - Clear acceptance criteria
321: - Dependencies on other tasks
322: 
323: ### Keep Plan Current
324: 
325: If scope changes:
326: - Update the plan
327: - Add new phases
328: - Adjust timeline estimates
329: - Note why scope changed
330: 
331: ---
332: 
333: ## For Claude Code
334: 
335: **When user asks to create dev docs:**
336: 
337: 1. **Use the /dev-docs slash command** if available
338: 2. **Or create manually:**
339:    - Ask about the task scope
340:    - Analyze relevant codebase files
341:    - Create comprehensive plan
342:    - Generate context and tasks
343: 
344: 3. **Structure the plan with:**
345:    - Clear phases
346:    - Actionable tasks
347:    - Acceptance criteria
348:    - Risk assessment
349: 
350: 4. **Make context file resumable:**
351:    - SESSION PROGRESS at top
352:    - Quick resume instructions
353:    - Key files list with explanations
354: 
355: **When resuming from dev docs:**
356: 
357: 1. **Read all three files** (plan, context, tasks)
358: 2. **Start with context.md** - has current state
359: 3. **Check tasks.md** - see what's done and what's next
360: 4. **Refer to plan.md** - understand overall strategy
361: 
362: **Update frequently:**
363: - Mark tasks complete immediately
364: - Update SESSION PROGRESS after significant work
365: - Add new tasks as discovered
366: 
367: ---
368: 
369: ## Creating Dev Docs Manually
370: 
371: If you don't have the /dev-docs command:
372: 
373: **1. Create directory:**
374: ```bash
375: mkdir -p dev/active/your-task-name
376: ```
377: 
378: **2. Create plan.md:**
379: - Executive summary
380: - Implementation phases
381: - Detailed tasks
382: - Timeline estimates
383: 
384: **3. Create context.md:**
385: - SESSION PROGRESS section
386: - Key files
387: - Important decisions
388: - Quick resume instructions
389: 
390: **4. Create tasks.md:**
391: - Phases with checkboxes
392: - [ ] Task format
393: - Acceptance criteria
394: 
395: ---
396: 
397: ## Benefits
398: 
399: **Before dev docs:**
400: - Context reset = start over
401: - Forget why decisions were made
402: - Lose track of progress
403: - Repeat work
404: 
405: **After dev docs:**

````markdown
  1: # Enterprise-Grade API Compliance Report
  2: 
  3: > **ISLAMU Event API - Performance, Security & Best Practices Analysis**
  4: >
  5: > Report Date: January 2026
  6: > .NET Version: .NET 10
  7: > Architecture: Clean Architecture + CQRS with MediatR
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## Executive Summary
 12: 
 13: The ISLAMU Event API demonstrates **solid architectural foundations** with Clean Architecture, CQRS/MediatR patterns, and REST Level 3 (HATEOAS) compliance. However, several enterprise-grade optimizations are missing that would significantly improve performance, security, and operational excellence.
 14: 
 15: ### Overall Grade: **B+** (Good, with room for improvement)
 16: 
 17: | Category | Current | Target | Priority |
 18: |----------|---------|--------|----------|
 19: | Architecture | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | - |
 20: | HATEOAS/REST | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | - |
 21: | Performance | ⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | 🔴 High |
 22: | Security | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | 🟡 Medium |
 23: | Code Consistency | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | 🟢 Low |
 24: | Observability | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | 🟡 Medium |
 25: 
 26: ---
 27: 
 28: ## Current Implementation Strengths ✅
 29: 
 30: ### 1. Clean Architecture Excellence
 31: - **Layer separation**: Domain → Application → Infrastructure → Presentation
 32: - **CQRS pattern**: Commands (write) and Queries (read) properly separated
 33: - **MediatR**: Decoupled request/response handling
 34: - **Repository pattern**: Data access abstraction with generic base
 35: 
 36: ### 2. REST Level 3 (HATEOAS) Compliance
 37: - **HAL+JSON format**: `_links` and `_embedded` structures
 38: - **RFC 7240 support**: `Prefer: return=minimal` header handling
 39: - **Authorization-aware links**: Links filtered by user permissions
 40: - **Entity-specific link policies**: Custom links per entity type
 41: 
 42: ### 3. Multi-Tenancy & Security
 43: - **Global query filters**: Automatic tenant isolation in DbContext
 44: - **Soft delete pattern**: `ISoftDeletable` interface with automatic handling
 45: - **JWT/Keycloak authentication**: BFF pattern with audience validation
 46: - **HSTS enabled**: Strict transport security with preload
 47: 
 48: ### 4. Operational Excellence
 49: - **Graceful shutdown**: 25-second grace period for zero-downtime deployments
 50: - **Health checks**: Kubernetes/container-ready with `/health` endpoints
 51: - **Database migration on startup**: EF Core 9+ concurrent-safe migrations
 52: - **Audit fields**: Automatic `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`, `CreatedBy`, `UpdatedBy`
 53: 
 54: ### 5. API Documentation
 55: - **OpenAPI/Swagger**: Full API documentation
 56: - **Scalar UI**: Modern API reference
 57: - **Endpoint attributes**: `[EndpointSummary]`, `[EndpointDescription]`, `[ProducesResponseType]`
 58: 
 59: ---
 60: 
 61: ## Critical Improvements Required 🔴
 62: 
 63: ### 1. Output Caching Middleware (HIGH PRIORITY)
 64: 
 65: **Current State**: No output caching
 66: **Impact**: Every GET request hits the database even for unchanged data
 67: 
 68: **Recommendation**: Add ASP.NET Core Output Caching for GET endpoints
 69: 
 70: ```csharp
 71: // Program.cs - Add after builder.Services.AddControllers()
 72: builder.Services.AddOutputCache(options =>
 73: {
 74:     options.AddBasePolicy(builder => builder
 75:         .Expire(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30))
 76:         .Tag("api"));
 77: 
 78:     // Cache GET /api/v1/event for 60 seconds
 79:     options.AddPolicy("Events", builder => builder
 80:         .Expire(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60))
 81:         .Tag("events")
 82:         .SetVaryByQuery("page", "pageSize", "search"));
 83: 
 84:     // Cache lookup tables for 5 minutes (rarely change)
 85:     options.AddPolicy("Lookups", builder => builder
 86:         .Expire(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5))
 87:         .Tag("lookups"));
 88: });
 89: 
 90: // In middleware pipeline (after UseRouting, before UseAuthorization)
 91: app.UseOutputCache();
 92: ```
 93: 
 94: **Controller usage**:
 95: ```csharp
 96: [HttpGet]
 97: [AllowAnonymous]
 98: [OutputCache(PolicyName = "Events")]
 99: public async Task<ActionResult<HalResource<PagedListDto<EventListDto>>>> GetAll(...)
100: ```
101: 
102: **Cache invalidation on write**:
103: ```csharp
104: [HttpPost]
105: [Authorize]
106: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> Create(
107:     [FromBody] CreateEventDto dto,
108:     IOutputCacheStore cacheStore)
109: {
110:     var response = await _mediator.Send(new CreateEventCommand { EventDto = dto });
111:     if (response.Success)
112:     {
113:         await cacheStore.EvictByTagAsync("events", default);
114:     }
115:     return response.Success ? Ok(response) : BadRequest(response);
116: }
117: ```
118: 
119: **Benefits**:
120: - 80-90% reduction in database queries for read operations
121: - Microsecond response times for cached responses
122: - Reduced database load
123: 
124: ---
125: 
126: ### 2. Response Compression Middleware (HIGH PRIORITY)
127: 
128: **Current State**: No response compression
129: **Impact**: Larger payloads, higher bandwidth costs, slower responses
130: 
131: **Recommendation**: Add Brotli + Gzip compression
132: 
133: ```csharp
134: // Program.cs
135: builder.Services.AddResponseCompression(options =>
136: {
137:     options.EnableForHttps = true;
138:     options.Providers.Add<BrotliCompressionProvider>();
139:     options.Providers.Add<GzipCompressionProvider>();
140:     options.MimeTypes = ResponseCompressionDefaults.MimeTypes.Concat(new[]
141:     {
142:         "application/json",
143:         "application/hal+json"
144:     });
145: });
146: 
147: builder.Services.Configure<BrotliCompressionProviderOptions>(options =>
148: {
149:     options.Level = CompressionLevel.Optimal;
150: });
151: 
152: builder.Services.Configure<GzipCompressionProviderOptions>(options =>
153: {
154:     options.Level = CompressionLevel.Optimal;
155: });
156: 
157: // In middleware pipeline (early, before UseRouting)
158: app.UseResponseCompression();
159: ```
160: 
161: **Benefits**:
162: - 60-80% reduction in payload sizes
163: - Faster time-to-first-byte
164: - Lower bandwidth costs
165: 
166: ---
167: 
168: ### 3. Rate Limiting Middleware (HIGH PRIORITY)
169: 
170: **Current State**: No rate limiting
171: **Impact**: API vulnerable to abuse, DoS attacks, and excessive usage
172: 
173: **Recommendation**: Add sliding window rate limiting
174: 
175: ```csharp
176: // Program.cs
177: builder.Services.AddRateLimiter(options =>
178: {
179:     options.RejectionStatusCode = StatusCodes.Status429TooManyRequests;
180: 
181:     // Global policy: 100 requests per minute per IP
182:     options.AddSlidingWindowLimiter("global", opt =>
183:     {
184:         opt.PermitLimit = 100;
185:         opt.Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1);
186:         opt.SegmentsPerWindow = 6; // 10-second segments
187:         opt.QueueProcessingOrder = QueueProcessingOrder.OldestFirst;
188:         opt.QueueLimit = 10;
189:     });
190: 
191:     // Authenticated users: 500 requests per minute
192:     options.AddSlidingWindowLimiter("authenticated", opt =>
193:     {
194:         opt.PermitLimit = 500;
195:         opt.Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1);
196:         opt.SegmentsPerWindow = 6;
197:     });
198: 
199:     // Write operations: 20 per minute (prevent spam)
200:     options.AddFixedWindowLimiter("write", opt =>
201:     {
202:         opt.PermitLimit = 20;
203:         opt.Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1);
204:     });
205: 
206:     options.OnRejected = async (context, token) =>
207:     {
208:         context.HttpContext.Response.Headers["Retry-After"] = "60";
209:         await context.HttpContext.Response.WriteAsJsonAsync(new
210:         {
211:             error = "Rate limit exceeded",
212:             retryAfter = 60
213:         }, token);
214:     };
215: });
216: 
217: // In middleware pipeline (after UseRouting, before UseAuthentication)
218: app.UseRateLimiter();
219: ```
220: 
221: **Controller usage**:
222: ```csharp
223: [HttpGet]
224: [AllowAnonymous]
225: [EnableRateLimiting("global")]
226: public async Task<ActionResult<List<EventListDto>>> GetAll() { }
227: 
228: [HttpPost]
229: [Authorize]
230: [EnableRateLimiting("write")]
231: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> Create(...) { }
232: ```
233: 
234: **Benefits**:
235: - Protection against DoS and abuse
236: - Fair usage enforcement
237: - Prevent database overload
238: 
239: ---
240: 
241: ### 4. EF Core Compiled Queries (HIGH PRIORITY)
242: 
243: **Current State**: Dynamic query compilation on every request
244: **Impact**: CPU overhead for query compilation, especially for complex queries
245: 
246: **Recommendation**: Add compiled queries for frequently-used operations
247: 
248: ```csharp
249: // EventRepository.cs
250: public class EventRepository : GenericRepository<Event, Guid>, IEventRepository
251: {
252:     private readonly ExploreDbContext _dbContext;
253: 
254:     // Compiled query for GetAll with includes
255:     private static readonly Func<ExploreDbContext, IAsyncEnumerable<Event>> GetEventsWithDetailsQuery =
256:         EF.CompileAsyncQuery((ExploreDbContext ctx) =>
257:             ctx.Events
258:                 .Include(e => e.EventType)
259:                 .Include(e => e.AudienceGender)
260:                 .Include(e => e.AudienceAge)
261:                 .Include(e => e.Actor)
262:                 .Include(e => e.Madhab)
263:                 .Include(e => e.VisibilityType)
264:                 .Include(e => e.EventStatus)
265:                 .Include(e => e.EventFormat)
266:                 .AsNoTracking());
267: 
268:     // Compiled query for GetById with includes
269:     private static readonly Func<ExploreDbContext, Guid, Task<Event?>> GetEventByIdQuery =
270:         EF.CompileAsyncQuery((ExploreDbContext ctx, Guid id) =>
271:             ctx.Events
272:                 .Include(e => e.EventType)
273:                 .Include(e => e.AudienceGender)
274:                 .Include(e => e.Actor)
275:                 .FirstOrDefault(e => e.Id == id));
276: 
277:     public async Task<List<Event>> GetEventsWithDetails()
278:     {
279:         var events = new List<Event>();
280:         await foreach (var evt in GetEventsWithDetailsQuery(_dbContext))
281:         {
282:             events.Add(evt);
283:         }
284:         return events;
285:     }
286: 
287:     public async Task<Event?> GetEventWithDetails(Guid id)
288:     {
289:         return await GetEventByIdQuery(_dbContext, id);
290:     }
291: }
292: ```
293: 
294: **Benefits**:
295: - 20-40% faster query execution
296: - Reduced CPU usage
297: - Lower GC pressure
298: 
299: ---
300: 
301: ### 5. Split Queries for Complex Includes (MEDIUM PRIORITY)
302: 
303: **Current State**: Single query with many includes (cartesian explosion risk)
304: **Impact**: Potential performance issues with large datasets
305: 
306: **Recommendation**: Use `AsSplitQuery()` for queries with multiple collection navigations
307: 
308: ```csharp
309: // EventRepository.cs - For queries with collection includes
310: public async Task<Event?> GetEventWithAllDetails(Guid id)
311: {
312:     return await _dbContext.Events
313:         .Include(e => e.EventType)
314:         .Include(e => e.EventSessions)
315:             .ThenInclude(s => s.Location)
316:         .Include(e => e.EventSessions)
317:             .ThenInclude(s => s.EventSessionLanguages)
318:         .Include(e => e.EventCategories)
319:             .ThenInclude(ec => ec.Category)
320:         .Include(e => e.EventTags)
321:             .ThenInclude(et => et.Tag)
322:         .AsSplitQuery()  // Prevents cartesian explosion
323:         .FirstOrDefaultAsync(e => e.Id == id);
324: }
325: ```
326: 
327: **When to use**:
328: - Queries with 2+ collection navigations
329: - Large collections (100+ items)
330: - Queries causing duplicate rows in results
331: 
332: ---

334: ## Security Enhancements 🟡
335: 
336: ### 6. Security Headers Middleware
337: 
338: **Current State**: Only HSTS configured
339: **Recommendation**: Add comprehensive security headers
340: 
341: ```csharp
342: // Create: Explore.API/Middleware/SecurityHeadersMiddleware.cs
343: public class SecurityHeadersMiddleware
344: {
345:     private readonly RequestDelegate _next;
346: 
347:     public SecurityHeadersMiddleware(RequestDelegate next) => _next = next;
348: 
349:     public async Task InvokeAsync(HttpContext context)
350:     {
351:         var headers = context.Response.Headers;
352: 
353:         // Prevent MIME type sniffing
354:         headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff";
355: 
356:         // Prevent clickjacking
357:         headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY";
358: 
359:         // Enable XSS filter
360:         headers["X-XSS-Protection"] = "1; mode=block";
361: 
362:         // Referrer policy
363:         headers["Referrer-Policy"] = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin";
364: 
365:         // Content Security Policy for API (restrictive)
366:         headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = "default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'";
367: 
368:         // Permissions policy
369:         headers["Permissions-Policy"] = "accelerometer=(), camera=(), geolocation=(), gyroscope=(), magnetometer=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=()";
370: 
371:         await _next(context);
372:     }
373: }
374: 
375: // Program.cs - Add before UseRouting()
376: app.UseMiddleware<SecurityHeadersMiddleware>();
377: ```
378: 
379: ### 7. Request Logging Sanitization
380: 
381: **Current State**: Logging includes potential PII
382: **Recommendation**: Sanitize sensitive data in logs
383: 
384: ```csharp
385: // Consider masking:

388: // - User IDs in certain contexts

391: ---
392: 
393: ## Code Consistency Improvements 🟢
394: 
395: ### 8. Replace Newtonsoft.Json with System.Text.Json
396: 
397: **Current State**: `ExceptionMiddleware.cs` uses Newtonsoft.Json (line 1)
398: **Rest of API**: Uses System.Text.Json (ASP.NET Core default)
399: 
400: **Recommendation**: Standardize on System.Text.Json
401: 
402: ```csharp
403: // ExceptionMiddleware.cs - Replace
404: using Newtonsoft.Json;  // REMOVE
405: 
406: // With
407: using System.Text.Json;  // ADD
408: 
409: // Change serialization calls from:
410: string result = JsonConvert.SerializeObject(new ErrorDetails() { ... });
411: 
412: // To:
413: string result = JsonSerializer.Serialize(new ErrorDetails() { ... },
414:     new JsonSerializerOptions { PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase });
415: ```
416: 
417: **Benefits**:
418: - Consistent JSON handling across the API
419: - Better performance (System.Text.Json is faster)
420: - Smaller memory footprint
421: - No external dependency for JSON

423: ---
424: 
425: ### 9. API Versioning Middleware
426: 
427: **Current State**: Manual URL path versioning (`/api/v1/`)
428: **Recommendation**: Use official API Versioning package for enterprise features
429: 
430: ```csharp
431: // Install: Asp.Versioning.Http, Asp.Versioning.Mvc
432: 
433: builder.Services.AddApiVersioning(options =>
434: {
435:     options.DefaultApiVersion = new ApiVersion(1, 0);
436:     options.AssumeDefaultVersionWhenUnspecified = true;
437:     options.ReportApiVersions = true;
438:     options.ApiVersionReader = ApiVersionReader.Combine(
439:         new UrlSegmentApiVersionReader(),
440:         new HeaderApiVersionReader("X-Api-Version"),
441:         new MediaTypeApiVersionReader("version")
442:     );
443: });
444: 
445: // Controller usage
446: [ApiController]
447: [Route("api/v{version:apiVersion}/[controller]")]
448: [ApiVersion("1.0")]
449: public class EventController : ControllerBase { }
450: ```
451: 
452: **Benefits**:
453: - Sunset headers for deprecated versions
454: - Multiple version readers (URL, header, media type)

## File: dev/active/secret-management-implementation.md
````markdown
   1: # Secret Management Implementation Plan (Enterprise-Grade)
   2: 
   3: > **Purpose**: Implement a unified, secret-manager-agnostic configuration system with database-backed dynamic settings, secure bootstrap, key rotation, and enterprise observability.
   4: >
   5: > **Date**: January 2026
   6: > **Status**: Planning
   7: > **Version**: 2.0 (Refactored based on security review)
   8: 
   9: ---
  10: 
  11: ## Executive Summary
  12: 
  13: This plan creates an **enterprise-grade layered configuration architecture** that:
  14: 
  15: 1. **Solves bootstrap trust** - Uses cloud-native identity (Managed Identity, IRSA, AppRole) to avoid credential chicken-and-egg
  16: 2. **Supports key rotation and versioning** - Key version metadata, staged re-encryption, zero-downtime rotation
  17: 3. **Enforces fail-fast in production** - `ValidateOnStart` for required secrets, health check integration
  18: 4. **Uses robust refresh patterns** - `IHostedService` with `PeriodicTimer`, exponential backoff, jittered intervals
  19: 5. **Provides observability and audit** - Prometheus metrics, health endpoints, structured audit logging
  20: 6. **Handles connection pool invalidation** - Atomic client swap patterns for secret rotation
  21: 7. **Constrains database secrets** - Only operational settings in DB, high-value secrets in external managers
  22: 
  23: ---
  24: 
  25: ## Architecture Overview
  26: 
  27: ```
  28: Configuration Priority (Highest to Lowest):
  29: +------------------------------------------------------------------+
  30: |  1. DATABASE (Operational Settings ONLY)                          |
  31: |     - Admin-managed: SMTP, feature flags, UI customization        |
  32: |     - Encrypted with versioned keys (supports rotation)           |
  33: |     - NEVER: DB connection, Master Key, Keycloak secrets          |
  34: |     - Live reload via IOptionsMonitor                             |
  35: +------------------------------------------------------------------+
  36:           |
  37:           v (fallback if not in DB)
  38: +------------------------------------------------------------------+
  39: |  2. SECRET MANAGER (High-Value Secrets)                           |
  40: |     - Infisical / Vault / Azure KV / AWS SM                       |
  41: |     - Bootstrap secrets: DB connection, Master Key, API keys      |
  42: |     - Cloud-native auth: Managed Identity, IRSA, AppRole          |
  43: |     - Token/lease renewal with jittered backoff                   |
  44: +------------------------------------------------------------------+
  45:           |
  46:           v (fallback if no secret manager configured)
  47: +------------------------------------------------------------------+
  48: |  3. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES (Self-Hoster Fallback)                  |
  49: |     - Plain env vars set by user                                  |
  50: |     - Docker Compose, Kubernetes, systemd, etc.                   |
  51: |     - Zero external dependencies                                  |
  52: +------------------------------------------------------------------+
  53:           |
  54:           v (fallback for defaults)
  55: +------------------------------------------------------------------+
  56: |  4. APPSETTINGS.JSON (Non-Sensitive Defaults Only)                |
  57: |     - Logging configuration                                       |
  58: |     - Feature toggles with SAFE defaults (disabled)               |
  59: |     - NEVER: Any secrets or credentials                           |
  60: +------------------------------------------------------------------+
  61: ```
  62: 
  63: ---
  64: 
  65: ## Critical Security Gaps Addressed
  66: 
  67: ### 1. Bootstrap Trust Problem (SOLVED)
  68: 
  69: **Problem**: How to fetch master key and secret manager credentials on first boot without hardcoding?
  70: 
  71: **Solution**: Cloud-native identity + envelope encryption
  72: 
  73: ```
  74: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  75: │                    BOOTSTRAP FLOW                                │
  76: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  77: │  AZURE (Managed Identity):                                       │
  78: │  1. App starts with NO credentials in code/env                   │
  79: │  2. DefaultAzureCredential auto-discovers Managed Identity       │
  80: │  3. Fetches bootstrap secrets from Key Vault                     │
  81: │  4. Uses secrets to initialize DB, other services                │
  82: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  83: │  AWS (IRSA - IAM Roles for Service Accounts):                    │
  84: │  1. Pod service account annotated with IAM role                  │
  85: │  2. AWS SDK auto-discovers IRSA credentials                      │
  86: │  3. Fetches bootstrap secrets from Secrets Manager               │
  87: │  4. Uses secrets to initialize DB, other services                │
  88: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  89: │  VAULT (AppRole with Response Wrapping):                         │
  90: │  1. Orchestrator provisions wrapped SecretID (single-use)        │
  91: │  2. App unwraps token to get SecretID                            │
  92: │  3. App authenticates with RoleID + SecretID                     │
  93: │  4. Fetches bootstrap secrets from Vault KV                      │
  94: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  95: │  INFISICAL (Machine Identity):                                   │
  96: │  1. Machine Identity ClientID/Secret from env (minimal trust)    │
  97: │  2. SDK authenticates and fetches all secrets                    │
  98: │  3. Secrets injected into configuration                          │
  99: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 100: │  SELF-HOSTED (Environment Variables):                            │
 101: │  1. User manually sets all required env vars                     │
 102: │  2. No secret manager dependency                                 │
 103: │  3. Suitable for small deployments                               │
 104: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 105: ```
 106: 
 107: ### 2. Key Rotation and Versioning (SOLVED)
 108: 
 109: **Problem**: No key version metadata, no re-encryption workflow.
 110: 
 111: **Solution**: Key version envelope with staged rotation
 112: 
 113: ```csharp
 114: // AppSetting entity with key versioning
 115: public class AppSetting
 116: {
 117:     public string Key { get; set; } = string.Empty;
 118:     public string EncryptedValue { get; set; } = string.Empty;
 119:     
 120:     // KEY VERSIONING (NEW)
 121:     public int KeyVersion { get; set; } = 1;  // Which master key version encrypted this
 122:     public DateTime EncryptedAt { get; set; }
 123:     
 124:     // AUDIT (NEW)
 125:     public Guid? EncryptedBy { get; set; }
 126:     public DateTime UpdatedAt { get; set; }
 127:     public Guid? UpdatedBy { get; set; }
 128:     
 129:     // CONCURRENCY (NEW)
 130:     public byte[] RowVersion { get; set; } = null!;  // EF Core concurrency token
 131:     
 132:     // METADATA
 133:     public bool IsSensitive { get; set; } = true;
 134:     public string? Description { get; set; }
 135:     public string? Category { get; set; }
 136: }
 137: 
 138: // Encryption service with key versioning
 139: public interface IEncryptionService
 140: {
 141:     (string Ciphertext, int KeyVersion) Encrypt(string plaintext);
 142:     string Decrypt(string ciphertext, int keyVersion);
 143:     int CurrentKeyVersion { get; }
 144:     Task ReEncryptAllAsync(CancellationToken ct);  // For key rotation
 145: }
 146: ```
 147: 
 148: **Rotation Workflow**:
 149: ```
 150: 1. Admin generates new master key (version N+1)
 151: 2. New key stored in secret manager alongside old key (version N)
 152: 3. Background job re-encrypts all AppSettings with version N+1
 153: 4. After all re-encrypted, old key (version N) marked for deletion
 154: 5. Grace period, then old key deleted
 155: ```
 156: 
 157: ### 3. Fail-Fast and Validation (SOLVED)
 158: 
 159: **Problem**: Fallback chain can mask misconfiguration in production.
 160: 
 161: **Solution**: `ValidateOnStart` + environment-aware fail-fast + health checks
 162: 
 163: ```csharp
 164: // Required secrets validation
 165: public class RequiredSecretsValidator : IValidateOptions<SecretProviderOptions>
 166: {
 167:     public ValidateOptionsResult Validate(string? name, SecretProviderOptions options)
 168:     {
 169:         var errors = new List<string>();
 170:         
 171:         // Always required
 172:         if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.DatabaseConnectionString))
 173:             errors.Add("Database:ConnectionString is required");
 174:         
 175:         // Required if using secret manager
 176:         if (options.Provider != SecretProviderType.None)
 177:         {
 178:             switch (options.Provider)
 179:             {
 180:                 case SecretProviderType.Infisical:
 181:                     if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.InfisicalClientId))
 182:                         errors.Add("Infisical:ClientId is required when using Infisical");
 183:                     if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.InfisicalClientSecret))
 184:                         errors.Add("Infisical:ClientSecret is required when using Infisical");
 185:                     break;
 186:                 // ... other providers
 187:             }
 188:         }
 189:         
 190:         return errors.Count > 0
 191:             ? ValidateOptionsResult.Fail(errors)
 192:             : ValidateOptionsResult.Success;
 193:     }
 194: }
 195: 
 196: // In Program.cs
 197: builder.Services.AddOptions<SecretProviderOptions>()
 198:     .BindConfiguration("SecretProvider")
 199:     .ValidateOnStart();  // CRITICAL: Fail at startup, not at first use
 200: ```
 201: 
 202: ### 4. Robust Refresh with IHostedService (SOLVED)
 203: 
 204: **Problem**: Timer with async fire-and-forget causes overlapping loads and swallowed exceptions.
 205: 
 206: **Solution**: `IHostedService` with `PeriodicTimer`, serialized runs, exponential backoff
 207: 
 208: ```csharp
 209: // Location: Explore.Secrets/Services/SecretRefreshService.cs
 210: 
 211: namespace Explore.Secrets.Services;
 212: 
 213: /// <summary>
 214: /// ABOUTME: Background service that periodically refreshes secrets from external providers.
 215: /// Uses PeriodicTimer for accurate intervals, serializes runs, and implements exponential backoff.
 216: /// </summary>
 217: public sealed class SecretRefreshService : BackgroundService
 218: {
 219:     private readonly ISecretProvider _secretProvider;
 220:     private readonly IConfigurationRoot _configurationRoot;
 221:     private readonly ILogger<SecretRefreshService> _logger;
 222:     private readonly SecretRefreshOptions _options;
 223:     private readonly SecretRefreshMetrics _metrics;
 224:     
 225:     private int _consecutiveFailures;
 226:     private static readonly Random _jitter = new();
 227: 
 228:     public SecretRefreshService(
 229:         ISecretProvider secretProvider,
 230:         IConfiguration configuration,
 231:         ILogger<SecretRefreshService> logger,
 232:         IOptions<SecretRefreshOptions> options,
 233:         SecretRefreshMetrics metrics)
 234:     {
 235:         _secretProvider = secretProvider;
 236:         _configurationRoot = (IConfigurationRoot)configuration;
 237:         _logger = logger;
 238:         _options = options.Value;
 239:         _metrics = metrics;
 240:     }
 241: 
 242:     protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken)
 243:     {
 244:         _logger.LogInformation("Secret refresh service starting. Interval: {Interval}", _options.RefreshInterval);
 245:         
 246:         // Add jitter to initial delay to prevent thundering herd in multi-instance deployments
 247:         var initialDelay = _options.RefreshInterval + TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(_jitter.Next(0, 5000));
 248:         
 249:         using var timer = new PeriodicTimer(initialDelay);
 250:         
 251:         while (await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken))
 252:         {
 253:             using var activity = _metrics.StartRefreshActivity();
 254:             
 255:             try
 256:             {
 257:                 _logger.LogDebug("Starting secret refresh cycle");
 258:                 var stopwatch = Stopwatch.StartNew();
 259:                 
 260:                 await _secretProvider.RefreshAsync(stoppingToken);
 261:                 
 262:                 // Trigger configuration reload
 263:                 foreach (var provider in _configurationRoot.Providers)
 264:                 {
 265:                     if (provider is IDisposable disposable)
 266:                     {
 267:                         // Reload supported providers
 268:                         provider.Load();
 269:                     }
 270:                 }
 271:                 
 272:                 stopwatch.Stop();
 273:                 _consecutiveFailures = 0;
 274:                 
 275:                 _metrics.RecordRefreshSuccess(stopwatch.Elapsed);
 276:                 _logger.LogInformation("Secret refresh completed in {Duration}ms", stopwatch.ElapsedMilliseconds);
 277:                 
 278:                 // Reset timer to normal interval after success
 279:                 timer.Period = AddJitter(_options.RefreshInterval);
 280:             }
 281:             catch (OperationCanceledException) when (stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)
 282:             {
 283:                 _logger.LogInformation("Secret refresh service stopping");
 284:                 break;
 285:             }
 286:             catch (Exception ex)
 287:             {
 288:                 _consecutiveFailures++;
 289:                 _metrics.RecordRefreshFailure(ex);
 290:                 
 291:                 var backoffDelay = CalculateBackoffDelay();
 292:                 _logger.LogError(ex, 
 293:                     "Secret refresh failed (attempt {Attempt}). Next retry in {Delay}",
 294:                     _consecutiveFailures, backoffDelay);
 295:                 
 296:                 // Apply backoff for next iteration
 297:                 timer.Period = backoffDelay;
 298:             }
 299:         }
 300:     }
 301: 
 302:     private TimeSpan CalculateBackoffDelay()
 303:     {
 304:         // Exponential backoff: base * 2^failures, capped at max
 305:         var exponentialDelay = _options.BaseBackoffDelay * Math.Pow(2, Math.Min(_consecutiveFailures, 6));
 306:         var cappedDelay = Math.Min(exponentialDelay.TotalMilliseconds, _options.MaxBackoffDelay.TotalMilliseconds);
 307:         
 308:         return AddJitter(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(cappedDelay));
 309:     }
 310: 
 311:     private static TimeSpan AddJitter(TimeSpan baseInterval)
 312:     {
 313:         // Add 0-10% jitter to prevent thundering herd
 314:         var jitterMs = _jitter.Next(0, (int)(baseInterval.TotalMilliseconds * 0.1));
 315:         return baseInterval + TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(jitterMs);
 316:     }
 317: }
 318: 
 319: public class SecretRefreshOptions
 320: {
 321:     public TimeSpan RefreshInterval { get; set; } = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);
 322:     public TimeSpan BaseBackoffDelay { get; set; } = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10);
 323:     public TimeSpan MaxBackoffDelay { get; set; } = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);
 324: }
 325: ```
 326: 
 327: ### 5. Observability and Audit (SOLVED)
 328: 
 329: **Problem**: No metrics, health checks, or audit trail.
 330: 
 331: **Solution**: Prometheus metrics, health endpoints, structured audit logging
 332: 
 333: ```csharp
 334: // Location: Explore.Secrets/Observability/SecretRefreshMetrics.cs
 335: 
 336: namespace Explore.Secrets.Observability;
 337: 
 338: /// <summary>
 339: /// ABOUTME: Prometheus metrics for secret refresh operations.
 340: /// Tracks refresh success/failure rates, latency, and provider health.
 341: /// </summary>
 342: public class SecretRefreshMetrics
 343: {
 344:     private readonly Counter<long> _refreshTotal;
 345:     private readonly Counter<long> _refreshFailures;
 346:     private readonly Histogram<double> _refreshDuration;
 347:     private readonly ObservableGauge<long> _lastRefreshTimestamp;
 348:     private readonly ObservableGauge<int> _consecutiveFailures;
 349:     
 350:     private long _lastSuccessfulRefresh;
 351:     private int _currentConsecutiveFailures;
 352: 
 353:     public SecretRefreshMetrics(IMeterFactory meterFactory)
 354:     {
 355:         var meter = meterFactory.Create("Explore.Secrets");
 356:         
 357:         _refreshTotal = meter.CreateCounter<long>(
 358:             "secrets_refresh_total",
 359:             description: "Total number of secret refresh attempts");
 360:         
 361:         _refreshFailures = meter.CreateCounter<long>(
 362:             "secrets_refresh_failures_total",
 363:             description: "Total number of failed secret refresh attempts");
 364:         
 365:         _refreshDuration = meter.CreateHistogram<double>(
 366:             "secrets_refresh_duration_seconds",
 367:             unit: "seconds",
 368:             description: "Duration of secret refresh operations");
 369:         
 370:         _lastRefreshTimestamp = meter.CreateObservableGauge(
 371:             "secrets_last_refresh_timestamp",
 372:             () => _lastSuccessfulRefresh,
 373:             description: "Unix timestamp of last successful refresh");
 374:         
 375:         _consecutiveFailures = meter.CreateObservableGauge(
 376:             "secrets_consecutive_failures",
 377:             () => _currentConsecutiveFailures,
 378:             description: "Current number of consecutive refresh failures");
 379:     }
 380: 
 381:     public Activity? StartRefreshActivity()
 382:     {
 383:         _refreshTotal.Add(1);
 384:         return Activity.Current?.Source.StartActivity("SecretRefresh");
 385:     }
 386: 
 387:     public void RecordRefreshSuccess(TimeSpan duration)
 388:     {
 389:         _refreshDuration.Record(duration.TotalSeconds);
 390:         _lastSuccessfulRefresh = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds();
 391:         _currentConsecutiveFailures = 0;
 392:     }
 393: 
 394:     public void RecordRefreshFailure(Exception ex)
 395:     {
 396:         _refreshFailures.Add(1, new KeyValuePair<string, object?>("exception_type", ex.GetType().Name));
 397:         _currentConsecutiveFailures++;
 398:     }
 399: }
 400: 
 401: // Health check for secret provider
 402: public class SecretProviderHealthCheck : IHealthCheck
 403: {
 404:     private readonly ISecretProvider _provider;
 405:     private readonly SecretRefreshMetrics _metrics;
 406:     private readonly ILogger<SecretProviderHealthCheck> _logger;
 407: 
 408:     public async Task<HealthCheckResult> CheckHealthAsync(
 409:         HealthCheckContext context,
 410:         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 411:     {
 412:         try
 413:         {
 414:             // Try to fetch a known secret (or use a health-check specific key)
 415:             var result = await _provider.GetSecretAsync("_health_check", cancellationToken);
 416:             
 417:             var data = new Dictionary<string, object>
 418:             {
 419:                 ["provider"] = _provider.GetType().Name,
 420:                 ["supports_refresh"] = _provider.SupportsRefresh,
 421:                 ["last_refresh"] = DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds(_metrics.LastRefreshTimestamp)
 422:             };
 423:             
 424:             return HealthCheckResult.Healthy("Secret provider is reachable", data);
 425:         }
 426:         catch (Exception ex)
 427:         {
 428:             _logger.LogWarning(ex, "Secret provider health check failed");
 429:             return HealthCheckResult.Unhealthy("Secret provider is unreachable", ex);
 430:         }
 431:     }
 432: }
 433: 
 434: // Audit logging for secret access
 435: public class AuditingSecretProvider : ISecretProvider
 436: {
 437:     private readonly ISecretProvider _inner;
 438:     private readonly ILogger<AuditingSecretProvider> _logger;
 439:     private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _httpContextAccessor;
 440: 
 441:     public async Task<string?> GetSecretAsync(string key, CancellationToken ct = default)
 442:     {
 443:         var userId = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("sub")?.Value ?? "system";
 444:         var correlationId = Activity.Current?.Id ?? Guid.NewGuid().ToString();
 445:         
 446:         _logger.LogInformation(
 447:             "SecretAccess: Key={SecretKey}, User={UserId}, CorrelationId={CorrelationId}, Timestamp={Timestamp}",
 448:             RedactKey(key), userId, correlationId, DateTimeOffset.UtcNow);
 449:         
 450:         return await _inner.GetSecretAsync(key, ct);
 451:     }
 452: 
 453:     private static string RedactKey(string key)
 454:     {
 455:         // Redact sensitive parts of key names for logging
 456:         if (key.Contains("password", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
 457:             key.Contains("secret", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
 458:             key.Contains("key", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
 459:         {
 460:             var parts = key.Split(':');
 461:             return string.Join(":", parts.Select((p, i) => i == parts.Length - 1 ? "***" : p));
 462:         }
 463:         return key;
 464:     }
 465: }
 466: ```
