1336: 
1337: ## Secret Categorization (What Goes Where)
1338: 
1339: ### HIGH-VALUE SECRETS (External Secret Manager ONLY)
1340: 
1341: These secrets **MUST NEVER** be stored in the database:
1342: 
1343: | Secret | Reason |
1344: |--------|--------|
1345: | `Database:ConnectionString` | Bootstrap dependency - needed to read DB |
1346: | `Security:MasterKey*` | Encrypts DB settings - chicken-and-egg |
1347: | `Keycloak:ClientSecret` | Auth infrastructure |
1348: | `S3:SecretAccessKey` | Cloud credentials |
1349: | Secret manager credentials | Bootstrap dependency |
1350: 
1351: ### OPERATIONAL SETTINGS (Database OK)
1352: 
1353: These settings are safe for database storage:
1354: 
1355: | Setting | Reason |
1356: |---------|--------|
1357: | `Smtp:Host`, `Smtp:Port` | Non-critical, admin-changeable |
1358: | `Email:FromAddress`, `Email:FromName` | Non-critical |
1359: | `Features:*` | Feature flags |
1360: | `UI:*` | Customization settings |
1361: | `RateLimiting:*` | Operational tuning |
1362: 
1363: ---
1364: 
1365: ## Implementation Phases (Updated)
1366: 
1367: ### Phase 1: Core Infrastructure with Validation (6-8 hours)
1368: 
1369: **Tasks:**
1370: 1. Create `Explore.Secrets` project with proper structure
1371: 2. Implement `ISecretProvider` interface with health info
1372: 3. Implement `EnvironmentSecretProvider` (fallback)
1373: 4. Implement `RequiredSecretsValidator` with `ValidateOnStart`
1374: 5. Implement `SecretProviderFactory`
1375: 6. Create `ServiceCollectionExtensions` with proper DI registration
1376: 7. Add comprehensive unit tests
1377: 
1378: **Acceptance Criteria:**
1379: - `ValidateOnStart` fails if required secrets missing
1380: - `SECRET_PROVIDER=none` works correctly
1381: - Health check endpoint returns provider status
1382: - Unit tests achieve >80% coverage
1383: 
1384: ### Phase 2: Observability Infrastructure (3-4 hours)
1385: 
1386: **Tasks:**
1387: 1. Implement `SecretRefreshMetrics` (Prometheus)
1388: 2. Implement `SecretProviderHealthCheck`
1389: 3. Implement `AuditingSecretProviderDecorator`
1390: 4. Wire up health checks to `/health` endpoint
1391: 5. Add metrics endpoint for Prometheus scraping
1392: 
1393: **Acceptance Criteria:**
1394: - Prometheus metrics exposed at `/metrics`
1395: - Health check reflects secret provider status
1396: - Audit logs include correlation ID, user, timestamp
1397: 
1398: ### Phase 3: Infisical Provider with Refresh (3-4 hours)
1399: 
1400: **Tasks:**
1401: 1. Add `Infisical.Sdk` NuGet package
1402: 2. Implement `InfisicalSecretProvider` with Universal Auth
1403: 3. Implement `SecretRefreshService` (IHostedService)
1404: 4. Add exponential backoff and jitter
1405: 5. Add integration tests
1406: 
1407: **Acceptance Criteria:**
1408: - Connects to Infisical and retrieves secrets
1409: - Refresh runs on schedule with backoff on failure
1410: - Metrics track refresh success/failure
1411: - Graceful handling of Infisical unavailability
1412: 
1413: ### Phase 4: Database Configuration with Key Versioning (4-5 hours)
1414: 
1415: **Tasks:**
1416: 1. Add `AppSetting` entity with versioning and audit fields
1417: 2. Add EF Core configuration with constraints
1418: 3. Create migration
1419: 4. Implement `AesEncryptionService` with key versioning
1420: 5. Implement `DbConfigurationProvider` with serialized loads
1421: 6. Implement `KeyRotationService` for re-encryption
1422: 7. Add unit tests for encryption round-trip and versioning
1423: 
1424: **Acceptance Criteria:**
1425: - Settings encrypted with key version metadata
1426: - Re-encryption workflow handles all settings
1427: - Concurrency conflicts handled gracefully
1428: - Check constraint prevents high-value secrets in DB
1429: 
1430: ### Phase 5: Additional Providers (2-3 hours each)
1431: 
1432: **HashiCorp Vault:**
1433: 1. Add `VaultSharp` NuGet package
1434: 2. Implement `VaultSecretProvider` with AppRole auth
1435: 3. Implement token renewal timer
1436: 4. Add response-wrapping support for SecretID
1437: 
1438: **Azure Key Vault:**
1439: 1. Add `Azure.Security.KeyVault.Secrets` + `Azure.Identity`
1440: 2. Implement `AzureKeyVaultSecretProvider`
1441: 3. Use `DefaultAzureCredential` for Managed Identity
1442: 4. Handle credential chain fallback
1443: 
1444: **AWS Secrets Manager:**
1445: 1. Add `AWSSDK.SecretsManager`
1446: 2. Implement `AwsSecretsManagerProvider`
1447: 3. Support IRSA credential chain
1448: 4. Implement caching with TTL
1449: 
1450: ### Phase 6: Connection Pool Rotation (2-3 hours)
1451: 
1452: **Tasks:**
1453: 1. Implement `RotationAwareHttpClientFactory`
1454: 2. Implement `RotationAwareDbContextFactory`
1455: 3. Wire up `IOptionsMonitor` change listeners
1456: 4. Add graceful drain with timeout
1457: 5. Add integration tests for rotation scenarios
1458: 
1459: **Acceptance Criteria:**
1460: - HttpClient rotates on credential change
1461: - DB connections use updated credentials
1462: - No connection leaks during rotation
1463: - Graceful handling of in-flight requests
1464: 
1465: ### Phase 7: Integration and Migration (3-4 hours)
1466: 
1467: **Tasks:**
1468: 1. Add `Explore.Secrets` reference to API and Blazor
1469: 2. Refactor `ConfigurationExtensions.cs`
1470: 3. Update `Program.cs` in each project
1471: 4. Remove Infisical from AppHost
1472: 5. Delete `entrypoint.sh`
1473: 6. Simplify Dockerfile
1474: 7. Update documentation
1475: 
1476: **Acceptance Criteria:**
1477: - API starts independently with any provider
1478: - Blazor starts independently
1479: - Docker image works without Infisical CLI
1480: - Self-hoster documentation complete
1481: 
1482: ---
1483: 
1484: ## Security Checklist
1485: 
1486: - [ ] Master key never stored in database
1487: - [ ] Master key never logged
1488: - [ ] Key material zeroed after use (`CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory`)
1489: - [ ] Secrets redacted in audit logs
1490: - [ ] `ValidateOnStart` enabled for required secrets
1491: - [ ] `FailFast=true` in production
1492: - [ ] Health check doesn't leak secret values
1493: - [ ] Metrics don't include secret content
1494: - [ ] DB check constraint prevents high-value secrets
1495: - [ ] Concurrency token prevents lost updates
1496: - [ ] Token renewal before expiry (75% TTL)
1497: - [ ] Exponential backoff on failures
1498: - [ ] Jitter prevents thundering herd
1499: 
1500: ---
1501: 
1502: ## Disaster Recovery
1503: 
1504: ### Master Key Loss
1505: 
1506: 1. **Prevention**: Store master key in multiple secret managers (Infisical + backup in Vault)
1507: 2. **Recovery**: Re-generate key, re-encrypt all DB settings, update secret manager
1508: 3. **Drill**: Test key recovery quarterly
1509: 
1510: ### Secret Manager Unavailable
1511: 
1512: 1. **Short-term**: Cached secrets continue working (last refresh)
1513: 2. **Medium-term**: Fallback to environment variables if `FailFast=false`
1514: 3. **Long-term**: Restore secret manager access
1515: 
1516: ### Database Settings Corruption
1517: 
1518: 1. **Prevention**: Regular backups, soft-delete pattern
1519: 2. **Recovery**: Restore from backup, re-encrypt with current key
1520: 3. **Audit**: Full audit trail identifies who/when/what changed
1521: 
1522: ---
1523: 
1524: ## References
1525: 
1526: - [OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html)
1527: - [Azure Key Vault Best Practices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/secrets-best-practices)
1528: - [AWS Secrets Manager Best Practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/best-practices.html)
1529: - [HashiCorp Vault AppRole Best Practices](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/auth/approle/approle-pattern)
1530: - [.NET Configuration Providers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/extensions/configuration-providers)
1531: - [Infisical .NET SDK](https://infisical.com/docs/sdks/languages/csharp)
1532: - [VaultSharp GitHub](https://github.com/rajanadar/VaultSharp)
````

## File: dev/active/unified-search-api-implementation.md
````markdown
 1: the search layer—search is where most flexible architectures either shine or feel "broken" to the user.
 2: 
 3: To reassure you: **Yes, you can have a single, unified, fuzzy search that looks through everything (Title, Description, and JSONB) without building a fragmented mess.**
 4: 
 5: Here is the realistic, high-performance "Search Strategy" for your decentralized implementation.
 6: 
 7: ---
 8: 
 9: # THE SEARCH EXECUTION PLAN: THE "UNIFIED SEARCH SHADOW"
10: 
11: To avoid the performance hit of searching across raw JSONB for every user query, we will use a **Search Shadow Table**. This table acts as a flattened "index" of your entire event, combining relational and JSON data into one searchable record.
12: 
13: ## 1. DATA MODEL: `EventSearchIndex`
14: 
15: Instead of searching the `Events` table directly, create a specialized table optimized for **Full-Text** and **Vector** search.
16: 
17: * **Id:** `Guid` (FK to Event)
18: * **TenantId:** `Guid` (For security filtering)
19: * **SearchVector:** `tsvector` (Standard Postgres Full-Text Search)
20: * **SemanticEmbedding:** `vector(1536)` (Using **pgvector** for AI/Concept search)
21: * **RawContent:** `text` (A flat string of *everything* important: Title + Desc + JSONB Values)
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## 2. THE SEARCH MODES (HYBRID SEARCH)
26: 
27: To get the "genius" results you want, the AI Agent should implement a **Hybrid Search** query.
28: 
29: ### A. The "Fuzzy" Keyword Search (Trigrams)
30: 
31: * **Technology:** `pg_trgm` extension.
32: * **How it works:** It breaks words into 3-letter chunks. If a user types "Islma" instead of "Islam," the trigram match (`isl`, `sla`, `lam`) still catches it.
33: * **Target:** `RawContent` column.
34: 
35: ### B. The "Semantic" Vector Search (pgvector)
36: 
37: * **Technology:** `pgvector`.
38: * **How it works:** When an event is saved, the API sends the text to an embedding model (like OpenAI or a local HuggingFace model). It converts the event into a list of numbers (a vector).
39: * **Benefit:** If a user searches for *"Gathering for tech-minded Muslims,"* the vector search will find your event even if those exact words aren't in the title, because it understands the **concept**.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 3. REAL-TIME SYNC LOGIC (NO REDIS NEEDED YET)
44: 
45: You mentioned caching software like Redis. For your scale, **stay inside PostgreSQL** using an **Outbox/Domain Event** pattern. This ensures your search index never drifts from your actual data.
46: 
47: 1. **Event Organizer** saves an event (Relational + JSONB).
48: 2. **MediatR Domain Event** (`EventCreated`) is fired.
49: 3. **SearchIndexer Handler** picks it up:
50: * Flattens the JSONB into a plain text string.
51: * Calls the Embedding API.
52: * Upserts the `EventSearchIndex` table.
53: 
54: 
55: 4. **Result:** The "Search Shadow" is updated in milliseconds.
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: ## 4. REFACTORED PLAN FOR THE AI AGENT
60: 
61: **Command to AI Agent:** "Implement the Unified Search System for the Explore API."
62: 
63: 1. **Enable Extensions:** Ensure `pg_trgm` and `vector` are enabled in the database migrations.
64: 2. **Create Search Table:** Implement the `EventSearchIndex` table with `tsvector` and `vector` columns.
65: 3. **Implement Flattener Service:** Create a service that iterates through the `EventAspects` (JSONB) and extracts only the **Values** (not the keys) into a single large string.
66: 4. **The Search Handler:** Create a MediatR `SearchEventsQueryHandler` that performs a **Hybrid Search**:
67: * Use `pg_trgm` for typo-tolerant keyword matching.
68: * Use `pgvector` for semantic similarity.
69: * **Weighting:** Give the Title a weight of 1.0, the Description 0.6, and the JSONB Aspect data 0.4.
70: 
71: 
72: 5. **Multi-Tenancy:** Ensure every search query includes `WHERE TenantId = @tenantId` to prevent data leakage between communities.
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## WHY THIS IS REALISTIC & SAFE:
77: 
78: * **Performance:** By searching a "Shadow Table" instead of raw JSONB, your queries will stay under 100ms even with hundreds of thousands of events.
79: * **No "Sync Pain":** Because the index is in the *same* database as your events, you get **ACID compliance**. You will never have a situation where an event exists in the DB but is "missing" from search because an external sync failed.
80: * **Future Proof:** If you decide to move to a dedicated search engine (like Typesense or Meilisearch) later, you just point the sync worker there. Your core logic doesn't change.
81: 
82: ### The Prediction:
83: 
84: If you implement the **pgvector + Trigram** hybrid, your users will feel like the search "reads their mind." It handles typos perfectly (Trigrams) and it handles "meaning" perfectly (Vectors). This is the gold standard for 2026 API design.
85: 
86: **Actionable Follow-up:**
87: Should I provide the specific SQL and C# `SearchIndex` entity configuration for your AI Agent to follow exactly?
````

## File: docs/ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md
````markdown
  1: # Administrative Hierarchy
  2: 
  3: > **Authority Model and Permission Boundaries**
  4: >
  5: > This document defines the administrative roles, their authorities, and the governance model
  6: > for the platform.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: The platform implements a strict hierarchical authority model that separates infrastructure concerns from business operations. This ensures that SaaS providers, self-hosters, and community administrators each have appropriate control without overstepping boundaries.
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## Role Definitions
 19: 
 20: ### Instance Administrator (Super Admin)
 21: 
 22: **Identity**: The organization or individual who operates the physical/virtual infrastructure.
 23: 
 24: **Examples**:
 25: - SaaS platform operator
 26: - IT department running self-hosted instance
 27: - DevOps team managing infrastructure
 28: 
 29: **Authority Scope**:
 30: 
 31: | Area | Can Do | Cannot Do |
 32: |------|--------|-----------|
 33: | **Infrastructure** | Server configuration, scaling, backups | Access tenant business data |
 34: | **Modules** | Enable/disable globally, set restrictions | Use modules within tenants |
 35: | **Tenants** | Create, suspend, archive, purge | Make business decisions for tenants |
 36: | **Policies** | Lock settings, enforce quotas | Override tenant preferences within allowed bounds |
 37: | **Security** | Authentication providers, encryption | Impersonate tenant users |
 38: 
 39: ### Tenant Administrator (Community Admin)
 40: 
 41: **Identity**: The organization or individual who manages a specific community/tenant.
 42: 
 43: **Examples**:
 44: - Mosque administrator
 45: - Event organizer for a community
 46: - Organization leadership
 47: 
 48: **Authority Scope**:
 49: 
 50: | Area | Can Do | Cannot Do |
 51: |------|--------|-----------|
 52: | **Configuration** | Customize allowed settings | Override locked settings |
 53: | **Modules** | Enable from allowed set | Enable globally disabled modules |
 54: | **Users** | Manage membership, roles | Access other tenants' users |
 55: | **Content** | Moderate, publish, archive | Bypass instance policies |
 56: | **Branding** | Colors, logos, themes | Change core UI patterns |
 57: 
 58: ### Organization Administrator
 59: 
 60: **Identity**: A user with elevated privileges within a specific organization entity.
 61: 
 62: **Authority Scope**:
 63: - Manage organization members and roles
 64: - Create and manage events
 65: - Approve registrations
 66: - Respond to reviews
 67: 
 68: ### Standard User
 69: 
 70: **Identity**: Regular platform user within a tenant.
 71: 
 72: **Authority Scope**:
 73: - View public content
 74: - Register for events (if permitted)
 75: - Manage own profile
 76: - Create content (if permitted by policies)
 77: 
 78: ---
 79: 
 80: ## Permission Boundaries
 81: 
 82: ### What Instance Admin CANNOT Do
 83: 
 84: These are hard boundaries protecting tenant autonomy:
 85: 
 86: | Restriction | Rationale |
 87: |-------------|-----------|
 88: | Access tenant business data | Privacy, data sovereignty |
 89: | Read individual user records | GDPR, privacy regulations |
 90: | Modify tenant content | Business autonomy |
 91: | Override tenant business rules | Operational independence |
 92: | Access tenant API tokens | Security isolation |
 93: 
 94: ### What Tenant Admin CANNOT Do
 95: 
 96: These are hard boundaries protecting platform integrity:
 97: 
 98: | Restriction | Rationale |
 99: |-------------|-----------|
100: | Disable enforced security policies | Platform security |
101: | Access other tenants' data | Multi-tenant isolation |
102: | Exceed resource quotas | Fair resource usage |
103: | Enable unapproved modules | Platform consistency |
104: | Modify system tables | Data integrity |
105: 
106: ---
107: 
108: ## Authority Cascade
109: 
110: ### Setting Resolution Order
111: 
112: 1. **System Default** → Baseline value
113: 2. **Instance Policy** → May override or lock
114: 3. **Tenant Configuration** → May override if not locked
115: 4. **User Preference** → May override if delegated
116: 
117: ### Lock States
118: 
119: | State | Instance Admin | Tenant Admin | User |
120: |-------|----------------|--------------|------|
121: | **System Default** | Override ✅ | Override ✅ | Override ✅ |
122: | **Instance Locked** | Override ✅ | Override ❌ | Override ❌ |
123: | **Tenant Locked** | Override ✅ | Override ✅ | Override ❌ |
124: | **User Preference** | Override ✅ | Override ✅ | Override ✅ |
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## Enforcement Policies
129: 
130: ### Policy Types
131: 
132: | Type | Enforced By | Example |
133: |------|-------------|---------|
134: | **Technical** | System code | Authentication required |
135: | **Configuration** | Settings engine | Render mode restrictions |
136: | **Resource** | Quota service | Storage limits |
137: | **Compliance** | Audit system | Data retention rules |
138: 
139: ### Policy Priority
140: 
141: When policies conflict:
142: 1. Legal/Compliance (highest priority)
143: 2. Security policies
144: 3. Instance policies
145: 4. Tenant policies
146: 5. User preferences (lowest priority)
147: 
148: ---
149: 
150: ## Delegation Model
151: 
152: ### Instance → Tenant Delegation
153: 
154: Instance Admin can delegate specific authorities:
155: 
156: | Delegatable | Default | Rationale |
157: |-------------|---------|-----------|
158: | Module selection | ✅ Delegated | Business flexibility |
159: | Branding | ✅ Delegated | Community identity |
160: | User management | ✅ Delegated | Operational need |
161: | Security settings | ❌ Locked | Platform protection |
162: | Payment processing | ⚙️ Configurable | Business model dependent |
163: 
164: ### Tenant → Organization Delegation
165: 
166: Tenant Admin can delegate to Organization Admins:
167: 
168: | Delegatable | Default | Rationale |
169: |-------------|---------|-----------|
170: | Event management | ✅ Delegated | Core function |
171: | Member management | ✅ Delegated | Operational need |
172: | Content moderation | ⚙️ Configurable | Trust level dependent |
173: | Financial access | ❌ Restricted | Liability |
174: 
175: ---
176: 
177: ## Audit and Accountability
178: 
179: ### Audit Requirements
180: 
181: | Role | Actions Audited | Retention |
182: |------|-----------------|-----------|
183: | Instance Admin | All system changes | Indefinite |
184: | Tenant Admin | Configuration, user management | Per policy |
185: | Organization Admin | Content, membership changes | Per policy |
186: | User | Security-relevant actions | Per policy |
187: 
188: ### Accountability Chain
189: 
190: Every administrative action must be:
191: 1. **Authenticated** - Verified identity
192: 2. **Authorized** - Proper role/permission
193: 3. **Logged** - Recorded with context
194: 4. **Traceable** - Linkable to human actor
195: 
196: ---
197: 
198: ## Special Scenarios
199: 
200: ### Emergency Access
201: 
202: Instance Admin may bypass restrictions only when:
203: - Security incident response
204: - Legal compliance requirement
205: - Disaster recovery
206: - Explicit tenant consent
207: 
208: **All emergency access is fully audited and reported.**
209: 
210: ### Tenant Offboarding
211: 
212: When a tenant leaves:
213: 1. Data export provided to tenant
214: 2. Grace period for data retrieval
215: 3. Anonymization of shared data
216: 4. Complete deletion after retention period
217: 
218: ### Dispute Resolution
219: 
220: When tenant and instance policies conflict:
221: 1. Instance policies prevail for security/legal
222: 2. Tenant preferences prevail for business
223: 3. Escalation path defined in service agreement
224: 
225: ---
226: 
227: ## Related Documentation
228: 
229: - **[MULTI_TENANCY.md](MULTI_TENANCY.md)** - Tenant isolation model
230: - **[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)** - Authentication and authorization
231: - **[OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md)** - Operational procedures
232: 
233: ## Implementation Reference
234: 
235: For code patterns:
236: - **`auth-patterns`** skill - Role-based authorization
237: - **`clean-architecture-rules`** skill - Layer boundaries
````

## File: docs/DEPLOYMENT_MODES.md
````markdown
  1: # Deployment Modes
  2: 
  3: > **Single-Tenant vs Multi-Tenant Deployment Strategies**
  4: >
  5: > This document describes how the platform supports both dedicated single-tenant
  6: > and shared multi-tenant deployments from a single codebase.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: The platform supports two deployment modes from the **same codebase**:
 15: 
 16: | Mode | Description | Target Use Case |
 17: |------|-------------|-----------------|
 18: | **Single-Tenant** | One community per installation | Self-hosted, dedicated deployments |
 19: | **Multi-Tenant** | Multiple communities per installation | SaaS, shared infrastructure |
 20: 
 21: **Key Insight**: The codebase is always multi-tenant internally. Single-tenant mode is a "mask" that simplifies the experience while preserving the underlying architecture.
 22: 
 23: ---
 24: 
 25: ## Virtual Tenant Strategy
 26: 
 27: ### How It Works
 28: 
 29: Instead of maintaining two codebases:
 30: 1. Multi-tenant code is the foundation
 31: 2. Single-tenant mode forces `TenantId = Default`
 32: 3. Tenant management UI is hidden/shown based on mode
 33: 4. Mode can be switched at runtime
 34: 
 35: ### Benefits
 36: 
 37: | Benefit | Description |
 38: |---------|-------------|
 39: | **One Codebase** | No divergence between modes |
 40: | **Upgrade Path** | Single-tenant can become multi-tenant |
 41: | **Testing Simplicity** | One set of tests covers both modes |
 42: | **Consistent Security** | Same isolation mechanisms apply |
 43: 
 44: ---
 45: 
 46: ## Mode Characteristics
 47: 
 48: ### Single-Tenant Mode
 49: 
 50: **Behavior**:
 51: - `TenantId` hardcoded to `Default` tenant
 52: - Tenant management UI hidden
 53: - Instance Admin and Tenant Admin permissions merged
 54: - No subdomain/header-based routing
 55: - Simplified first-run experience
 56: 
 57: **Experience**:
 58: - Feels like a traditional single-user application
 59: - Admin sees combined settings panel
 60: - No awareness of multi-tenant engine underneath
 61: 
 62: ### Multi-Tenant Mode
 63: 
 64: **Behavior**:
 65: - `TenantId` resolved from subdomain or header
 66: - Full tenant management UI visible
 67: - Clear separation between Instance and Tenant Admin
 68: - Tenant-specific routing (e.g., `mosque.app.com`)
 69: 
 70: **Experience**:
 71: - Full SaaS platform capabilities
 72: - Tenant isolation clearly visible
 73: - Self-service or managed onboarding
 74: 
 75: ---
 76: 
 77: ## First-Run Experience
 78: 
 79: ### Single-Tenant Default
 80: 
 81: 1. Application installs with seeded data:
 82:    - `DeploymentMode = Single`
 83:    - `RegistrationPolicy = Closed`
 84:    - Default tenant created
 85: 2. First user visits application
 86: 3. Middleware detects single mode, forces default tenant
 87: 4. User registers as Admin of default tenant
 88: 5. Application feels like standard single-user app
 89: 
 90: ### No Configuration Required
 91: 
 92: The single-tenant first run requires:
 93: - ❌ No tenant creation
 94: - ❌ No subdomain setup
 95: - ❌ No complex configuration
 96: - ✅ Just install and use
 97: 
 98: ---
 99: 
100: ## Runtime Mode Switching
101: 
102: ### Enabling Multi-Tenant
103: 
104: When the deployment grows beyond a single community:
105: 
106: 1. Instance Admin navigates to Settings → Instance
107: 2. Toggles "Deployment Mode" to Multi-Tenant
108: 3. Application clears relevant caches
109: 4. Immediate effects:
110:    - Tenant sidebar menu appears
111:    - "Create Tenant" button visible
112:    - Subdomain routing activates
113:    - Original tenant becomes first of many
114: 
115: ### Switching Back
116: 
117: Multi-tenant → Single-tenant is possible with constraints:
118: - Only one active tenant can exist
119: - Other tenants must be archived/purged
120: - Warning displayed about data implications
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ## Tenant Resolution
125: 
126: ### Single-Tenant Mode
127: 
128: | Mechanism | Behavior |
129: |-----------|----------|
130: | Middleware | Short-circuits, returns `Default` |
131: | Routing | Standard routes, no subdomain |
132: | Context | Always populated with default tenant |
133: 
134: ### Multi-Tenant Mode
135: 
136: | Mechanism | Options |
137: |-----------|---------|
138: | **Subdomain** | `tenant1.app.com` → Tenant1 |
139: | **Header** | `X-Tenant-Id: tenant1` → Tenant1 |
140: | **Path** | `/tenants/tenant1/...` → Tenant1 |
141: | **Claim** | JWT contains tenant ID → Tenant from token |
142: 
143: ### Resolution Priority
144: 
145: 1. Explicit header (highest priority)
146: 2. JWT claim
147: 3. Subdomain
148: 4. Path segment
149: 5. Default tenant (fallback)
150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: ## Configuration Model
154: 
155: ### System Settings
156: 
157: | Setting | Values | Description |
158: |---------|--------|-------------|
159: | `DeploymentMode` | `Single` / `Multi` | Current mode |
160: | `TenantRegistrationPolicy` | `Open` / `InviteOnly` / `Closed` | New tenant policy |
161: | `DefaultTenantId` | Tenant ID | Virtual tenant for single mode |
162: 
163: ### Environment Overrides
164: 
165: For containerized deployments:
166: 
167: | Environment Variable | Purpose |
168: |---------------------|---------|
169: | `DEPLOYMENT_MODE` | Force mode (overrides database) |
170: | `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` | Custom default tenant |
171: | `ALLOW_MODE_SWITCH` | Enable/disable runtime switching |
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: ## Infrastructure Considerations
176: 
177: ### Single-Tenant Infrastructure
178: 
179: | Component | Configuration |
180: |-----------|---------------|
181: | Database | Single schema, single connection string |
182: | DNS | Single domain |
183: | SSL | Single certificate |
184: | Storage | Shared bucket/container |
185: 
186: ### Multi-Tenant Infrastructure
187: 
188: | Component | Configuration |
189: |-----------|---------------|
190: | Database | Shared schema with tenant isolation |
191: | DNS | Wildcard domain (`*.app.com`) or tenant subdomains |
192: | SSL | Wildcard certificate or per-tenant |
193: | Storage | Tenant-prefixed paths or separate containers |
194: 
195: ---
196: 
197: ## Migration Paths
198: 
199: ### Single → Multi (Growth)
200: 
201: **Trigger**: Organization wants to host other communities
202: 
203: **Steps**:
204: 1. Enable multi-tenant mode
205: 2. Configure DNS for subdomains
206: 3. Update SSL certificate (wildcard)
207: 4. Create additional tenants
208: 5. Original tenant continues as-is
209: 
210: ### Multi → Single (Consolidation)
211: 
212: **Trigger**: SaaS shutting down, moving to dedicated
213: 
214: **Steps**:
215: 1. Export target tenant data
216: 2. Archive/purge other tenants
217: 3. Switch to single-tenant mode
218: 4. Remove multi-tenant infrastructure
219: 
220: ---
221: 
222: ## Tenant Registration Policies
223: 
224: ### Registration Flow Options
225: 
226: | Policy | Description | Visible UI |
227: |--------|-------------|------------|
228: | **Open** | Anyone can create tenant | "Start Your Community" button |
229: | **Invite-Only** | Instance Admin sends link | Hidden signup, invite link works |
230: | **Closed** | No new tenants | No signup UI |
231: 
232: ### Policy Use Cases
233: 
234: | Scenario | Recommended Policy |
235: |----------|-------------------|
236: | Public SaaS | Open |
237: | Enterprise SaaS | Invite-Only |
238: | Pilot/Beta | Invite-Only |
239: | Maintenance | Closed |
240: | Single-Tenant | Closed (default) |
241: 
242: ---
243: 
244: ## Related Documentation
245: 
246: - **[MULTI_TENANCY.md](MULTI_TENANCY.md)** - Tenant isolation model
247: - **[ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md](ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md)** - Authority boundaries
248: - **[OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md)** - Deployment procedures
249: - **[CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md)** - Environment setup
250: 
251: ## Implementation Reference
252: 
253: For code patterns:
254: - **`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`** skill - Tenant query filters
255: - **`auth-patterns`** skill - Tenant context middleware
````

## File: docs/EXTENSIBILITY.md
````markdown
  1: # Extensibility Architecture
  2: 
  3: > **Metadata-Driven Modular Design**
  4: >
  5: > This document describes the aspect-based extensibility model that enables deep customization
  6: > without database schema changes or application restarts.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: The platform uses a **Metadata-Driven Aspect Architecture** to handle diverse requirements (cultural, religious, technical) dynamically. This allows:
 15: - Adding new "aspects" to entities without schema changes
 16: - Enabling/disabling features per tenant
 17: - Cultural customization (e.g., Islamic prayer-based scheduling)
 18: - Technical configuration (e.g., render modes, API versioning)
 19: 
 20: ---
 21: 
 22: ## Core Concept: Aspects vs Inheritance
 23: 
 24: ### The Problem with Inheritance
 25: 
 26: Traditional OOP inheritance creates combinatorial explosion:
 27: - `IslamicEvent`, `TechEvent` - 2 types
 28: - `IslamicTechEvent` - need a third?
 29: - Every combination requires a new class
 30: 
 31: ### The Aspect Solution
 32: 
 33: Instead of "Is this an Islamic Event?", ask "Does this Event have Islamic details?"
 34: 
 35: **Key Insight**: An event is a generic container that can "wear" different hats (aspects) simultaneously.
 36: 
 37: | Approach | Flexibility | Schema Changes | Runtime Cost |
 38: |----------|-------------|----------------|--------------|
 39: | Inheritance | Low | Every combination | None |
 40: | Aspects | High | Never | Minimal |
 41: 
 42: ---
 43: 
 44: ## Data Architecture: The Relational Aspect Pattern
 45: 
 46: ### Core Entity Structure
 47: 
 48: Core entities contain only universal properties:
 49: - Identity fields (`Id`, `TenantId`)
 50: - Common properties (`Title`, `CreatedAt`)
 51: - Audit fields (`CreatedBy`, `UpdatedAt`)
 52: 
 53: ### Extension Tables (Aspects)
 54: 
 55: Aspects are optional 1:1 relationships using **shared primary key**:
 56: 
 57: | Table | Purpose | Links To |
 58: |-------|---------|----------|
 59: | `Events` | Core event data | - |
 60: | `EventIslamicDetails` | Islamic-specific attributes | `Events.Id` |
 61: | `EventTechDetails` | Tech-specific attributes | `Events.Id` |
 62: 
 63: **Key Design**: The aspect table's primary key IS also its foreign key to the core entity.
 64: 
 65: ### Composition Example
 66: 
 67: An event that is **both** Islamic and Tech simply has rows in all relevant tables sharing the same ID:
 68: 
 69: | Event #100 | Has Row In |
 70: |------------|------------|
 71: | Core data | `Events` |
 72: | Islamic data | `EventIslamicDetails` |
 73: | Tech data | `EventTechDetails` |
 74: 
 75: ---
 76: 
 77: ## Module Governance Pattern
 78: 
 79: ### Three-Tier Module Availability
 80: 
 81: Modules (sets of aspects and logic) cascade through three levels:
 82: 
 83: | Tier | Scope | Example |
 84: |------|-------|---------|
 85: | **Instance** | What's physically possible | "Server has Islamic + Tech modules" |
 86: | **Tenant** | What's active for this org | "Our mosque only uses Islamic" |
 87: | **Entity** | What's selected for this item | "This event is Islamic-only" |
 88: 
 89: ### Module Visibility Rules
 90: 
 91: A module appears in UI only if:
 92: 1. ✅ Instance Admin has enabled it globally
 93: 2. ✅ Tenant Admin has activated it for their community
 94: 3. ✅ User has permission to use it
 95: 
 96: **Result**: Tenant A (Mosque) never sees "Hackathon" field; Tenant B (Tech Hub) never sees "Madhab" dropdown.
 97: 
 98: ---
 99: 
100: ## Logic Architecture: Request-Scoped Strategies
101: 
102: ### Strategy Selection at Runtime
103: 
104: Business logic adapts per-request without application restart:
105: 
106: 1. **HTTP Request** → User attempts action
107: 2. **Tenant Context** → Middleware identifies tenant
108: 3. **Module Check** → System determines active modules
109: 4. **Strategy Selection** → Resolver returns appropriate implementation
110: 
111: ### Strategy Pattern Examples
112: 
113: | Module | Strategy Interface | Implementation |
114: |--------|-------------------|----------------|
115: | Islamic | `ISchedulingStrategy` | Calculates time based on prayer schedule |
116: | Tech | `ISchedulingStrategy` | Standard datetime scheduling |
117: | Default | `ISchedulingStrategy` | Fallback implementation |
118: 
119: ### Policy Engine
120: 
121: Cross-cutting policies evaluate before operations:
122: - **Submission Policy**: Can this user create this entity type?
123: - **Visibility Policy**: Can this user view this entity?
124: - **Approval Policy**: Does this require moderation?
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## Dynamic Taxonomies
129: 
130: ### User-Defined Metadata
131: 
132: For flexibility beyond compiled modules, use a metadata schema:
133: 
134: | Concept | Purpose |
135: |---------|---------|
136: | **Taxonomy Definition** | Defines a field (name, type, allowed values) |
137: | **Taxonomy Value** | Stores data linked to an entity |
138: 
139: ### When to Use
140: 
141: | Scenario | Use Module? | Use Taxonomy? |
142: |----------|-------------|---------------|
143: | Complex business logic | ✅ | ❌ |
144: | Simple categorization | ❌ | ✅ |
145: | Requires validation | ✅ | ❌ |
146: | User-defined labels | ❌ | ✅ |
147: 
148: ---
149: 
150: ## API Architecture: Polymorphic Responses
151: 
152: ### Discriminated DTOs
153: 
154: API responses include a base DTO plus a list of active aspects:
155: 
156: | Response Field | Purpose |
157: |----------------|---------|
158: | `id`, `title`, etc. | Core entity data |
159: | `aspects[]` | List of active aspect types |
160: | `islamicDetails` | Islamic aspect data (if present) |
161: | `techDetails` | Tech aspect data (if present) |
162: 
163: ### Client-Side Mapping
164: 
165: Frontend dynamically renders components based on aspect presence:
166: 
167: | Aspect Type | Renders Component |
168: |-------------|-------------------|
169: | `Islamic` | Prayer time selector, Madhab dropdown |
170: | `Tech` | GitHub link, hackathon track |
171: | (none) | Generic form only |
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: ## UI Architecture: Dynamic Forms
176: 
177: ### Blueprint-Driven Forms
178: 
179: The API sends form definitions, not hardcoded UIs:
180: 1. Client requests entity creation form
181: 2. Server returns schema based on tenant's active modules
182: 3. Client renders form dynamically
183: 4. Submission includes only relevant aspect data
184: 
185: ### Step Sequencer Pattern
186: 
187: Complex wizards use dynamic step loading:
188: 1. User selects intent ("What type of event?")
189: 2. System fetches module's wizard steps
190: 3. UI loads appropriate components
191: 4. Data saved with module discriminator
192: 
193: ---
194: 
195: ## Module Development Guidelines
196: 
197: ### Adding a New Module
198: 
199: 1. **Define Aspect Table** - Schema for module-specific data
200: 2. **Create Strategy Implementations** - Business logic variations
201: 3. **Register in Module Catalog** - Make discoverable to system
202: 4. **Build UI Components** - Forms, displays, wizards
203: 5. **Document Configuration** - Tenant-facing settings
204: 
205: ### Module Independence
206: 
207: Modules should be:
208: - **Self-contained** - No hard dependencies on other modules
209: - **Gracefully degrading** - Works if dependencies missing
210: - **Tenant-configurable** - Respects tenant settings
211: - **Performance-conscious** - Lazy-loaded when possible
212: 
213: ---
214: 
215: ## Related Documentation
216: 
217: - **[MULTI_TENANCY.md](MULTI_TENANCY.md)** - Tenant isolation model
218: - **[DOMAIN.md](DOMAIN.md)** - Core entity definitions
219: - **[RENDER_POLICIES.md](RENDER_POLICIES.md)** - UI flexibility patterns
220: 
221: ## Implementation Reference
222: 
223: For code patterns and implementation details:
224: - **`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`** skill - Optional 1:1 relationships
225: - **`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`** skill - Handler patterns for aspects
226: - **`blazor-ui-conventions`** skill - Dynamic component rendering
````

## File: docs/FEDERATION.md
````markdown
  1: # Federation
  2: 
  3: ## Status
  4: 
  5: Federation (ATProto / ActivityPub) is a **roadmap feature**.
  6: 
  7: - The domain contains federation-related entities (e.g., `Actor`, `AtprotoRecord`, `SyncState`).
  8: - `Explore.API` does **not** currently expose federation HTTP endpoints (e.g., WebFinger, Inbox/Outbox).
  9: 
 10: ## Protocol Overview
 11: 
 12: This section describes the intended federation model for ISLAMU Event.
 13: 
 14: - **Server-to-Server (S2S)** (planned): Instances exchange activities via inbox/outbox
 15: - **HTTP Signatures** (planned): Cryptographic verification of federated messages
 16: - **WebFinger** (planned): Actor discovery via `/.well-known/webfinger`
 17: - **Collections** (planned): Followers, Following, Liked as ordered collections
 18: 
 19: ## Architecture Philosophy
 20: 
 21: ```
 22: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 23: │                           ISLAMU Event Architecture                          │
 24: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 25: │                                                                             │
 26: │   ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────────────────────┐   │
 27: │   │   Users     │────▶│    PDS      │────▶│    ATProto Network          │   │
 28: │   │  (DIDs)     │     │  (Hosting)  │     │  (Relay/Firehose/AppView)   │   │
 29: │   └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └─────────────────────────────┘   │
 30: │         │                                              │                    │
 31: │         │                                              │                    │
 32: │         ▼                                              ▼                    │
 33: │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
 34: │   │                    ISLAMU Event AppView                              │   │
 35: │   │  • Indexes ngo.islamu.event.* records                               │   │
 36: │   │  • Provides search/discovery APIs                                    │   │
 37: │   │  • Manages cultural/audience filtering                               │   │
 38: │   │  • Hosts ActivityPub Gateway                                         │   │
 39: │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
 40: │                                        │                                    │
 41: │                                        ▼                                    │
 42: │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
 43: │   │               ActivityPub Gateway (Bridge)                           │   │
 44: │   │  • Exposes ATProto events as ActivityPub Event objects              │   │
 45: │   │  • Translates ActivityPub Follow → ATProto follow records           │   │
 46: │   │  • Translates ActivityPub RSVP → ATProto participation records      │   │
 47: │   │  • Would provide WebFinger, Actor endpoints, Inbox/Outbox (planned) │   │
 48: │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
 49: │                                        │                                    │
 50: │                                        ▼                                    │
 51: │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
 52: │   │                      Fediverse                                       │   │
 53: │   │              (Mastodon, Mobilizon, Pleroma, etc.)                   │   │
 54: │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
 55: │                                                                             │
 56: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 57: ```
 58: 
 59: ## Event Data Flow
 60: 
 61: ```
 62: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 63: │                        Event Data Flow                                       │
 64: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 65: │                                                                             │
 66: │  ATProto/ActivityPub Federation                    ISLAMU Event WebApp      │
 67: │  ─────────────────────────────────                 ───────────────────      │
 68: │                                                                             │
 69: │  ┌─────────────────────────────┐                  ┌─────────────────────┐   │
 70: │  │  Federated Event Record     │                  │  Full Event Detail  │   │
 71: │  │  ─────────────────────────  │                  │  ─────────────────  │   │
 72: │  │  • Title                    │                  │  • All event info   │   │
 73: │  │  • Summary/Description      │    Link to       │  • Session 1        │   │
 74: │  │  • Start Date (first)       │ ──────────────▶  │    - Time, Location │   │
 75: │  │  • Location (primary)       │                  │    - Agenda         │   │
 76: │  │  • Cover Image              │                  │    - Speakers       │   │
 77: │  │  • URL → webapp             │                  │  • Session 2        │   │
 78: │  │  • Basic audience info      │                  │    - Time, Location │   │
 79: │  └─────────────────────────────┘                  │    - Agenda         │   │
 80: │                                                    │  • Session N...     │   │
 81: │  What Mastodon/Bluesky users see:                 │  • Registration     │   │
 82: │  "🗓️ Community Iftar 2025                         │  • Comments         │   │
 83: │   March 15-17, Amsterdam                          │  • Participants     │   │
 84: │   Join us for 3 days of..."                       └─────────────────────┘   │
 85: │   [View Event →]                                                            │
 86: │                                                                             │
 87: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 88: ```
 89: 
 90: ## CID
 91: ```
 92: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 93: │                          How CID Works                                       │
 94: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 95: │                                                                             │
 96: │  1. User creates event record                                               │
 97: │     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐                                     │
 98: │     │ {                               │                                     │
 99: │     │   "$type": "ngo.islamu.event...",│                                    │
100: │     │   "title": "Community Iftar",   │                                     │
101: │     │   "startsAt": "2025-03-15...",  │                                     │
102: │     │   ...                           │                                     │
103: │     │ }                               │                                     │
104: │     └─────────────────────────────────┘                                     │
105: │                    │                                                        │
106: │                    ▼                                                        │
107: │  2. PDS serializes to DAG-CBOR (deterministic binary format)               │
108: │                    │                                                        │
109: │                    ▼                                                        │
110: │  3. PDS computes SHA-256 hash → CID                                        │
111: │     ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
112: │     │ bafyreigxyz123... (base32 encoded multihash)                │        │
113: │     └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
114: │                    │                                                        │
115: │  4. CID is included in the repo commit (signed by user's key)              │
116: │                                                                             │
117: │  WHY THIS MATTERS:                                                          │
118: │  ─────────────────                                                          │
119: │  • Anyone can verify the record hasn't been tampered with                  │
120: │  • If content changes → CID changes → old references become invalid        │
121: │  • Enables "strong references" (URI + CID = exact version)                 │
122: │                                                                             │
123: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
124: ```
125: 
126: ## Identity system Hybrid Approach
127: Support BOTH Keycloak (traditional) AND ATProto OAuth, with custodial DIDs for Keycloak users:
128: 
129: ```
130: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
131: │                    Hybrid Auth Architecture                                  │
132: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
133: │                                                                             │
134: │                      ┌─────────────────┐                                    │
135: │                      │   Login Page    │                                    │
136: │                      └────────┬────────┘                                    │
137: │                               │                                             │
138: │              ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐                            │
139: │              ▼                                 ▼                            │
140: │    ┌──────────────────┐              ┌──────────────────┐                  │
141: │    │ Login with Email │              │ Login with ATProto│                  │
142: │    │   (Keycloak)     │              │ (Bring your DID)  │                  │
143: │    └────────┬─────────┘              └────────┬─────────┘                  │
144: │             │                                  │                            │
145: │             ▼                                  ▼                            │
146: │    ┌──────────────────┐              ┌──────────────────┐                  │
147: │    │ Keycloak returns │              │ ATProto OAuth    │                  │
148: │    │ UUID + email     │              │ returns DID      │                  │
149: │    └────────┬─────────┘              └────────┬─────────┘                  │
150: │             │                                  │                            │
151: │             ▼                                  ▼                            │
152: │    ┌──────────────────┐              ┌──────────────────┐                  │
153: │    │ Create custodial │              │ Link existing    │                  │
154: │    │ DID for user     │              │ DID to account   │                  │
155: │    └────────┬─────────┘              └────────┬─────────┘                  │
156: │             │                                  │                            │
157: │             └────────────────┬─────────────────┘                            │
158: │                              ▼                                              │
159: │                    ┌──────────────────┐                                     │
160: │                    │  user + actor    │                                     │
161: │                    │  records created │                                     │
162: │                    └──────────────────┘                                     │
163: │                                                                             │
164: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
165: ```
166: 
167: ## Handling Nullable DID (did_status)
168: 
169: The key insight is that DID creation is **async**. Here's how to handle it:
170: ```
171: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
172: │                    DID Status State Machine                                  │
173: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
174: │                                                                             │
175: │  ┌─────────┐     Background job      ┌─────────┐                           │
176: │  │ pending │ ──────────────────────▶ │ active  │                           │
177: │  └─────────┘     creates DID         └─────────┘                           │
178: │       │                                                                     │
179: │       │ DID creation fails                                                  │
180: │       ▼                                                                     │
181: │  ┌─────────┐     Retry succeeds      ┌─────────┐                           │
182: │  │ failed  │ ──────────────────────▶ │ active  │                           │
183: │  └─────────┘                         └─────────┘                           │
184: │                                                                             │
185: │  WHAT USERS CAN DO:                                                         │
186: │  ──────────────────                                                         │
187: │  pending → Browse, edit profile (read-heavy)                                │
188: │  failed  → Same as pending, show "retry" button                            │
189: │  active  → Full access: post events, comment, etc. (write access)          │
190: │                                                                             │
191: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
192: ```
````

## File: docs/MODULAR_EVENTS.md
````markdown
  1: # Modular Event Architecture
  2: 
  3: > **Cultural and Domain-Specific Event Customization**
  4: >
  5: > This document describes how the platform supports deep customization for different
  6: > cultural, religious, and domain-specific event types through the aspect pattern.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: Events are the core aggregate of the platform. Rather than using inheritance to handle different event types (Islamic, Tech, Educational, etc.), the platform uses a **composition-based aspect pattern** that allows:
 15: 
 16: - Any event to have multiple "aspects" simultaneously
 17: - Cultural customization without schema changes
 18: - Domain-specific fields added per tenant
 19: - Graceful degradation when aspects are unavailable
 20: 
 21: ---
 22: 
 23: ## The Aspect Pattern for Events
 24: 
 25: ### Core Event vs Aspects
 26: 
 27: | Component | Contains | Example |
 28: |-----------|----------|---------|
 29: | **Core Event** | Universal properties | Title, date, organization, status |
 30: | **Islamic Aspect** | Religious customization | Madhab, prayer time offset, gender segregation |
 31: | **Tech Aspect** | Technical events | GitHub repo, hackathon track |
 32: | **Educational Aspect** | Learning events | Certification, prerequisites |
 33: 
 34: ### Why Not Inheritance?
 35: 
 36: | Scenario | Inheritance Approach | Aspect Approach |
 37: |----------|---------------------|-----------------|
 38: | Islamic Conference | `IslamicEvent` class | Event + Islamic aspect |
 39: | Tech Hackathon | `TechEvent` class | Event + Tech aspect |
 40: | Islamic Tech Conference | `IslamicTechEvent` class? | Event + Islamic aspect + Tech aspect |
 41: | 5 event types | 31 possible classes | 5 aspect tables |
 42: 
 43: **Aspect pattern scales linearly; inheritance scales exponentially.**
 44: 
 45: ---
 46: 
 47: ## Islamic Event Customization
 48: 
 49: ### Islamic-Specific Attributes
 50: 
 51: | Attribute | Purpose | Values |
 52: |-----------|---------|--------|
 53: | **Madhab** | Jurisprudence school | Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali, Mixed |
 54: | **Prayer Time Offset** | Schedule relative to prayer | Minutes before/after Fajr, Dhuhr, etc. |
 55: | **Gender Segregation** | Attendance policy | Men-only, Women-only, Segregated, Mixed |
 56: | **Language Mode** | Primary language | Arabic, English, Urdu, etc. |
 57: 
 58: ### Prayer-Based Scheduling
 59: 
 60: Instead of absolute times, events can be scheduled relative to prayer times:
 61: 
 62: | Scheduling Mode | Description |
 63: |-----------------|-------------|
 64: | **Absolute** | Standard datetime (default) |
 65: | **After Prayer** | X minutes after specified prayer |
 66: | **Before Prayer** | X minutes before specified prayer |
 67: | **Between Prayers** | Between two specified prayers |
 68: 
 69: **Benefit**: Same event "30 minutes after Maghrib" automatically adjusts for different locations and dates.
 70: 
 71: ### Gender Segregation Modes
 72: 
 73: | Mode | Description | Facility Requirements |
 74: |------|-------------|----------------------|
 75: | **Men Only** | Restricted to men | Single section |
 76: | **Women Only** | Restricted to women | Single section |
 77: | **Segregated** | Both attend, separate areas | Dual sections, barriers |
 78: | **Family** | Families together, singles separate | Family + singles sections |
 79: | **Mixed** | No segregation | Open seating |
 80: 
 81: ---
 82: 
 83: ## Tech Event Customization
 84: 
 85: ### Tech-Specific Attributes
 86: 
 87: | Attribute | Purpose | Example |
 88: |-----------|---------|---------|
 89: | **Repository URL** | Code repository link | GitHub, GitLab URL |
 90: | **Hackathon Track** | Competition category | AI, Web, Mobile |
 91: | **Skill Level** | Required expertise | Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced |
 92: | **Stack Tags** | Technologies used | .NET, React, Python |
 93: 
 94: ---
 95: 
 96: ## Event Type Resolution
 97: 
 98: ### Determining Active Aspects
 99: 
100: When loading an event:
101: 
102: 1. **Core data** always loaded
103: 2. **Aspect presence** determined by existence of aspect record
104: 3. **UI components** rendered based on present aspects
105: 4. **Validation** applies aspect-specific rules
106: 
107: ### API Response Structure
108: 
109: Events include metadata about active aspects:
110: 
111: | Field | Purpose |
112: |-------|---------|
113: | `id`, `title`, etc. | Core event data |
114: | `aspects[]` | List of active aspect identifiers |
115: | `islamicDetails` | Islamic aspect data (if present) |
116: | `techDetails` | Tech aspect data (if present) |
117: 
118: ---
119: 
120: ## Module-Based Aspect Availability
121: 
122: ### Tenant Configuration
123: 
124: Tenants enable aspects through module configuration:
125: 
126: | Tenant Type | Enabled Modules | Available Aspects |
127: |-------------|-----------------|-------------------|
128: | Mosque | Core, Islamic | Basic + Islamic |
129: | Tech Community | Core, Tech | Basic + Tech |
130: | University | Core, Islamic, Educational | Basic + Islamic + Educational |
131: 
132: ### Aspect Visibility
133: 
134: Aspects appear in UI only when:
135: 1. ✅ Module enabled at instance level
136: 2. ✅ Module activated for tenant
137: 3. ✅ User has permission to use it
138: 
139: **Result**: A tech community never sees "Madhab" dropdown; a mosque never sees "GitHub Repo" field.
140: 
141: ---
142: 
143: ## Creating Events with Aspects
144: 
145: ### Event Creation Flow
146: 
147: 1. **Select Intent** → "What type of event?" (filters by tenant's modules)
148: 2. **Core Details** → Title, description, organization
149: 3. **Aspect Details** → Dynamic forms based on selected aspects
150: 4. **Review & Publish** → Validation across all aspects
151: 
152: ### Dynamic Form Generation
153: 
154: The API returns form schema based on active aspects:
155: 
156: | Request | Response |
157: |---------|----------|
158: | `GET /api/events/schema` | Core fields only |
159: | `GET /api/events/schema?aspects=islamic` | Core + Islamic fields |
160: | `GET /api/events/schema?aspects=islamic,tech` | Core + Islamic + Tech fields |
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## Validation Across Aspects
165: 
166: ### Aspect-Specific Validation
167: 
168: Each aspect can contribute validation rules:
169: 
170: | Aspect | Validation Rule | Example |
171: |--------|-----------------|---------|
172: | Islamic | Prayer time must be valid | Can't schedule during Jumah prayer |
173: | Tech | Repository URL must be accessible | GitHub URL returns 200 |
174: | Educational | Prerequisites must exist | Referenced courses must exist |
175: 
176: ### Cross-Aspect Validation
177: 
178: Some validations span multiple aspects:
179: 
180: | Rule | Aspects Involved |
181: |------|------------------|
182: | "Women-only tech workshop" | Islamic (gender) + Tech (track) |
183: | "Prayer break during hackathon" | Islamic (prayer) + Tech (hackathon) |
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## Querying Events by Aspect
188: 
189: ### Filtered Queries
190: 
191: Events can be queried by aspect presence:
192: 
193: | Query | Returns |
194: |-------|---------|
195: | All events | Events regardless of aspects |
196: | Islamic events | Events with Islamic aspect |
197: | Tech events | Events with Tech aspect |
198: | Islamic tech events | Events with both aspects |
199: 
200: ### Aspect-Specific Filters
201: 
202: Within an aspect, specific filters apply:
203: 
204: | Filter | Aspect | Example |
205: |--------|--------|---------|
206: | By Madhab | Islamic | "Hanafi events only" |
207: | By Gender | Islamic | "Women-only events" |
208: | By Track | Tech | "AI hackathon events" |
209: | By Stack | Tech | ".NET events" |
210: 
211: ---
212: 
213: ## Extending with New Aspects
214: 
215: ### Adding a New Aspect
216: 
217: To add a new event aspect (e.g., "Medical"):
218: 
219: 1. **Define Aspect Table** → `EventMedicalDetails` with medical-specific fields
220: 2. **Create Module** → Package aspect with logic and UI
221: 3. **Register** → Add to module catalog
222: 4. **Enable** → Instance/tenant can activate
223: 
224: ### Aspect Independence
225: 
226: Aspects should be:
227: - **Self-contained** → No dependencies on other aspects
228: - **Gracefully optional** → Events work without any aspects
229: - **Backward compatible** → New aspects don't break existing events
230: 
231: ---
232: 
233: ## Related Documentation
234: 
235: - **[EXTENSIBILITY.md](EXTENSIBILITY.md)** - General aspect architecture
236: - **[MULTI_TENANCY.md](MULTI_TENANCY.md)** - Tenant module configuration
237: - **[DOMAIN.md](DOMAIN.md)** - Entity relationships
238: 
239: ## Implementation Reference
240: 
241: For code patterns:
242: - **`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`** skill - Optional 1:1 relationships
243: - **`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`** skill - Handler patterns for aspects
````

## File: docs/MULTI_TENANCY.md
````markdown
  1: # Multi-Tenancy Architecture
  2: 
  3: > **Conceptual Guide for Multi-Tenant System Design**
  4: >
  5: > This document describes the multi-tenancy model, authority hierarchy, and data isolation patterns.
  6: > For implementation details and code patterns, see the relevant skills in `.claude/skills/`.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: The platform operates as a **multi-tenant system** where multiple independent organizations (tenants) share the same application infrastructure while maintaining complete data isolation. The architecture supports both dedicated single-tenant deployments and shared multi-tenant SaaS models.
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## Hierarchy of Authority
 19: 
 20: ### Two-Tier Administration Model
 21: 
 22: The system distinguishes between two fundamentally different administrative roles:
 23: 
 24: | Tier | Role | Scope | Typical Use Case |
 25: |------|------|-------|------------------|
 26: | **Tier 1** | Instance Administrator | Infrastructure, global policies, module enablement | SaaS provider, IT department |
 27: | **Tier 2** | Tenant Administrator | Community data, local configuration, user management | Organization leader, community admin |
 28: 
 29: ### Instance Administrator (Super Admin)
 30: 
 31: **Responsibilities:**
 32: - Physical server and infrastructure management
 33: - Global resource limits and quotas
 34: - Module enablement/disablement at platform level
 35: - Enforcement policies that cannot be overridden
 36: - Tenant provisioning and lifecycle management
 37: - System-wide security policies
 38: 
 39: **Cannot Do:**
 40: - Access tenant-specific business data
 41: - Make decisions on behalf of tenants
 42: - Override tenant preferences within allowed bounds
 43: 
 44: ### Tenant Administrator (Customer)
 45: 
 46: **Responsibilities:**
 47: - Community-specific configuration
 48: - User management within their tenant
 49: - Branding and customization
 50: - Local business rules and workflows
 51: - Content moderation policies
 52: 
 53: **Constrained By:**
 54: - Instance-level enforcement policies
 55: - Module availability set by Instance Admin
 56: - Resource quotas and limits
 57: 
 58: ---
 59: 
 60: ## Cascading Configuration Engine
 61: 
 62: ### Resolution Strategy
 63: 
 64: Settings are resolved at runtime using a **fall-through strategy**:
 65: 
 66: 1. **Check Tenant Override** → Does the tenant have a specific value?
 67: 2. **Check Instance Enforcement** → Is this setting locked by the Instance Admin?
 68: 3. **Fall to Default** → Use the system default value
 69: 
 70: ### Setting Types
 71: 
 72: | Type | Behavior | Example |
 73: |------|----------|---------|
 74: | **Locked** | Tenant cannot override | Security policies, payment provider |
 75: | **Delegated** | Tenant may customize | Theme colors, notification preferences |
 76: | **Default-Only** | System default, no UI exposed | Internal technical settings |
 77: 
 78: ### Enforcement Scenarios
 79: 
 80: **Scenario: Render Mode Control**
 81: - Instance Admin sets `RenderMode = Auto` with `IsLocked = false`
 82: - Tenant Admin sees a dropdown and can change to `Server` or `WebAssembly`
 83: - If Instance Admin sets `IsLocked = true`, dropdown is disabled/hidden
 84: 
 85: **Scenario: Module Restriction**
 86: - Instance Admin configures `AllowedModules = ["Core", "Islamic"]`
 87: - Tenant Admin cannot enable "Tech" module even if code exists
 88: - Tenant only sees modules within their allowed set
 89: 
 90: ---
 91: 
 92: ## Data Isolation
 93: 
 94: ### Tenant Boundary Enforcement
 95: 
 96: Every tenant-scoped entity implements `ITenantEntity`:
 97: - Contains `TenantId` property
 98: - Automatically filtered in all queries via global query filters
 99: - Cannot be accidentally accessed across tenant boundaries
100: 
101: ### Isolation Guarantees
102: 
103: | Layer | Mechanism |
104: |-------|-----------|
105: | **Database** | Global query filters on `TenantId` |
106: | **Application** | Tenant context injected per-request |
107: | **API** | Middleware validates tenant claims |
108: | **UI** | Routes scoped to tenant context |
109: 
110: ### Cross-Tenant Operations
111: 
112: Cross-tenant operations are **explicitly forbidden** except:
113: - Instance Admin reporting and analytics
114: - System-wide notifications (opt-in)
115: - Federation sync (ATProto/ActivityPub)
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Tenant Lifecycle
120: 
121: ### Provisioning Flow
122: 
123: 1. **Request** → Tenant Admin requests new tenant (or Instance Admin creates)
124: 2. **Validation** → Check quotas, naming conflicts, policy compliance
125: 3. **Creation** → Database schema initialized with tenant seed data
126: 4. **Configuration** → Module selection, initial settings
127: 5. **Activation** → Tenant becomes operational
128: 
129: ### Tenant States
130: 
131: | State | Description | Operations Allowed |
132: |-------|-------------|-------------------|
133: | **Pending** | Created but not activated | Configuration only |
134: | **Active** | Fully operational | All operations |
135: | **Suspended** | Temporarily disabled | Read-only access |
136: | **Archived** | Soft-deleted | None (data retained) |
137: | **Purged** | Permanently deleted | None (data removed) |
138: 
139: ---
140: 
141: ## Single-Tenant vs Multi-Tenant Deployment
142: 
143: ### Virtual Tenant Strategy
144: 
145: The codebase is **always multi-tenant internally** to avoid maintaining separate codebases. Single-tenant mode is achieved through a "Virtual Tenant" that masks the complexity.
146: 
147: | Mode | Behavior |
148: |------|----------|
149: | **Single-Tenant** | `TenantId` hardcoded to `Default`; tenant management UI hidden |
150: | **Multi-Tenant** | `TenantId` resolved from subdomain/header; full tenant management |
151: 
152: ### Runtime Mode Switching
153: 
154: The deployment mode can be changed at runtime without application restart:
155: 1. Instance Admin toggles setting in dashboard
156: 2. Database updated, cache invalidated
157: 3. Next request uses new mode
158: 4. UI adapts automatically (tenant menu appears/disappears)
159: 
160: ---
161: 
162: ## Onboarding Patterns
163: 
164: ### Instance Admin First-Run
165: 
166: When the platform is first installed:
167: 1. First user becomes Instance Admin
168: 2. Wizard asks deployment purpose (Dedicated vs. SaaS)
169: 3. Module selection for the instance
170: 4. Default tenant configuration
171: 
172: ### Tenant Registration Policies
173: 
174: | Policy | Description |
175: |--------|-------------|
176: | **Open** | Self-service registration via public form |
177: | **Invite-Only** | Instance Admin sends invitation link |
178: | **Sales-Gated** | Request must be approved by sales team |
179: | **Closed** | No new tenants (maintenance mode) |
180: 
181: ---
182: 
183: ## Related Documentation
184: 
185: - **[ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md](ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md)** - Detailed authority model
186: - **[DEPLOYMENT_MODES.md](DEPLOYMENT_MODES.md)** - Single vs multi-tenant deployment
187: - **[EXTENSIBILITY.md](EXTENSIBILITY.md)** - Module and aspect architecture
188: - **[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)** - Overall system architecture
189: 
190: ## Implementation Reference
191: 
192: For code patterns and implementation details:
193: - **`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`** skill - Tenant query filters
194: - **`auth-patterns`** skill - Tenant context extraction
195: - **`clean-architecture-rules`** skill - Layer boundaries
````

## File: docs/PROJECT.md
````markdown
  1: ## 1. Project Overview
  2: 
  3: ## What is ISLAMU Event?
  4: 
  5: **ISLAMU Event** (also known as ISLAMU Explore or Event Explorer) is an **open-source event discovery platform**.
  6: 
  7: The long-term vision includes **ATProto-first federation** with an **ActivityPub gateway**, but HTTP federation endpoints are **not currently implemented** in `Explore.API`.
  8: 
  9: ## Core Value Proposition
 10: 
 11: | Component | Value |
 12:   |-----------|-------|
 13: | **Software** | Multi-tenant federated event platform (AGPL) |
 14: | **Primary Instance** | Trusted Islamic event directory with verification |
 15: | **Filtering System** | Culturally-appropriate discovery (age, gender, madhab) |
 16: 
 17: ## Organizational Context
 18: 
 19: - **Organization**: ISLAMU Non Profit Organization (Islamic Software Lighthouse Alliance of the Muslim Ummah)
 20: - **Legal Entity**: Belgian non-profit organization ASBL (Association sans but lucratif)
 21: - **GitHub Organization**: `islamu-ngo`
 22: - **Repository**: `https://github.com/islamu-ngo/explore`
 23: - **License**: AGPL-3.0
 24: 
 25: ---
 26: 
 27: # Strategic Context
 28: 
 29: ## Ecosystem Architecture
 30: 
 31: ```
 32: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 33: │                      ISLAMU Event Ecosystem                         │
 34: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 35: │                                                                     │
 36: │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
 37: │  │           ISLAMU-Hosted Instance (Primary Focus)            │   │
 38: │  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │   │
 39: │  │  • Islamic events globally                                  │   │
 40: │  │  • Verified actors (fact-checked)                           │   │
 41: │  │  • User-submitted events (flagged as unverified)            │   │
 42: │  │  • Strike/ban system for policy violations                  │   │
 43: │  │  • Advanced filtering (age, gender, location, language, and more)│   │
 44: │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
 45: │                              │                                      │
 46: │                    ActivityPub Federation                           │
 47: │                              │                                      │
 48: │  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐              │
 49: │  │ Community A  │  │ Community B  │  │ Organization │  ...         │
 50: │  │ Instance     │  │ Instance     │  │ Instance     │              │
 51: │  │ (3rd party)  │  │ (3rd party)  │  │ (3rd party)  │              │
 52: │  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘              │
 53: │         │                  │                  │                     │
 54: │         └──────────────────┴──────────────────┘                     │

 56: │                    (Revenue share with ISLAMU)                      │
 57: │                                                                     │

 60: 
 61: ## Architecture Philosophy
 62: 
 63: ```
 64: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 66: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

 69: │   │   Users     │────▶│    PDS      │────▶│    ATProto Network          │   │

100: 
101: # Core Features
102: 
103: ## Two-Tier Verification System
104: 
105: ```
106: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
107: │                    VERIFICATION SYSTEM                              │
108: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
109: │                                                                     │
110: │  TIER 1: User-Submitted Events                                      │
111: │  ├── Anyone can create account                                      │
112: │  ├── Can post events immediately                                    │
113: │  ├── Events marked as "User Reported"                               │
114: │  ├── Subject to community moderation                                │
115: │  └── Strike/ban system for violations                               │
116: │                                                                     │
117: │  TIER 2: Verified Organizations                                     │
118: │  ├── Application required                                           │
119: │  └── Fact-checking process:                                         │
120: │      └── Organization exists? (registration check)                  │
121: │                                                                     │
122: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
123: ```
124: 
125: ## Advanced Filtering System
126: 
127: | Filter | Options | Description |
128: |--------|---------|-------------|
129: | **Audience Age** | Children, Youth, Adults, Seniors, All Ages | Target demographic |
130: | **Gender** | Men-only, Women-only, Mixed, Family | Audience type |
131: | **Location** | Country, Region, City, Radius | Geographic filtering with PostGIS |
132: | **Language** | Arabic, English, French, etc. | Event language |
133: | **Event Type** | Webinar, Conference | Event Type |
134: | **Madhab** | Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali | Islamic jurisprudence school |
135: | **Category** | Aqidah, Fiqh, Tafsir, Hadith, etc. | Event classification |
136: | **Tag** | Mohammed Hijab, Mufti Menk etc... | Event tags |
137: | **TagType** | Person, Channel, oeuvres | Tag classification |
138: | **TagTypeTags** | Specific tags within TagType | e.g., Person → Mohammed Hijab |
139: | **Event Format** | In-person Local (physical), Digital (online), Hybrid | Event format |
140: | **Date/Time** | Upcoming, This Week, This Month, Custom | Temporal filtering |
141: | **Verification** | Verified only, All | Trust level |
142: 
143: ## Liturgical Temporal Engine
144: 
145: **Dynamic Prayer-Relative Scheduling**:
146: 
147: - Events can be scheduled relative to prayer times (e.g., "15 minutes after Maghrib")
148: - exact times based on event geolocation using Third-party API
149: 
150: ## Moderation System
151: 
152: Still todo
153: 
154: ## Data Portability
155: 
156: Export formats supported:
157: - **iCal/ICS**: Standard calendar format for events
158: - **CSV**: Attendee lists, organizations, bulk data
159: - **ActivityPub-native** (planned): Federation-compatible JSON-LD
160: - **Full database dump**: Complete data export for self-hosters
161: 
162: ---
