## File: Explore.Infrastructure/Services/ModuleService.cs
````csharp
  1: namespace Explore.Infrastructure.Services;
  2: 
  3: using Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory;
  4: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;
  5: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
  6: using Explore.Domain.Modules;
  7: 
  8: 
  9: 
 10: 
 11: public class ModuleService : IModuleService
 12: {
 13:     private readonly IModuleDefinitionRepository _moduleDefinitionRepository;
 14:     private readonly ITenantCapabilityRepository _tenantCapabilityRepository;
 15:     private readonly IMemoryCache _cache;
 16:     private readonly TimeSpan _cacheExpiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);
 17: 
 18:     private const string AllModulesCacheKey = "Modules_All";
 19:     private const string TenantModulesCacheKeyPrefix = "Modules_Tenant_";
 20: 
 21:     public ModuleService(
 22:         IModuleDefinitionRepository moduleDefinitionRepository,
 23:         ITenantCapabilityRepository tenantCapabilityRepository,
 24:         IMemoryCache cache)
 25:     {
 26:         _moduleDefinitionRepository = moduleDefinitionRepository;
 27:         _tenantCapabilityRepository = tenantCapabilityRepository;
 28:         _cache = cache;
 29:     }
 30: 
 31:     public async Task<IReadOnlyList<ModuleInfo>> GetAllModulesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 32:     {
 33:         return await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(AllModulesCacheKey, async entry =>
 34:         {
 35:             entry.AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow = _cacheExpiration;
 36:             var modules = await _moduleDefinitionRepository.GetAllActive();
 37:             return modules.Select(m => MapToModuleInfo(m)).ToList();
 38:         }) ?? new List<ModuleInfo>();
 39:     }
 40: 
 41:     public async Task<IReadOnlyList<ModuleInfo>> GetEnabledModulesAsync(Guid tenantId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 42:     {
 43:         var cacheKey = $"{TenantModulesCacheKeyPrefix}{tenantId}";
 44: 
 45:         return await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(cacheKey, async entry =>
 46:         {
 47:             entry.AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow = _cacheExpiration;
 48: 
 49:             var capabilities = await _tenantCapabilityRepository.GetEnabledByTenantId(tenantId);
 50:             return capabilities
 51:                 .Where(c => c.Module != null)
 52:                 .Select(c => MapToModuleInfo(c.Module!, isEnabledForTenant: true))
 53:                 .ToList();
 54:         }) ?? new List<ModuleInfo>();
 55:     }
 56: 
 57:     public async Task<bool> IsModuleEnabledAsync(Guid tenantId, string moduleKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 58:     {
 59: 
 60:         var enabledModules = await GetEnabledModulesAsync(tenantId, cancellationToken);
 61:         return enabledModules.Any(m => m.ModuleKey.Equals(moduleKey, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     public async Task<string?> GetModuleWizardSchemaUrlAsync(string moduleKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 65:     {
 66:         var module = await _moduleDefinitionRepository.GetByKey(moduleKey);
 67:         return module?.WizardSchemaUrl;
 68:     }
 69: 
 70:     public async Task<bool> EnableModuleAsync(Guid tenantId, string moduleKey, Guid? enabledBy = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 71:     {
 72: 
 73:         var module = await _moduleDefinitionRepository.GetByKey(moduleKey);
 74:         if (module == null || !module.IsActive)
 75:             return false;
 76: 
 77: 
 78:         var existing = await _tenantCapabilityRepository.GetByTenantAndModuleKey(tenantId, moduleKey);
 79:         if (existing != null)
 80:         {
 81: 
 82:             if (!existing.IsEnabled)
 83:             {
 84:                 existing.IsEnabled = true;
 85:                 existing.EnabledAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
 86:                 existing.EnabledBy = enabledBy;
 87:                 await _tenantCapabilityRepository.Update(existing);
 88:                 InvalidateCache(tenantId);
 89:             }
 90:             return true;
 91:         }
 92: 
 93: 
 94:         var capability = new TenantCapability
 95:         {
 96:             TenantId = tenantId,
 97:             ModuleId = module.Id,
 98:             IsEnabled = true,
 99:             EnabledAt = DateTime.UtcNow,
100:             EnabledBy = enabledBy
101:         };
102: 
103:         await _tenantCapabilityRepository.Create(capability);
104:         InvalidateCache(tenantId);
105:         return true;
106:     }
107: 
108:     public async Task<bool> DisableModuleAsync(Guid tenantId, string moduleKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
109:     {
110:         var capability = await _tenantCapabilityRepository.GetByTenantAndModuleKey(tenantId, moduleKey);
111:         if (capability == null)
112:             return false;
113: 
114: 
115:         capability.IsEnabled = false;
116:         await _tenantCapabilityRepository.Update(capability);
117:         InvalidateCache(tenantId);
118:         return true;
119:     }
120: 
121:     public void InvalidateCache(Guid? tenantId = null)
122:     {
123:         _cache.Remove(AllModulesCacheKey);
124: 
125:         if (tenantId.HasValue)
126:         {
127:             _cache.Remove($"{TenantModulesCacheKeyPrefix}{tenantId}");
128:         }
129:     }
130: 
131:     private static ModuleInfo MapToModuleInfo(ModuleDefinition module, bool? isEnabledForTenant = null)
132:     {
133:         return new ModuleInfo
134:         {
135:             Id = module.Id,
136:             ModuleKey = module.ModuleKey,
137:             Name = module.Name,
138:             Description = module.Description,
139:             IconName = module.IconName,
140:             Category = module.Category,
141:             DisplayOrder = module.DisplayOrder,
142:             WizardSchemaUrl = module.WizardSchemaUrl,
143:             IsActive = module.IsActive,
144:             IsEnabledForTenant = isEnabledForTenant
145:         };
146:     }
147: }
````

## File: Explore.Infrastructure/Services/SettingsResolver.cs
````csharp
  1: namespace Explore.Infrastructure.Services;
  2: 
  3: using System.Text.Json;
  4: using Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory;
  5: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;
  6: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
  7: using Explore.Domain;
  8: 
  9: 
 10: 
 11: 
 12: public class SettingsResolver : ISettingsResolver
 13: {
 14:     private readonly ISystemSettingRepository _systemSettingRepository;
 15:     private readonly ITenantSettingRepository _tenantSettingRepository;
 16:     private readonly IMemoryCache _cache;
 17:     private readonly TimeSpan _cacheExpiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);
 18: 
 19:     private const string SystemSettingsCacheKey = "SystemSettings_All";
 20:     private const string TenantSettingsCacheKeyPrefix = "TenantSettings_";
 21: 
 22:     public SettingsResolver(
 23:         ISystemSettingRepository systemSettingRepository,
 24:         ITenantSettingRepository tenantSettingRepository,
 25:         IMemoryCache cache)
 26:     {
 27:         _systemSettingRepository = systemSettingRepository;
 28:         _tenantSettingRepository = tenantSettingRepository;
 29:         _cache = cache;
 30:     }
 31: 
 32:     public async Task<T?> GetSettingAsync<T>(string settingKey, Guid? tenantId = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 33:     {
 34:         var resolved = await GetSettingWithMetadataAsync(settingKey, tenantId, cancellationToken);
 35:         if (resolved == null)
 36:             return default;
 37: 
 38:         try
 39:         {
 40:             return JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>(resolved.Value);
 41:         }
 42:         catch
 43:         {
 44:             return default;
 45:         }
 46:     }
 47: 
 48:     public async Task<ResolvedSetting?> GetSettingWithMetadataAsync(string settingKey, Guid? tenantId = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 49:     {
 50: 
 51:         var systemSettings = await GetSystemSettingsAsync(cancellationToken);
 52:         var systemSetting = systemSettings.FirstOrDefault(s => s.SettingKey == settingKey);
 53: 
 54:         if (systemSetting == null)
 55:             return null;
 56: 
 57: 
 58:         if (systemSetting.IsLocked || tenantId == null)
 59:         {
 60:             return new ResolvedSetting
 61:             {
 62:                 Key = systemSetting.SettingKey,
 63:                 Value = systemSetting.Value,
 64:                 ValueType = systemSetting.ValueType,
 65:                 Source = systemSetting.IsLocked ? SettingSource.SystemLocked : SettingSource.SystemDefault,
 66:                 IsLocked = systemSetting.IsLocked,
 67:                 Description = systemSetting.Description,
 68:                 Category = systemSetting.Category,
 69:                 AllowedValues = systemSetting.AllowedValues
 70:             };
 71:         }
 72: 
 73: 
 74:         var tenantSettings = await GetTenantSettingsAsync(tenantId.Value, cancellationToken);
 75:         var tenantOverride = tenantSettings.FirstOrDefault(s => s.SettingKey == settingKey);
 76: 
 77:         if (tenantOverride != null)
 78:         {
 79:             return new ResolvedSetting
 80:             {
 81:                 Key = settingKey,
 82:                 Value = tenantOverride.Value,
 83:                 ValueType = systemSetting.ValueType,
 84:                 Source = SettingSource.TenantOverride,
 85:                 IsLocked = false,
 86:                 Description = systemSetting.Description,
 87:                 Category = systemSetting.Category,
 88:                 AllowedValues = systemSetting.AllowedValues
 89:             };
 90:         }
 91: 
 92: 
 93:         return new ResolvedSetting
 94:         {
 95:             Key = systemSetting.SettingKey,
 96:             Value = systemSetting.Value,
 97:             ValueType = systemSetting.ValueType,
 98:             Source = SettingSource.SystemDefault,
 99:             IsLocked = false,
100:             Description = systemSetting.Description,
101:             Category = systemSetting.Category,
102:             AllowedValues = systemSetting.AllowedValues
103:         };
104:     }
105: 
106:     public async Task<IReadOnlyList<ResolvedSetting>> GetAllSettingsAsync(Guid? tenantId = null, string? category = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
107:     {
108:         var systemSettings = await GetSystemSettingsAsync(cancellationToken);
109:         var tenantSettings = tenantId.HasValue
110:             ? await GetTenantSettingsAsync(tenantId.Value, cancellationToken)
111:             : new List<TenantSetting>();
112: 
113:         var tenantSettingsDict = tenantSettings.ToDictionary(s => s.SettingKey, s => s.Value);
114: 
115:         var result = systemSettings
116:             .Where(s => category == null || s.Category == category)
117:             .Select(s =>
118:             {
119:                 var hasOverride = tenantSettingsDict.TryGetValue(s.SettingKey, out var overrideValue);
120:                 var effectiveValue = s.IsLocked || !hasOverride ? s.Value : overrideValue!;
121:                 var source = s.IsLocked ? SettingSource.SystemLocked
122:                     : hasOverride ? SettingSource.TenantOverride
123:                     : SettingSource.SystemDefault;
124: 
125:                 return new ResolvedSetting
126:                 {
127:                     Key = s.SettingKey,
128:                     Value = effectiveValue,
129:                     ValueType = s.ValueType,
130:                     Source = source,
131:                     IsLocked = s.IsLocked,
132:                     Description = s.Description,
133:                     Category = s.Category,
134:                     AllowedValues = s.AllowedValues
135:                 };
136:             })
137:             .ToList();
138: 
139:         return result;
140:     }
141: 
142:     public async Task<bool> CanOverrideAsync(string settingKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
143:     {
144:         return !await _systemSettingRepository.IsLocked(settingKey);
145:     }
146: 
147:     public async Task<bool> SetTenantOverrideAsync(string settingKey, object value, Guid tenantId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
148:     {
149: 
150:         if (!await CanOverrideAsync(settingKey, cancellationToken))
151:             return false;
152: 
153:         var existingOverride = await _tenantSettingRepository.GetByTenantAndKey(tenantId, settingKey);
154:         var jsonValue = JsonSerializer.Serialize(value);
155: 
156:         if (existingOverride != null)
157:         {
158:             existingOverride.Value = jsonValue;
159:             existingOverride.UpdatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
160:             await _tenantSettingRepository.Update(existingOverride);
161:         }
162:         else
163:         {
164:             var newOverride = new TenantSetting
165:             {
166:                 TenantId = tenantId,
167:                 SettingKey = settingKey,
168:                 Value = jsonValue,
169:                 CreatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow
170:             };
171:             await _tenantSettingRepository.Create(newOverride);
172:         }
173: 
174:         InvalidateCache(settingKey, tenantId);
175:         return true;
176:     }
177: 
178:     public async Task<bool> RemoveTenantOverrideAsync(string settingKey, Guid tenantId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
179:     {
180:         var result = await _tenantSettingRepository.RemoveOverride(tenantId, settingKey);
181:         if (result)
182:         {
183:             InvalidateCache(settingKey, tenantId);
184:         }
185:         return result;
186:     }
187: 
188:     public void InvalidateCache(string? settingKey = null, Guid? tenantId = null)
189:     {
190:         if (settingKey == null && tenantId == null)
191:         {
192:             _cache.Remove(SystemSettingsCacheKey);
193:         }
194:         else if (tenantId.HasValue)
195:         {
196:             _cache.Remove($"{TenantSettingsCacheKeyPrefix}{tenantId}");
197:         }
198:         else
199:         {
200:             _cache.Remove(SystemSettingsCacheKey);
201:         }
202:     }
203: 
204:     private async Task<List<SystemSetting>> GetSystemSettingsAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
205:     {
206:         return await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(SystemSettingsCacheKey, async entry =>
207:         {
208:             entry.AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow = _cacheExpiration;
209:             return await _systemSettingRepository.GetAllSettings();
210:         }) ?? new List<SystemSetting>();
211:     }
212: 
213:     private async Task<List<TenantSetting>> GetTenantSettingsAsync(Guid tenantId, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
214:     {
215:         var cacheKey = $"{TenantSettingsCacheKeyPrefix}{tenantId}";
216:         return await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(cacheKey, async entry =>
217:         {
218:             entry.AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow = _cacheExpiration;
219:             return await _tenantSettingRepository.GetAllForTenant(tenantId);
220:         }) ?? new List<TenantSetting>();
221:     }
222: }
````

## File: Explore.Infrastructure/Strategies/StrategyResolver.cs
````csharp
  1: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;
  2: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Strategies;
  3: using Explore.Application.DTOs.Event;
  4: using Explore.Domain;
  5: using FluentValidation.Results;
  6: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
  7: 
  8: namespace Explore.Infrastructure.Strategies;
  9: 
 10: 
 11: 
 12: 
 13: public class StrategyResolver : IStrategyResolver
 14: {
 15:     private readonly IEnumerable<IEventStrategy> _strategies;
 16:     private readonly IModuleService _moduleService;
 17:     private readonly ILogger<StrategyResolver> _logger;
 18: 
 19:     public StrategyResolver(
 20:         IEnumerable<IEventStrategy> strategies,
 21:         IModuleService moduleService,
 22:         ILogger<StrategyResolver> logger)
 23:     {
 24:         _strategies = strategies;
 25:         _moduleService = moduleService;
 26:         _logger = logger;
 27:     }
 28: 
 29:     public async Task<IReadOnlyList<IEventStrategy>> GetApplicableStrategiesAsync(
 30:         Guid tenantId,
 31:         CreateEventDto dto,
 32:         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 33:     {
 34:         var applicableStrategies = new List<IEventStrategy>();
 35: 
 36:         foreach (var strategy in _strategies)
 37:         {
 38: 
 39:             var isModuleEnabled = await _moduleService.IsModuleEnabledAsync(
 40:                 tenantId, strategy.ModuleKey, cancellationToken);
 41: 
 42:             if (!isModuleEnabled)
 43:             {
 44:                 _logger.LogDebug(
 45:                     "Strategy {StrategyKey} skipped - module not enabled for tenant {TenantId}",
 46:                     strategy.ModuleKey, tenantId);
 47:                 continue;
 48:             }
 49: 
 50: 
 51:             if (strategy.IsApplicable(dto))
 52:             {
 53:                 applicableStrategies.Add(strategy);
 54:                 _logger.LogDebug(
 55:                     "Strategy {StrategyKey} is applicable for event",
 56:                     strategy.ModuleKey);
 57:             }
 58:         }
 59: 
 60: 
 61:         return applicableStrategies
 62:             .OrderBy(s => s.Priority)
 63:             .ToList();
 64:     }
 65: 
 66:     public async Task<ValidationResult> ValidateWithStrategiesAsync(
 67:         Guid tenantId,
 68:         CreateEventDto dto,
 69:         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 70:     {
 71:         var result = new ValidationResult();
 72:         var strategies = await GetApplicableStrategiesAsync(tenantId, dto, cancellationToken);
 73: 
 74:         foreach (var strategy in strategies)
 75:         {
 76:             try
 77:             {
 78:                 var strategyResult = await strategy.ValidateAsync(dto, cancellationToken);
 79:                 if (!strategyResult.IsValid)
 80:                 {
 81:                     result.Errors.AddRange(strategyResult.Errors);
 82:                     _logger.LogDebug(
 83:                         "Strategy {StrategyKey} validation failed with {ErrorCount} errors",
 84:                         strategy.ModuleKey, strategyResult.Errors.Count);
 85:                 }
 86:             }
 87:             catch (Exception ex)
 88:             {
 89:                 _logger.LogError(ex,
 90:                     "Error validating with strategy {StrategyKey}",
 91:                     strategy.ModuleKey);
 92: 
 93:                 result.Errors.Add(new ValidationFailure(
 94:                     strategy.ModuleKey,
 95:                     $"Strategy validation error: {ex.Message}"));
 96:             }
 97:         }
 98: 
 99:         return result;
100:     }
101: 
102:     public async Task ExecutePostCreateAsync(
103:         Guid tenantId,
104:         Event @event,
105:         CreateEventDto dto,
106:         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
107:     {
108:         var strategies = await GetApplicableStrategiesAsync(tenantId, dto, cancellationToken);
109: 
110:         foreach (var strategy in strategies)
111:         {
112:             try
113:             {
114:                 await strategy.PostCreateAsync(@event, cancellationToken);
115:                 _logger.LogDebug(
116:                     "Strategy {StrategyKey} post-create completed for event {EventId}",
117:                     strategy.ModuleKey, @event.Id);
118:             }
119:             catch (Exception ex)
120:             {
121: 
122:                 _logger.LogError(ex,
123:                     "Error executing post-create for strategy {StrategyKey} on event {EventId}",
124:                     strategy.ModuleKey, @event.Id);
125:             }
126:         }
127:     }
128: 
129:     public async Task ExecutePostUpdateAsync(
130:         Guid tenantId,
131:         Event @event,
132:         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
133:     {
134: 
135:         var enabledModules = await _moduleService.GetEnabledModulesAsync(tenantId, cancellationToken);
136:         var enabledModuleKeys = enabledModules.Select(m => m.ModuleKey).ToHashSet();
137: 
138:         foreach (var strategy in _strategies.Where(s => enabledModuleKeys.Contains(s.ModuleKey)))
139:         {
140: 
141:             var isApplicable = strategy.ModuleKey switch
142:             {
143:                 "Mod_Islamic" => @event.IslamicAspect != null,
144:                 "Mod_Tech" => @event.TechAspect != null,
145:                 _ => false
146:             };
147: 
148:             if (!isApplicable) continue;
149: 
150:             try
151:             {
152:                 await strategy.PostUpdateAsync(@event, cancellationToken);
153:                 _logger.LogDebug(
154:                     "Strategy {StrategyKey} post-update completed for event {EventId}",
155:                     strategy.ModuleKey, @event.Id);
156:             }
157:             catch (Exception ex)
158:             {
159:                 _logger.LogError(ex,
160:                     "Error executing post-update for strategy {StrategyKey} on event {EventId}",
161:                     strategy.ModuleKey, @event.Id);
162:             }
163:         }
164:     }
165: 
166:     public async Task<IReadOnlyList<StrategyLink>> GetStrategyLinksAsync(
167:         Guid tenantId,
168:         Event @event,
169:         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
170:     {
171:         var links = new List<StrategyLink>();
172:         var enabledModules = await _moduleService.GetEnabledModulesAsync(tenantId, cancellationToken);
173:         var enabledModuleKeys = enabledModules.Select(m => m.ModuleKey).ToHashSet();
174: 
175:         foreach (var strategy in _strategies.Where(s => enabledModuleKeys.Contains(s.ModuleKey)))
176:         {
177:             try
178:             {
179:                 var strategyLinks = strategy.GetLinks(@event);
180:                 links.AddRange(strategyLinks);
181:             }
182:             catch (Exception ex)
183:             {
184:                 _logger.LogError(ex,
185:                     "Error getting links from strategy {StrategyKey} for event {EventId}",
186:                     strategy.ModuleKey, @event.Id);
187:             }
188:         }
189: 
190:         return links;
191:     }
192: }
````

  1: namespace Explore.Persistence.Repositories;

  6: 
  7: public class AppSettingRepository : IAppSettingRepository
  8: {
  9:     private readonly ExploreDbContext _dbContext;
 10: 
 11:     public AppSettingRepository(ExploreDbContext dbContext)
 12:     {
 13:         _dbContext = dbContext;
 14:     }
 15: 
 16:     public async Task<AppSetting?> GetByKeyAsync(string configKey)
 17:     {
 18:         return await _dbContext.AppSettings
 19:             .AsNoTracking()
 20:             .FirstOrDefaultAsync(s => s.ConfigKey == configKey);
 21:     }
 22: 
 23:     public async Task<List<AppSetting>> GetByCategoryAsync(string? category = null)
 24:     {
 25:         var query = _dbContext.AppSettings.AsNoTracking();
 26: 
 27:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(category))
 28:         {
 29:             query = query.Where(s => s.Category == category);
 30:         }
 31: 
 32:         return await query
 33:             .OrderBy(s => s.Category)
 34:             .ThenBy(s => s.ConfigKey)
 35:             .ToListAsync();
 36:     }
 37: 
 38:     public async Task<List<AppSetting>> GetSettingsNeedingReEncryptionAsync(int currentKeyVersion)
 39:     {
 40:         return await _dbContext.AppSettings
 41:             .AsNoTracking()
 42:             .Where(s => s.KeyVersion < currentKeyVersion)
 43:             .OrderBy(s => s.ConfigKey)
 44:             .ToListAsync();
 45:     }
 46: 
 47:     public async Task<List<AppSetting>> GetAllAsync()
 48:     {
 49:         return await _dbContext.AppSettings
 50:             .AsNoTracking()
 51:             .OrderBy(s => s.ConfigKey)
 52:             .ToListAsync();
 53:     }
 54: 
 55:     public async Task<AppSetting> CreateAsync(AppSetting setting)
 56:     {
 57:         await _dbContext.AppSettings.AddAsync(setting);
 58:         await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 59:         return setting;
 60:     }
 61: 
 62:     public async Task UpdateAsync(AppSetting setting)
 63:     {
 64: 
 65:         _dbContext.AppSettings.Update(setting);
 66:         await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 67:     }
 68: 
 69:     public async Task<bool> DeleteAsync(string configKey)
 70:     {
 71:         var setting = await _dbContext.AppSettings.FirstOrDefaultAsync(s => s.ConfigKey == configKey);
 72:         if (setting == null)
 73:         {
 74:             return false;
 75:         }
 76: 
 77:         _dbContext.AppSettings.Remove(setting);
 78:         await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 79:         return true;
 80:     }
 81: 
 82:     public async Task<bool> ExistsAsync(string configKey)
 83:     {
 84:         return await _dbContext.AppSettings.AnyAsync(s => s.ConfigKey == configKey);
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     public async Task BulkUpdateAsync(IEnumerable<AppSetting> settings)
 88:     {
 89:         await using var transaction = await _dbContext.Database.BeginTransactionAsync();
 90:         try
 91:         {
 92:             foreach (var setting in settings)
 93:             {
 94:                 _dbContext.AppSettings.Update(setting);
 95:             }
 96:             await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 97:             await transaction.CommitAsync();

103:         }

 53:         if (await context.Tenants.AnyAsync(t => t.Id == SeedIds.DefaultTenantId, cancellationToken))
 54:         {
 55:             return;
 56:         }
 57: 
 58: 
 59:         await SeedTenantsAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 60:         await SeedUsersAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 61:         await SeedOrganizationsAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 62:         await SeedActorsAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 63:         await SeedOrganizationMembersAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 64:         await SeedStorageObjectsAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 65:         await SeedTenantSettingsAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 66:         await SeedTenantCapabilitiesAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 67:         await SeedLocationsAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 68:         await SeedCategoriesAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 69:         await SeedTagsAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 70:         await SeedUserRolesAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 71:         await SeedSampleEventsAsync(context, cancellationToken);
 72: 
 73:         await context.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
 74:     }

````csharp
  1: using System.Text.Json;
  2: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder;
  3: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.HealthChecks;
  4: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;
  5: using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
  6: using Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks;
  7: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
  8: using Microsoft.Extensions.ServiceDiscovery;
  9: using OpenTelemetry;
 10: using OpenTelemetry.Metrics;
 11: using OpenTelemetry.Trace;
 12: 
 13: namespace Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting;
 14: 
 15: 
 16: 
 17: 
 18: public static class Extensions
 19: {
 20:     private const string HealthEndpointPath = "/health";
 21:     private const string AlivenessEndpointPath = "/alive";
 22: 
 23:     public static TBuilder AddServiceDefaults<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder) where TBuilder : IHostApplicationBuilder
 24:     {
 25:         builder.ConfigureOpenTelemetry();
 26: 
 27:         builder.AddDefaultHealthChecks();
 28: 
 29:         builder.Services.AddServiceDiscovery();
 30: 
 31:         builder.Services.ConfigureHttpClientDefaults(http =>
 32:         {
 33: 
 34:             http.AddStandardResilienceHandler();
 35: 
 36: 
 37:             http.AddServiceDiscovery();
 38:         });
 39: 
 40: 
 41: 
 42: 
 43: 
 44: 
 45: 
 46:         return builder;
 47:     }
 48: 
 49:     public static TBuilder ConfigureOpenTelemetry<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder) where TBuilder : IHostApplicationBuilder
 50:     {
 51:         builder.Logging.AddOpenTelemetry(logging =>
 52:         {
 53:             logging.IncludeFormattedMessage = true;
 54:             logging.IncludeScopes = true;
 55:         });
 56: 
 57:         builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
 58:             .WithMetrics(metrics =>
 59:             {
 60:                 metrics.AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()
 61:                     .AddHttpClientInstrumentation()
 62:                     .AddRuntimeInstrumentation();
 63:             })
 64:             .WithTracing(tracing =>
 65:             {
 66:                 tracing.AddSource(builder.Environment.ApplicationName)
 67:                     .AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation(tracing =>
 68: 
 69:                         tracing.Filter = context =>
 70:                             !context.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments(HealthEndpointPath)
 71:                             && !context.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments(AlivenessEndpointPath)
 72:                     )
 73: 
 74: 
 75:                     .AddHttpClientInstrumentation();
 76:             });
 77: 
 78:         builder.AddOpenTelemetryExporters();
 79: 
 80:         return builder;
 81:     }
 82: 
 83:     private static TBuilder AddOpenTelemetryExporters<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder) where TBuilder : IHostApplicationBuilder
 84:     {
 85:         var useOtlpExporter = !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(builder.Configuration["OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT"]);
 86: 
 87:         if (useOtlpExporter)
 88:         {
 89:             builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry().UseOtlpExporter();
 90:         }
 91: 
 92: 
 93: 
 94: 
 95: 
 96: 
 97: 
 98: 
 99:         return builder;
100:     }
101: 
102:     public static TBuilder AddDefaultHealthChecks<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder) where TBuilder : IHostApplicationBuilder
103:     {
104:         builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()
105: 
106:             .AddCheck("self", () => HealthCheckResult.Healthy(), ["live"]);
107: 
108:         return builder;
109:     }
110: 
111:     public static WebApplication MapDefaultEndpoints(this WebApplication app)
112:     {
113: 
114: 
115: 
116: 
117:         var healthCheckOptions = new HealthCheckOptions
118:         {
119:             ResponseWriter = WriteHealthCheckResponse,
120:             ResultStatusCodes =
121:             {
122:                 [HealthStatus.Healthy] = StatusCodes.Status200OK,
123:                 [HealthStatus.Degraded] = StatusCodes.Status200OK,
124:                 [HealthStatus.Unhealthy] = StatusCodes.Status503ServiceUnavailable
125:             }
126:         };
127: 
128: 
129:         app.MapHealthChecks(HealthEndpointPath, healthCheckOptions);
130: 
131: 
132:         app.MapHealthChecks(AlivenessEndpointPath, new HealthCheckOptions
133:         {
134:             Predicate = r => r.Tags.Contains("live"),
135:             ResponseWriter = WriteHealthCheckResponse,
136:             ResultStatusCodes =
137:             {
138:                 [HealthStatus.Healthy] = StatusCodes.Status200OK,
139:                 [HealthStatus.Degraded] = StatusCodes.Status200OK,
140:                 [HealthStatus.Unhealthy] = StatusCodes.Status503ServiceUnavailable
141:             }
142:         });
143: 
144:         return app;
145:     }
146: 
147:     private static async Task WriteHealthCheckResponse(HttpContext context, HealthReport report)
148:     {
149: 
150:         context.Response.ContentType = "application/json; charset=utf-8";
151:         context.Response.Headers["Connection"] = "close";
152:         context.Response.Headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"] = "*";
153:         context.Response.Headers["X-Health-Status"] = report.Status.ToString();
154:         context.Response.Headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate";
155:         context.Response.Headers["Pragma"] = "no-cache";
156: 
157:         var response = new
158:         {
159:             status = report.Status.ToString(),
160:             message = report.Status switch
161:             {
162:                 HealthStatus.Healthy => "Ok",
163:                 HealthStatus.Degraded => "Degraded",
164:                 HealthStatus.Unhealthy => "Service Unavailable",
165:                 _ => "Unknown"
166:             },
167:             totalDuration = report.TotalDuration.TotalMilliseconds,
168:             checks = report.Entries.Select(e => new
169:             {
170:                 name = e.Key,
171:                 status = e.Value.Status.ToString(),
172:                 description = e.Value.Description,
173:                 duration = e.Value.Duration.TotalMilliseconds,
174:                 error = e.Value.Exception?.Message,
175:                 data = e.Value.Data.Count > 0 ? e.Value.Data : null
176:             })
177:         };
178: 
179:         var jsonOptions = new JsonSerializerOptions
180:         {
181:             WriteIndented = true,
182:             PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase,
183:             DefaultIgnoreCondition = System.Text.Json.Serialization.JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull
184:         };
185: 
186:         await context.Response.WriteAsync(JsonSerializer.Serialize(response, jsonOptions));
187:     }
188: }
````

````markdown
  1: # Technical Architecture
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic .NET Clean Architecture Guide**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## Placeholder Substitutions
 12: 
 13: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 14: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 15: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 16: | `{Project}.Domain` | Domain layer project | `Explore.Domain` |
 17: | `{Project}.Application` | Application layer project | `Explore.Application` |
 18: | `{Project}.Persistence` | Persistence layer project | `Explore.Persistence` |
 19: | `{Project}.Infrastructure` | Infrastructure layer project | `Explore.Infrastructure` |
 20: | `{Project}.API` | API project | `Explore.API` |
 21: | `{Project}.Blazor` | Blazor Server project | `Explore.Blazor` |
 22: | `{Project}.Blazor.Client` | Blazor WASM project | `Explore.Blazor.Client` |
 23: | `{Project}.AppHost` | Aspire AppHost project | `Explore.AppHost` |
 24: | `{DbContext}` | EF Core DbContext class | `ExploreDbContext` |
 25: | `{IdType}` | Primary key type | `Guid` |
 26: 
 27: ---
 28: 
 29: ## 1. Technology Stack
 30: 
 31: | Layer | Technology | Purpose |
 32: |-------|------------|---------|
 33: | **Runtime** | .NET 10.0 | Primary framework |
 34: | **Orchestration** | .NET Aspire | Service orchestration, observability |
 35: | **Web UI** | Blazor (Server + WebAssembly) | Hybrid rendering model |
 36: | **UI Components** | MudBlazor | Material Design components |
 37: | **Database** | PostgreSQL + PostGIS | Primary datastore with spatial queries |
 38: | **ORM** | Entity Framework Core | Data access layer |
 39: | **Authentication** | Keycloak | OIDC/JWT identity provider |
 40: | **Authorization** | ASP.NET Core Authorization | `[Authorize]` attributes and resource-based logic |
 41: | **Secrets** | Infisical | Secrets management |
 42: | **Logging** | Serilog | Structured logging |
 43: | **Telemetry** | OpenTelemetry | Distributed tracing and metrics |
 44: | **API Docs** | Scalar + Swagger | OpenAPI documentation |
 45: | **Federation** | ATProto / ActivityPub (Planned) | Domain model exists; federation endpoints are not yet implemented. |
 46: 
 47: ## 2. Architectural Paradigm: Clean Architecture + CQRS
 48: 
 49: The project is built upon **Clean Architecture** principles to ensure a separation of concerns, testability, and maintainability. It uses **Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)** to separate read and write operations within the application layer.
 50: 
 51: ### Layer Dependencies
 52: 
 53: Dependencies must only flow inwards. The domain layer has no dependencies on any other layer.
 54: 
 55: **Generic Structure:**
 56: - **Presentation Layer**: `{Project}.API`, `{Project}.Blazor`
 57: - **Application Layer**: `{Project}.Application`
 58: - **Domain Layer**: `{Project}.Domain`
 59: - **Infrastructure Layer**: `{Project}.Persistence`, `{Project}.Infrastructure`
 60: 
 61: **Diagram (Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event):**
 62: 
 63: ```mermaid
 64: graph TD
 65:     subgraph Presentation Layer
 66:         A[Explore.API]
 67:         B[Explore.Blazor]
 68:     end
 69: 
 70:     subgraph Application Layer
 71:         C[Explore.Application]
 72:     end
 73: 
 74:     subgraph Domain Layer
 75:         D[Explore.Domain]
 76:     end
 77: 
 78:     subgraph Infrastructure Layer
 79:         E[Explore.Persistence]
 80:         F[Explore.Infrastructure]
 81:     end
 82: 
 83:     A --> C
 84:     B --> C
 85:     C --> D
 86:     E --> C
 87:     F --> C
 88: ```
 89: 
 90: *Substitute "Explore" with your `{Project}` name.*
 91: 
 92: **Layer Responsibilities:**
 93: 
 94: -   **Domain**: Contains pure business logic, entities, and value objects. It is the core of the application and has no external dependencies.
 95: -   **Application**: Orchestrates the domain logic. It contains use cases (commands/queries), DTOs, and interfaces for infrastructure services. It depends only on the Domain layer.
 96: -   **Infrastructure**: Provides concrete implementations for data access with repository pattern (Persistence via `{Project}.Persistence`) and external services (email, file storage via `{Project}.Infrastructure`). It depends on the Application layer to implement its interfaces.
 97: -   **Presentation**: The entry points to the application, including the REST API (`{Project}.API`) and the Blazor UI (`{Project}.Blazor`). This layer composes the other layers and handles user interaction and HTTP requests.
 98: 
 99: ### Data Flow (CQRS Pattern)
100: 
101: The CQRS pattern is implemented using the **MediatR** library.
102: 
103: **Generic Flow:**
104: 1. Client sends HTTP request to `{Entity}Controller`
105: 2. Controller sends command/query to MediatR
106: 3. MediatR routes to appropriate handler
107: 4. Handler interacts with repository
108: 5. Response flows back through the chain
109: 
110: **Sequence Diagram:**
111: 
112: ```mermaid
113: sequenceDiagram
114:     participant Client
115:     participant Controller
116:     participant MediatR
117:     participant Handler
118:     participant Repository
119: 
120:     Client->>Controller: HTTP Request (e.g., POST /api/v1/{entity})
121:     Controller->>MediatR: `_mediator.Send(command)`
122:     MediatR->>Handler: `Handle(command)`
123:     Handler->>Repository: `_repository.Create(entity)`
124:     Repository-->>Handler: Returns updated entity
125:     Handler-->>MediatR: Returns `BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>`
126:     MediatR-->>Controller: Returns response
127:     Controller-->>Client: HTTP Response (e.g., 200 OK)
128: ```
129: 
130: *Replace `{entity}` with your resource name (e.g., `event`, `order`, `product`) and `{IdType}` with your ID type (`Guid`, `int`).*
131: 
132: *For detailed implementation guidance, see the `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` skill.*
133: 
134: ## 3. Frontend Architecture: Blazor Hybrid with BFF
135: 
136: The frontend is a **Blazor Hybrid** application that uses the **Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)** pattern for security and performance.
137: 
138: ### Rendering Mode: InteractiveAuto
139: 
140: The application uses the `InteractiveAuto` render mode by default.
141: 
142: 1.  **Fast Initial Load**: The first visit renders pages on the **server** via a SignalR connection, providing immediate content to the user.
143: 2.  **Background Download**: The Blazor **WebAssembly** runtime and application DLLs are downloaded in the background.
144: 3.  **Seamless Transition**: Once the WASM assets are cached, the application transitions to client-side rendering, offloading work from the server and enabling potential offline capabilities.
145: 
146: ### BFF Security Model
147: 
148: The `{Project}.Blazor` project acts as a security gateway for the `{Project}.Blazor.Client` frontend.
149: 
150: **Architecture Flow:**
151: 
152: ```mermaid
153: graph LR
154:     A[Browser / WASM] -- Cookie --> B[BFF / Blazor Server]
155:     B -- OIDC Redirect --> C[OIDC Provider]
156:     B -- YARP Proxy --> D[Backend API]
157:     D -- JWT Auth --> D
158: ```
159: 
160: **Security Layers:**
161: 
162: -   The **BFF** (`{Project}.Blazor`) handles the OIDC authentication flow with your identity provider (e.g., Keycloak) and maintains the user session in a secure, `HttpOnly` cookie.
163: -   The **WASM Client** (`{Project}.Blazor.Client`) is "dumb" regarding authentication; it simply sends the cookie with each request to the BFF.
164: -   The **BFF** uses **YARP** as a reverse proxy. When a request for `/api/v1/...` arrives, it reads the access token from the session cookie and forwards the request to the `{Project}.API` backend with a `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
165: -   This architecture ensures **no tokens are ever exposed to the browser**.
166: 
167: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
168: 
169: - **BFF**: `Explore.Blazor` (Blazor Server)
170: - **WASM Client**: `Explore.Blazor.Client`
171: - **Backend API**: `Explore.API`
172: - **OIDC Provider**: Keycloak
173: 
174: *For detailed implementation guidance, see the `blazor-bff-patterns` and `auth-patterns` skills.*
175: 
176: ## 4. API Architecture
177: 
178: The `{Project}.API` project is a standard ASP.NET Core REST API following Clean Architecture principles.
179: 
180: ### Key Conventions
181: 
182: -   **Stateless**: The API is stateless and relies solely on the provided JWT for authentication and authorization.
183: -   **Thin Controllers**: Controllers are minimal. Their only job is to receive an HTTP request, send a command or query to MediatR, and return an appropriate HTTP response.
184: -   **Authorization**: Write endpoints (`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) are protected with `[Authorize]`. Read endpoints (`GET`) are public with `[AllowAnonymous]`.
185: -   **Documentation**: Endpoints are documented using `[EndpointSummary]`, `[EndpointDescription]`, and `[ProducesResponseType]` attributes for OpenAPI generation.
186: 
187: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
188: 
189: - **API Project**: `Explore.API`
190: - **Base URL**: `https://localhost:7001/api/v1`
191: 
192: *For detailed implementation guidance, see `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` skill.*
193: 
194: ## 5. Project Structure
195: 
196: The solution is organized into projects that directly map to the layers of Clean Architecture.
197: 
198: ### Generic Template
199: 
200: ```
201: {Project}.sln
202: ├── {Project}.Domain/              # Domain layer: Entities, Enums, Value Objects
203: ├── {Project}.Application/         # Application layer: CQRS handlers, DTOs, Interfaces
204: ├── {Project}.Persistence/         # Infrastructure: EF Core DbContext, Repositories
205: ├── {Project}.Infrastructure/      # Infrastructure: External services (email, storage, etc.)
206: ├── {Project}.API/                 # Presentation: REST API
207: ├── {Project}.Blazor/              # Presentation: Blazor Server (BFF)
208: ├── {Project}.Blazor.Client/       # Presentation: Blazor WebAssembly (UI)
209: ├── {Project}.AppHost/             # .NET Aspire Orchestrator
210: └── {Project}.ServiceDefaults/     # Shared Aspire configuration (observability, resilience)
211: ├── tests/
212: │   ├── {Project}.Application.UnitTests/
213: │   ├── {Project}.Domain.UnitTests/
214: │   └── {Project}.API.IntegrationTests/
215: └── docs/
216:     └── ... (Architecture documentation, guides)
217: ```
218: 
219: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
220: 
221: ```
222: Explore.sln
223: ├── Explore.Domain/              # Domain layer: Event, Organization, User entities
224: ├── Explore.Application/         # Application layer: Event handlers, DTOs
225: ├── Explore.Persistence/         # Infrastructure: ExploreDbContext, Repositories
226: ├── Explore.Infrastructure/      # Infrastructure: Email, file storage services
227: ├── Explore.API/                 # Presentation: REST API
228: ├── Explore.Blazor/              # Presentation: Blazor Server (BFF)
229: ├── Explore.Blazor.Client/       # Presentation: Blazor WebAssembly (UI)
230: ├── Explore.AppHost/             # .NET Aspire Orchestrator
231: └── Explore.ServiceDefaults/     # Shared Aspire configuration
232: ├── tests/
233: │   ├── Event.Application.UnitTests/
234: │   └── ... (other test projects)
235: └── docs/
236:     └── ... (High-level documentation)
237: ```
238: 
239: *Substitute `{Project}` with your solution name (e.g., `OrderSystem`, `InventoryApp`, `HRPortal`).*
````

````markdown
  1: # Configuration
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Configuration Guide**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ## Placeholder Substitutions
  8: 
  9: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 10: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 11: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 12: | `{project}` | Lowercase project name | `explore` |
 13: | `{Project}.API` | API project name | `Explore.API` |
 14: | `{Instance Name}` | Your instance display name | `ISLAMU Event` |
 15: | `{Instance Domain}` | Your instance domain | `events.islamu.org` |
 16: 
 17: ---
 18: 
 19: ## Application Settings
 20: 
 21: **Generic Template:**
 22: ```json
 23: {
 24:   "Keycloak": {
 25:     "Authority": "https://your-keycloak-instance.com/realms/{realm}",
 26:     "Realm": "your-realm",
 27:     "ClientId": "{project}-api",
 28:     "ClientSecret": ""
 29:   },
 30:   "ConnectionStrings": {
 31:     "DefaultConnection": ""
 32:   },
 33:   "Federation": {
 34:     "InstanceDomain": "{Instance Domain}",
 35:     "InstanceName": "{Instance Name}",
 36:     "EnableFederation": true,
 37:     "SharedInboxEnabled": true
 38:   },
 39:   "Serilog": {
 40:     "MinimumLevel": {
 41:       "Default": "Information",
 42:       "Override": {
 43:         "Microsoft": "Warning",
 44:         "System": "Warning"
 45:       }
 46:     },
 47:     "WriteTo": [
 48:       { "Name": "Console" },
 49:       { "Name": "File", "Args": { "path": "logs/log-.txt", "rollingInterval": "Day" } },
 50:       { "Name": "Seq", "Args": { "serverUrl": "http://localhost:5341" } }
 51:     ]
 52:   }
 53: }
 54: ```
 55: 
 56: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 57: ```json
 58: {
 59:   "Keycloak": {
 60:     "Authority": "https://keycloak.openislamu.org/realms/islamu-dev",
 61:     "Realm": "islamu-dev",
 62:     "ClientId": "explore-api",
 63:     "ClientSecret": ""
 64:   },
 65:   "Federation": {
 66:     "InstanceDomain": "events.islamu.org",
 67:     "InstanceName": "ISLAMU Event",
 68:     "EnableFederation": true,
 69:     "SharedInboxEnabled": true
 70:   }
 71: }
 72: ```
 73: 
 74: ## Environment Variables
 75: 
 76: | Variable | Description | Example |
 77: |----------|-------------|---------|
 78: | `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` | Runtime environment | `Development`, `Staging`, `Production` |
 79: | `ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection` | PostgreSQL connection | `Host=...;Database=...` |
 80: | `Keycloak__ClientSecret` | Keycloak client secret | `...` |
 81: | `Infisical__ClientId` | Secrets manager client | `...` |
 82: | `Infisical__ClientSecret` | Secrets manager secret | `...` |
 83: 
 84: ## Secret Management
 85: 
 86: The application uses a unified secret management system (`Explore.Secrets`) that supports multiple providers:
 87: 
 88: ### Secret Providers
 89: 
 90: | Provider | Use Case | Configuration |
 91: |----------|----------|---------------|
 92: | `none` | Self-hosters, local dev | Use environment variables directly |
 93: | `infisical` | Production with Infisical | Connects to Infisical service |
 94: 
 95: ### Configuration Options
 96: 
 97: ```json
 98: {
 99:   "SecretProvider": {
100:     "Provider": "infisical",
101:     "FailFast": true
102:   },
103:   "Infisical": {
104:     "Url": "https://app.infisical.com",
105:     "ProjectId": "your-project-id",
106:     "ClientId": "your-client-id",
107:     "ClientSecret": "your-client-secret",
108:     "Environment": "dev"
109:   },
110:   "SecretRefresh": {
111:     "RefreshInterval": "00:05:00",
112:     "BaseBackoffDelay": "00:00:30",
113:     "MaxBackoffDelay": "00:05:00"
114:   }
115: }
116: ```
117: 
118: ### Environment Variables
119: 
120: | Variable | Description | Required |
121: |----------|-------------|----------|
122: | `SECRET_PROVIDER` | Provider type: `none` or `infisical` | No (default: `none`) |
123: | `Infisical__Url` | Infisical server URL | Only if using Infisical |
124: | `Infisical__ProjectId` | Infisical project ID | Only if using Infisical |
125: | `Infisical__ClientId` | Universal Auth client ID | Only if using Infisical |
126: | `Infisical__ClientSecret` | Universal Auth client secret | Only if using Infisical |
127: | `Infisical__Environment` | Environment slug (dev, staging, prod) | No (default: `dev`) |
128: 
129: ### Self-Hosted Deployment (No Secret Manager)
130: 
131: For self-hosters who don't want to use Infisical, set `SECRET_PROVIDER=none` and provide all secrets via environment variables:
132: 
133: ```bash
134: # Required environment variables for self-hosted deployment
135: SECRET_PROVIDER=none
136: ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection=Host=...;Database=...;Username=...;Password=...
137: Keycloak__Authority=https://your-keycloak/realms/your-realm
138: Keycloak__ClientId=explore-api
139: Keycloak__ClientSecret=your-secret
140: S3Settings__AccessKeyId=your-access-key
141: S3Settings__SecretAccessKey=your-secret-key
142: ```
143: 
144: ### Infisical Deployment
145: 
146: For production with Infisical:
147: 
148: ```bash
149: SECRET_PROVIDER=infisical
150: Infisical__Url=https://app.infisical.com
151: Infisical__ProjectId=your-project-id
152: Infisical__ClientId=your-client-id
153: Infisical__ClientSecret=your-client-secret
154: Infisical__Environment=prod
155: ```
156: 
157: Secrets are automatically loaded from Infisical paths:
158: - `/keycloak` - Keycloak configuration
159: - `/postgresql` - Database credentials
160: - `/api` - API-specific secrets (S3, etc.)
161: - `/blazor` - Blazor-specific configuration
162: 
163: ### Features
164: 
165: - **Automatic Refresh**: Secrets are refreshed periodically (configurable interval)
166: - **Health Checks**: Secret provider health is exposed at `/health`
167: - **Metrics**: Prometheus-compatible metrics for monitoring
168: - **Audit Logging**: All secret access is logged with redaction
169: - **Graceful Fallback**: Falls back to environment variables if Infisical unavailable
170: 
171: ## Cerbos (Planned)
172: 
173: Some older docs/templates mention a `Cerbos` configuration section.
174: 
175: Cerbos is **not currently wired** into `{Project}.API`, so there is no active Cerbos configuration required for the running system.
176: 
177: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
178: Cerbos is not currently wired into `Explore.API`, so there is no active Cerbos configuration required.
````

## File: docs/CONTRIBUTING.md
````markdown
  1: # Contribution Workflow
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Contribution Guidelines**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ## Placeholder Substitutions
  8: 
  9: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 10: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 11: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 12: | `{Project}.API` | API project | `{Project}.API` |
 13: | `{Project}.AppHost` | Aspire AppHost | `{Project}.AppHost` |
 14: | `{Project}ApiClient` | Generated API client | `{Project}ApiClient` |
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## Branch Strategy
 19: 
 20: ```
 21: main                    # Default branch
 22: ├── feature/xxx         # New features
 23: ├── bugfix/xxx          # Bug fixes
 24: └── refactor/xxx        # Code improvements
 25: ```
 26: 
 27: ## Commit Convention
 28: 
 29: ```
 30: type(scope): subject
 31: 
 32: body (optional)
 33: 
 34: footer (optional)
 35: ```
 36: 
 37: **Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`
 38: 
 39: **Examples**:
 40: ```
 41: feat(events): add prayer-relative scheduling
 42: fix(federation): correct HTTP signature validation
 43: docs(api): update endpoint documentation
 44: ```
 45: 
 46: ## Pull Request Process
 47: 
 48: 1. Create a branch from `main`
 49: 2. Implement changes with tests
 50: 3. Ensure all tests pass: `dotnet test`
 51: 4. Ensure code formatting: `dotnet format`
 52: 5. Create PR with description and linked issue
 53: 6. Request review from maintainers
 54: 7. Address feedback
 55: 8. Squash and merge when approved
 56: 
 57: ## Issue Templates
 58: 
 59: - **Bug Report**: Describe bug, steps to reproduce, expected behavior
 60: - **Feature Request**: Describe need, proposed solution, alternatives
 61: - **Task**: Technical work without user-facing change
 62: 
 63: ---
 64: 
 65: ## DTO Change Workflow (API → Blazor Client)
 66: 
 67: When making changes to DTOs in the API project, follow this specific workflow to ensure the Blazor client is properly updated.
 68: 
 69: ### Why This Workflow Matters
 70: 
 71: The project uses **.NET Aspire** for orchestration, which:
 72: 1. Fetches secrets from Infisical and injects them as environment variables
 73: 2. Starts all projects in the correct order
 74: 3. **Triggers OpenAPI schema regeneration** in the API project on startup
 75: 4. **NSwag watches for schema changes** and automatically regenerates the Blazor API client
 76: 
 77: **Key Point**: You must run Aspire to regenerate the client. Building alone won't update the generated client code.
 78: 
 79: ### The Vicious Cycle Problem
 80: 
 81: Understanding **why** this workflow exists prevents frustrating debugging sessions.
 82: 
 83: #### The Problem: Build Errors Block Client Regeneration
 84: 
 85: When you change DTOs in the API and then try to build the **full solution**, you enter a vicious cycle:
 86: 
 87: ```
 88: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 89: │                    ❌ THE VICIOUS CYCLE                              │
 90: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 91: │                                                                     │
 92: │  1. You change a DTO in the API (add new property)                  │
 93: │     ↓                                                               │
 94: │  2. You try to build the FULL SOLUTION                              │
 95: │     ↓                                                               │
 96: │  3. ❌ BUILD FAILS - Blazor references the OLD generated client     │
 97: │     │   (The generated client doesn't have the new property yet)    │
 98: │     ↓                                                               │
 99: │  4. ❌ ASP.NET API won't run (solution didn't build)                │
100: │     ↓                                                               │
101: │  5. ❌ swagger.json can't regenerate (API isn't running)            │
102: │     ↓                                                               │
103: │  6. ❌ NSwag can't update the client (no new schema)                │
104: │     ↓                                                               │
105: │  7. ❌ Generated client stays outdated                              │
106: │     ↓                                                               │
107: │  8. ❌ Build errors persist → BACK TO STEP 3                        │
108: │                                                                     │
109: │  💀 YOU ARE STUCK IN AN INFINITE LOOP                               │
110: │                                                                     │
111: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
112: ```
113: 
114: #### The Solution: Build API Separately First
115: 
116: By building **only the API project** first, you break the cycle:
117: 
118: ```
119: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
120: │                    ✅ THE CORRECT WORKFLOW                           │
121: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
122: │                                                                     │
123: │  1. You change a DTO in the API (add new property)                  │
124: │     ↓                                                               │
125: │  2. Build ONLY the API project: `dotnet build {Project}.API`          │
126: │     ↓                                                               │
127: │  3. ✅ API builds successfully (no Blazor dependency issues)        │
128: │     ↓                                                               │
129: │  4. Run Aspire: `dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost`              │
130: │     ↓                                                               │
131: │  5. ✅ API starts and generates new swagger.json                    │
132: │     ↓                                                               │
133: │  6. ✅ NSwag detects changes, regenerates client                    │
134: │     ↓                                                               │
135: │  7. ✅ Generated client now has the new property                    │
136: │     ↓                                                               │
137: │  8. NOW update Blazor services/components                           │
138: │     ↓                                                               │
139: │  9. ✅ Build full solution: `dotnet build {Project}.sln`              │
140: │                                                                     │
141: │  🎉 SUCCESS - No build errors!                                      │
142: │                                                                     │
143: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
144: ```
145: 
146: #### Common Trap: Updating Blazor Services Too Early
147: 
148: A particularly frustrating mistake is updating **Blazor services that interact with the generated API client** before the client is regenerated:
149: 
150: ```
151: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
152: │              ❌ THE SERVICE UPDATE TRAP                              │
153: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
154: │                                                                     │
155: │  Scenario: You add `Description` property to `EventDto`             │
156: │                                                                     │
157: │  1. You update EventDto in API (✅ correct)                         │
158: │     ↓                                                               │
159: │  2. You update EventService in Blazor to use `.Description`         │
160: │     ↓                                                               │
161: │  3. ❌ ERROR: 'EventDto' does not contain 'Description'             │
162: │     │                                                               │
163: │     │   WHY? The generated client ({Project}ApiClient.cs) still       │
164: │     │   has the OLD EventDto without Description!                   │
165: │     │                                                               │
166: │     │   Your service references: Generated.EventDto (OLD)           │
167: │     │   You expect:              Generated.EventDto.Description     │
168: │     │   Reality:                 Property doesn't exist yet         │
169: │     ↓                                                               │
170: │  4. Build fails on BOTH sides:                                      │
171: │     • API side: Works fine (your DTO has the property)              │
172: │     • Blazor side: Fails (generated client is outdated)             │
173: │                                                                     │
174: │  💡 The generated client is OUT OF SYNC with the API!               │
175: │                                                                     │
176: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
177: ```
178: 
179: **Rule of Thumb**:
180: - **API-only changes** → Build API only, run Aspire, then update Blazor
181: - **UI-only changes** (no DTO changes) → Can work directly in Blazor
182: - **Both API + Blazor changes** → Follow the full checklist, API first
183: 
184: ### Standard Workflow
185: 
186: ```
187: API Changes → Build API → Run Aspire → Client Regenerates → Update Blazor UI
188: ```
189: 
190: ### Process Checklist for DTO Changes
191: 
192: Follow this checklist whenever you add/modify DTO properties:
193: 
194: ```markdown
195: ## DTO Change Checklist
196: 
197: ### 1. Application Layer Changes
198: - [ ] Add/update properties in `{Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/` files
199: - [ ] Update `{Entity}Dto.cs` (full details)
200: - [ ] Update `{Entity}ListDto.cs` (list view) if applicable
201: - [ ] Update `Create{Entity}Dto.cs` / `Update{Entity}Dto.cs` if applicable
202: 
203: ### 2. Mapping & Data Access
204: - [ ] Update `MappingProfile.cs` if new navigation properties
205: - [ ] Update Repository `.Include()` statements if loading related data
206: - [ ] Update Handler if new processing logic needed
207: 
208: ### 3. Build & Regenerate
209: - [ ] Build API project only: `dotnet build {Project}.API`
210: - [ ] Start Aspire: `dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost`
211: - [ ] Wait for swagger.json to regenerate (automatic on API startup)
212: - [ ] NSwag regenerates client automatically (watches schema file)
213: 
214: ### 4. Blazor UI Updates
215: - [ ] NOW update Blazor components to use new properties
216: - [ ] Build full solution: `dotnet build {Project}.sln`
217: - [ ] Test the changes in browser
218: ```
219: 
220: ### Quick Fix: If You Forgot the Workflow
221: 
222: If you already updated Blazor UI before running Aspire and the generated client is missing properties:
223: 
224: **Option 1: Proper Fix (Recommended)**
225: ```powershell
226: # Stop any running instances
227: # Run Aspire to regenerate everything
228: dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost
229: ```
230: 
231: **Option 2: Manual Fix (Quick Workaround)**
232: Manually add the missing properties to the generated client file as a temporary fix, then run Aspire later to properly regenerate.
233: 
234: ### Architecture Diagram
235: 
236: ```
237: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
238: │                         .NET Aspire Orchestration                    │
239: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
240: │                                                                     │
241: │  1. Aspire Starts                                                   │
242: │     └── Fetches secrets from Infisical                              │
243: │     └── Injects environment variables to all projects               │
244: │                                                                     │
245: │  2. API Project Starts                                              │
246: │     └── Generates swagger.json (OpenAPI schema)                     │
247: │     └── Schema reflects current DTO structure                       │
248: │                                                                     │
249: │  3. Blazor Project Watches                                          │
250: │     └── NSwag detects swagger.json changes                          │
251: │     └── Regenerates API client ({Project}ApiClient.cs)                │
252: │                                                                     │
253: │  4. Blazor Components                                               │
254: │     └── Use the regenerated client with new properties              │
255: │                                                                     │
256: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
257: ```
258: 
259: ### Common Mistakes
260: 
261: | Mistake | Why It Fails | Fix |
262: |---------|--------------|-----|
263: | Build solution without running Aspire | swagger.json not regenerated | Run Aspire first |
264: | Update Blazor before API | Generated client missing new properties | Follow the checklist order |
265: | Manually edit generated files | Changes overwritten on next regeneration | Add to source DTOs, regenerate |
266: | Skip the MappingProfile update | AutoMapper doesn't map new properties | Always update profile |
267: 
268: ### Related Documentation
269: 
270: - [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) - Overall system architecture
271: - [API.md](API.md) - API endpoint patterns
272: - [BLAZOR.md](BLAZOR.md) - Blazor client architecture
273: - [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md) - DTO patterns and conventions
````

## File: docs/GOVERNANCE.md
````markdown
  1: # Code Conventions & Governance
  2: 
  3: > **Standards and Conventions for .NET Clean Architecture Projects**
  4: >
  5: > This document defines naming conventions, organizational patterns, and architectural decisions.
  6: > For code examples and implementation patterns, see the relevant skills in `.claude/skills/`.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Table of Contents
 13: 
 14: 1. [Critical Rules Summary](#critical-rules-summary)
 15: 2. [Naming Conventions](#naming-conventions)
 16: 3. [File Organization](#file-organization)
 17: 4. [Layer Responsibilities](#layer-responsibilities)
 18: 5. [Design Principles](#design-principles)
 19: 6. [Pattern Selection Guide](#pattern-selection-guide)
 20: 7. [Decision Framework](#decision-framework)
 21: 
 22: ---
 23: 
 24: ## Critical Rules Summary
 25: 
 26: These rules are **non-negotiable**. Violations break architectural integrity.
 27: 
 28: | # | Rule | Rationale |
 29: |---|------|-----------|
 30: | 1 | Repositories return **entities**, never DTOs | Single responsibility; mapping belongs in handlers |
 31: | 2 | Validators use **manual instantiation**, not DI | Fine-grained control; consistent pattern |
 32: | 3 | Navigation properties are **readonly for writes** | Tenant isolation; explicit repository operations |
 33: | 4 | Use `int` for IDs (except where `Guid`/`long` needed) | Consistency; sufficient for most scenarios |
 34: | 5 | No default values in entity properties | Explicit initialization; clear value origins |
 35: | 6 | Keep all using statements | Build system dependencies; prevents issues |
 36: | 7 | Commands return `BaseCommandResponse<T>` | Consistent error handling; structured responses |
 37: | 8 | GET = AllowAnonymous, Write = Authorize | Public discovery; protected writes |
 38: | 9 | UserId extraction uses fallback pattern | Provider compatibility; claim name variations |
 39: | 10 | Use file-scoped namespaces | C# 10+ convention; cleaner code |
 40: 
 41: **For detailed examples**: See `QUICK_REFERENCE.md` and relevant skills.
 42: 
 43: ---
 44: 
 45: ## Naming Conventions
 46: 
 47: ### General Rules
 48: 
 49: | Element | Convention | Example |
 50: |---------|------------|---------|
 51: | Public members | PascalCase | `Title`, `CreatedAt` |
 52: | Private fields | _camelCase with underscore | `_eventRepository` |
 53: | Parameters | camelCase | `eventId`, `createDto` |
 54: | Constants | PascalCase | `DefaultPageSize` |
 55: | Interfaces | IPascalCase | `IEventRepository` |
 56: | Async methods | Suffix with Async | `GetEventsAsync()` |
 57: 
 58: ### Entity Naming
 59: 
 60: | Type | Pattern | Example |
 61: |------|---------|---------|
 62: | Core entity | Singular noun | `Event`, `Organization` |
 63: | Lookup/enum entity | Singular noun | `EventType`, `ApprovalStatus` |
 64: | Join table | Combined names | `EventCategories`, `EventTags` |
 65: | Aspect table | Parent + Details | `EventIslamicDetails` |
 66: 
 67: ### DTO Naming
 68: 
 69: | Type | Pattern | Purpose |
 70: |------|---------|---------|
 71: | Full details | `{Entity}Dto` | Read operations with all fields |
 72: | List view | `{Entity}ListDto` | Minimal fields for lists |
 73: | Create payload | `Create{Entity}Dto` | Write operations (no ID) |
 74: | Update payload | `Update{Entity}Dto` | Write operations (ID required) |
 75: 
 76: ### Handler Naming
 77: 
 78: | Type | Pattern | Example |
 79: |------|---------|---------|
 80: | Command | `Create{Entity}Command` | `CreateEventCommand` |
 81: | Command Handler | `Create{Entity}CommandHandler` | `CreateEventCommandHandler` |
 82: | Query | `Get{Entity}ListRequest` | `GetEventListRequest` |
 83: | Query Handler | `Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler` | `GetEventListRequestHandler` |
 84: 
 85: ### Repository Naming
 86: 
 87: | Type | Pattern | Example |
 88: |------|---------|---------|
 89: | Interface | `I{Entity}Repository` | `IEventRepository` |
 90: | Implementation | `{Entity}Repository` | `EventRepository` |
 91: | Generic base | `IGenericRepository<T, TId>` | Base interface |
 92: 
 93: ---
 94: 
 95: ## File Organization
 96: 
 97: ### Solution Structure
 98: 
 99: ```
100: {Project}.sln
101: ├── src/
102: │   ├── {Project}.Domain/           # Entities, Enums, Interfaces
103: │   ├── {Project}.Application/      # CQRS, DTOs, Validators
104: │   ├── {Project}.Persistence/      # DbContext, Repositories
105: │   ├── {Project}.Infrastructure/   # External services
106: │   ├── {Project}.API/              # REST endpoints
107: │   ├── {Project}.Blazor/           # BFF (Blazor Server)
108: │   └── {Project}.Blazor.Client/    # UI (Blazor WASM)
109: ├── tests/
110: │   ├── {Project}.Domain.UnitTests/
111: │   ├── {Project}.Application.UnitTests/
112: │   ├── {Project}.API.IntegrationTests/
113: │   └── {Project}.Persistence.IntegrationTests/
114: └── docs/
115: ```
116: 
117: ### Application Layer Organization
118: 
119: ```
120: {Project}.Application/
121: ├── Features/{Entity}/
122: │   ├── Requests/
123: │   │   ├── Commands/           # Create, Update, Delete
124: │   │   └── Queries/            # Get, List, Search
125: │   └── Handlers/
126: │       ├── Commands/           # Command handlers
127: │       └── Queries/            # Query handlers
128: ├── DTOs/{Entity}/
129: │   ├── {Entity}Dto.cs
130: │   ├── {Entity}ListDto.cs
131: │   ├── Create{Entity}Dto.cs
132: │   ├── Update{Entity}Dto.cs
133: │   └── Validators/
134: ├── Contracts/
135: │   ├── Persistence/            # Repository interfaces
136: │   ├── Infrastructure/         # Service interfaces
137: │   └── Identity/               # User context interfaces
138: ├── Responses/                  # BaseCommandResponse, etc.
139: ├── Exceptions/                 # Custom exceptions
140: └── Profiles/                   # AutoMapper profiles
141: ```
142: 
143: ### Domain Layer Organization
144: 
145: ```
146: {Project}.Domain/
147: ├── Entities/                   # Core business entities
148: ├── Enums/                      # Enum definitions
149: ├── Interfaces/                 # Domain interfaces
150: │   ├── ITenantEntity.cs
151: │   ├── IAuditableEntity.cs
152: │   └── ISoftDeletable.cs
153: └── ValueObjects/               # Value objects (if any)
154: ```
155: 
156: ### Persistence Layer Organization
157: 
158: ```
159: {Project}.Persistence/
160: ├── Configurations/
161: │   └── Entities/               # EF Core configurations
162: ├── Repositories/               # Repository implementations
163: ├── Migrations/                 # Database migrations
164: └── {DbContext}.cs              # Main DbContext
165: ```
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ## Layer Responsibilities
170: 
171: ### What Goes Where
172: 
173: | Concern | Layer | Location |
174: |---------|-------|----------|
175: | Entity definition | Domain | `{Project}.Domain/` |
176: | Business rules | Domain | Entity methods, value objects |
177: | Repository interface | Application | `Contracts/Persistence/` |
178: | Command/Query | Application | `Features/{Entity}/Requests/` |
179: | Handler logic | Application | `Features/{Entity}/Handlers/` |
180: | DTO definition | Application | `DTOs/{Entity}/` |
181: | Validation rules | Application | `DTOs/{Entity}/Validators/` |
182: | Repository implementation | Persistence | `Repositories/` |
183: | EF configuration | Persistence | `Configurations/Entities/` |
184: | External service impl | Infrastructure | Service classes |
185: | API endpoint | Presentation | `Controllers/` |
186: | UI component | Presentation | `Components/` |
187: 
188: ### Dependency Rules
189: 
190: | Layer | Can Reference | Cannot Reference |
191: |-------|--------------|------------------|
192: | Domain | Nothing | Application, Infrastructure, Presentation |
193: | Application | Domain | Infrastructure, Presentation |
194: | Infrastructure | Domain, Application | Presentation |
195: | Presentation | All | (Entry point) |
196: 
197: ---
198: 
199: ## Design Principles
200: 
201: ### SOLID Application
202: 
203: | Principle | How We Apply It |
204: |-----------|-----------------|
205: | **S**ingle Responsibility | One handler per command/query; one repository per entity |
206: | **O**pen/Closed | Extend via new handlers, not modifying existing |
207: | **L**iskov Substitution | All repository implementations honor interface contracts |
208: | **I**nterface Segregation | Small, focused interfaces per entity type |
209: | **D**ependency Inversion | Application defines interfaces; Infrastructure implements |
210: 
211: ### Additional Principles
212: 
213: | Principle | Application |
214: |-----------|-------------|
215: | **DRY** | Generic repository base; shared validation patterns |
216: | **KISS** | Simple handlers; one responsibility per class |
217: | **YAGNI** | Don't add abstractions until needed |
218: | **Explicit > Implicit** | Clear initialization; obvious dependencies |
219: | **Fail Fast** | Validate early; return errors immediately |
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ## Pattern Selection Guide
224: 
225: ### When to Use Each Pattern
226: 
227: | Scenario | Pattern | Reasoning |
228: |----------|---------|-----------|
229: | Simple CRUD | CQRS + Generic Repository | Standard approach |
230: | Complex query | Custom repository method | Optimize for specific needs |
231: | Cross-entity operation | Domain service | Coordinate multiple entities |
232: | External integration | Infrastructure service | Isolate external dependencies |
233: | Validation | FluentValidation | Consistent, testable rules |
234: | Mapping | AutoMapper | Convention-based, less boilerplate |
235: 
236: ### When NOT to Use Patterns
237: 
238: | Anti-Pattern | Why to Avoid |
239: |--------------|--------------|
240: | Repository for simple lookups | Over-engineering |
241: | Domain service for single-entity ops | Should be in handler |
242: | Generic repository for complex queries | Loses optimization |
243: | MediatR behaviors for one-off logic | Use handler directly |
244: 
245: ---
246: 
247: ## Decision Framework
248: 
249: ### Choosing ID Types
250: 
251: | Type | Use When | Examples |
252: |------|----------|----------|
253: | `Guid` | Main entities, distributed systems | Event, Organization, User |
254: | `int` | Lookup tables, enums, sequential IDs | EventType, ApprovalStatus |
255: | `long` | Large sequences, file sizes, cursors | Pagination, storage metrics |
256: 
257: ### Choosing Validation Location
258: 
259: | Location | Use When |
260: |----------|----------|
261: | DTO Validator | Input validation, format checks |
262: | Handler | Business rules requiring data access |
263: | Entity | Invariants that must always hold |
264: | Controller | Quick format/auth checks |
265: 
266: ### Choosing Query Strategy
267: 
268: | Strategy | Use When |
269: |----------|----------|
270: | Repository method | Standard queries, reusable |
271: | Handler-specific query | One-off, optimized for use case |
272: | Specification pattern | Complex, composable filters |
273: 
274: ---
275: 
276: ## Code Quality Standards
277: 
278: ### Required in Every File
279: 
280: - File-scoped namespace
281: - All necessary using statements preserved
282: - Async suffix on async methods
283: - CancellationToken passed through
284: 
285: ### Required in Every Entity
286: 
287: - Primary key property
288: - TenantId (for tenant-scoped entities)
289: - Audit fields (CreatedAt, UpdatedAt)
290: - Soft delete support (IsDeleted)
291: 
292: ### Required in Every Controller
293: 
294: - Route attribute with version
295: - OpenAPI attributes on actions
296: - Authorization attributes
297: - Proper HTTP status codes
298: 
299: ---
